vocab.meaning: A close match/contest, a tight race where the outcome is uncertain until the end.
vocab.example: 決勝戦は最後まで分からない接戦となった。— The final was a close match that was uncertain until the very end.

vocab.word: 自己概念 【じこがいねん】
vocab.meaning: Self-concept, one's own mental image/understanding of who one is (a psychology term).
vocab.example: 幼少期の経験は自己概念の形成に大きく影響する。— Childhood experiences greatly influence the formation of self-concept.

vocab.meaning: Cognition, recognition; also used for legal "acknowledgment" (e.g., of paternity) and in 認知症 (dementia).
vocab.example: 高齢化に伴い、認知症患者が増加している。— With an aging population, the number of dementia patients is increasing.

vocab.meaning: Dented, caved in (describing a physical indentation); colloquially, "deflated/demoralized" emotionally.
vocab.example: 車のドアがぶつかってへこんでしまった。— The car door got dented from the collision.

vocab.word: ふくらんだ 【ふくらんだ】
vocab.meaning: Bulging, swollen, puffed out (describing something that has expanded outward).
vocab.example: 風船がどんどんふくらんだ。— The balloon kept inflating more and more.

vocab.meaning: Pointed, sharp-tipped (describing a physical shape); figuratively, "edgy/unconventional" (slang, e.g., とがった意見).
vocab.example: 鉛筆の先がとがっている。— The tip of the pencil is pointed.

vocab.word: まるまった 【まるまった】
vocab.meaning: Rounded up, curled up (into a ball shape), e.g., an animal curling up to sleep.
vocab.example: 猫がこたつの中でまるまって寝ている。— The cat is curled up asleep inside the kotatsu.

vocab.meaning: Thick (of books, materials, or layers — notably thicker than merely 厚い).
vocab.example: 彼は分厚い辞書を持ち歩いている。— He carries around a thick dictionary.

vocab.word: みすぼらしい 【みすぼらしい】
vocab.meaning: Shabby, poor/wretched-looking in appearance (often implying poverty).
vocab.example: 彼はみすぼらしい身なりで駅前に立っていた。— He stood in front of the station, shabbily dressed.

vocab.meaning: Worn out, tattered, falling apart (describing the physical state of an object); also used for a person who is utterly exhausted/battered.
vocab.example: 長年使った靴はもうぼろぼろだ。— The shoes I've used for years are now worn to tatters.

vocab.meaning: To be bulky, take up a lot of space (often said of luggage or belongings).
vocab.example: 冬服は荷物がかさばるので旅行には不便だ。— Winter clothes are bulky, so they're inconvenient for travel.

vocab.word: ありふれた 【ありふれた】
vocab.meaning: Commonplace, ordinary, run-of-the-mill (often with a slightly dismissive/unremarkable nuance).
vocab.example: それはどこにでもあるありふれた話だ。— That's a commonplace story you can find anywhere.

vocab.word: 四つ角/交差点 【よつかど/こうさてん】
vocab.example: 次の交差点を右に曲がってください。— Please turn right at the next intersection.

vocab.meaning: Secret, something kept hidden/confidential (casual register, often between individuals).
vocab.example: これは内緒だけど、彼女にプレゼントを用意しているんだ。— This is a secret, but I'm preparing a present for her.

vocab.meaning: Remnant, lingering trace (of something past); also the lingering feeling of reluctance at parting (名残惜しい).
vocab.example: この街には昔の名残が今も残っている。— Traces of the old days still remain in this town.

vocab.meaning: Groundwork, behind-the-scenes lobbying/consensus-building before a formal decision (common in Japanese business/organizational culture).
vocab.example: 会議の前に関係者に根回しをしておいた。— I did the groundwork (informally consulted) with the people involved before the meeting.

vocab.meaning: (Humble) borrowing — a humble-register word for "to borrow," used when the speaker is lowering themselves relative to the lender.
vocab.example: お手洗いをちょっと拝借できますでしょうか。— Might I humbly borrow your restroom for a moment?

vocab.meaning: To bind, fasten together (papers, pages), e.g., with staples or thread.
vocab.example: 書類をホチキスで綴じてください。— Please staple the documents together.
この温泉の入浴時間は午後10時までです。— The bathing hours at this hot spring are until 10 p.m.

vocab.meaning: Swamp, marsh, bog (a body of still, shallow water with muddy/weedy ground); slang: an obsession/rabbit hole one can't escape from (沼にハマる).
vocab.example: その沼にはたくさんの生き物が生息している。— Many creatures live in that swamp.

vocab.meaning: To tame, domesticate, acclimate/accustom (an animal or oneself to something).
vocab.example: 野良猫を少しずつ馴らしていった。— I gradually tamed the stray cat.

vocab.meaning: All the more, even more so (used to intensify a statement given an additional reason).
vocab.example: 雨が降っているなら、尚更出かけたくない。— If it's raining, I want to go out even less.

vocab.meaning: Consideration, thoughtful care/attention given to someone's needs or feelings.
vocab.example: この施設は障害者への配慮が行き届いている。— This facility shows thorough consideration for people with disabilities.

vocab.meaning: To obstruct, block, cut off (a view, light, sound, or someone's speech).
vocab.example: 高いビルが日光を遮っている。— The tall building is blocking the sunlight.

vocab.meaning: Villa, vacation home, second house (typically in a resort/countryside location).
vocab.example: 彼は軽井沢に別荘を持っている。— He has a vacation home in Karuizawa.

vocab.meaning: To look at, gaze at, view (often at length, taking in a scene, e.g., scenery).
vocab.example: 窓から海を眺めるのが好きだ。— I like gazing at the sea from the window.

vocab.meaning: Starting a new post/assignment, especially relocating for a job transfer (often to a distant branch office).
vocab.example: 彼は来月から大阪支社に赴任することになった。— He is set to take up a new post at the Osaka branch starting next month.

vocab.meaning: Nursing care, caregiving (typically for the elderly, sick, or disabled).
vocab.example: 祖母の介護をするために実家に戻った。— I returned to my parents' home to care for my grandmother.

vocab.meaning: Service, selfless service/devotion (to the public, community, or a higher cause); often in 奉仕活動 "volunteer/service activities."
vocab.example: 学生たちは地域の奉仕活動に参加した。— The students participated in community service activities.

vocab.meaning: To hold back, refrain from, cut down on; also "to be near/at hand" (時間が差し迫る) and "to note/jot down" (控えておく).
vocab.example: 医者に塩分を控えるように言われた。— The doctor told me to cut down on salt.

vocab.meaning: Friction (both physical, as in physics, and figurative, as in interpersonal or diplomatic conflict).
vocab.example: 二つの金属がこすれ合うと摩擦が生じる。— When two metals rub together, friction is generated.

vocab.meaning: The conservatives, conservative faction (in politics or within an organization).
vocab.example: 保守派は伝統的な価値観を重視する。— The conservative faction places importance on traditional values.

vocab.meaning: Actor/actress (performer in film, TV, or theater).
vocab.example: 彼は舞台俳優として長いキャリアを持つ。— He has a long career as a stage actor.

vocab.meaning: Confiscation, seizure (of property, items, or privileges, often as a penalty).
vocab.example: 授業中にスマホを使っていた生徒は没収された。— The student who was using their smartphone during class had it confiscated.

vocab.meaning: To give (charity), perform/apply (a treatment, measure, or decoration), bestow.
vocab.example: 貧しい人々に食料を施した。— He gave food to the poor (charitable giving).

vocab.meaning: Decoration, ornamentation (adding decorative elements to something).
vocab.example: クリスマスツリーには華やかな装飾が施されている。— The Christmas tree is decorated with gorgeous ornamentation.

vocab.meaning: To pass through, go via, elapse (time), undergo (a process or stage).
vocab.example: 長い年月を経て、ようやく夢が叶った。— After many years passed, my dream finally came true.

vocab.meaning: Various, varied, differing (describing a lack of uniformity among items or opinions).
vocab.example: 参加者の意見はまちまちだった。— The participants' opinions were all over the place (varied/inconsistent).

vocab.meaning: Dissatisfaction, discontent (especially with a decision or ruling); often in 不服を申し立てる "to file an objection/appeal."
vocab.example: 判決に不服があるなら控訴することができる。— If you are dissatisfied with the ruling, you can appeal.

vocab.meaning: Prejudice, bias (an unfair, preconceived opinion, often negative).
vocab.example: 彼は外国人に対する偏見を持っていた。— He held prejudice against foreigners.

vocab.meaning: Reward, compensation, remuneration (payment for work, service, or achievement).
vocab.example: この仕事の報酬は思ったより高かった。— The compensation for this job was higher than expected.

vocab.meaning: True intention, one's genuine feelings/opinion (as opposed to a diplomatic public stance).
vocab.example: 本音を言うと、この仕事はあまり好きではない。— To tell you my true feelings, I don't really like this job.

vocab.meaning: Trunk (of a tree); figuratively, the main/core part of something (as opposed to branches/details).
vocab.example: その木の幹はとても太い。— That tree's trunk is very thick.

vocab.meaning: Support (a dependent), providing for someone financially (a legal/tax term, e.g., 扶養家族 "dependent family members").
vocab.example: 彼は両親を扶養する義務がある。— He has a duty to support his parents.

vocab.meaning: To give up, abandon, relinquish (a right, responsibility, or possession).
vocab.example: 彼は相続権を放棄した。— He renounced his inheritance rights.

vocab.meaning: Supplement, supplementary addition/explanation (to fill in missing information).
vocab.example: 先ほどの説明に補足させてください。— Allow me to add a supplement to my earlier explanation.

vocab.word: へりくだる 【へりくだる】
vocab.meaning: To be humble, speak/act modestly by lowering oneself (often toward someone of higher status).
vocab.example: 彼はいつも目上の人にへりくだった態度を取る。— He always takes a humble attitude toward his superiors.

vocab.meaning: To be confused, flustered, at a loss over what to do (especially in an unfamiliar situation).
vocab.example: 初めての場所で道に迷い、まごついてしまった。— I got lost in an unfamiliar place and was flustered about what to do.

vocab.meaning: To escape, avoid, be spared from (a negative consequence, danger, or responsibility).
vocab.example: 彼は辛うじて事故を免れた。— He narrowly escaped the accident.

vocab.meaning: Beside, edge of, vicinity (typically of water — a river, lake, or pond); a somewhat literary/poetic word.
vocab.example: 彼は湖のほとりに小さな家を建てた。— He built a small house by the lakeside.

vocab.meaning: Indignation, resentful anger (especially at something perceived as unjust).
vocab.example: 不当な扱いに彼は憤慨した。— He was indignant at the unfair treatment.

vocab.meaning: Excuse, explanation/justification offered to defend oneself (often with a slightly negative "making excuses" connotation).
vocab.example: 彼は遅刻の理由を弁解しようとした。— He tried to make an excuse for being late.

vocab.meaning: To swarm, crowd, cluster together (often used for crowds of people, animals, or insects gathering densely).
vocab.example: 甘い蜜にアリが群がっていた。— Ants were swarming around the sweet nectar.

vocab.meaning: To repay, reward, requite (an act of kindness, effort, or sometimes a wrong — as in revenge).
vocab.example: 彼の努力はついに報われた。— His efforts were finally rewarded.

vocab.meaning: To be blessed, fortunate (with good circumstances, talent, resources, or environment).
vocab.example: 彼は才能に恵まれている。— He is blessed with talent.

vocab.meaning: Going around, touring, circulation (e.g., of blood, seasons, or visiting a series of places, as in 観光巡り "sightseeing tour").
vocab.example: 京都の寺院巡りを楽しんだ。— I enjoyed touring around the temples of Kyoto.

vocab.meaning: Compromise (reaching a middle ground by each side yielding something).
vocab.example: 両者は最終的に妥協点を見つけた。— The two parties finally found a point of compromise.

vocab.meaning: Training, ascetic practice, spiritual/disciplinary training (often religious, martial, or skill-based, implying rigorous, sustained effort).
vocab.example: 僧侶たちは山で厳しい修行を積んでいる。— The monks undergo severe ascetic training in the mountains.

vocab.meaning: Register, roster, list of names (e.g., a class roster, membership list, attendance list).
vocab.example: 新入生の名簿を作成した。— I created a roster of new students.

vocab.word: 取り扱い 【とりあつかい】
vocab.meaning: Handling, treatment (of goods, items, or matters — both physical handling and procedural/administrative treatment).
vocab.example: この荷物は「取り扱い注意」と書かれている。— This package is labeled "Handle with care."
彼女は紫のドレスを着ていた。— She wore a purple dress.

vocab.meaning: Pattern, design (on fabric, surfaces); also used to describe "the look of things"/situation, as in 〜模様 "it appears that...".
vocab.example: この着物には美しい花の模様が描かれている。— This kimono has a beautiful floral pattern on it.

vocab.meaning: To bury (a person, i.e., hold a funeral/burial); figuratively, to bury/suppress (a scandal, plan, or fact, consigning it to oblivion).
vocab.example: 彼は故郷の墓地に葬られた。— He was buried in his hometown's cemetery.

vocab.meaning: To avoid (a person, situation, topic, or danger).
vocab.example: 彼女はその話題を避けているようだった。— She seemed to be avoiding that topic.

vocab.word: ややこしい 【ややこしい】
vocab.meaning: Complicated, convoluted, confusingly intricate (often with a frustrated or exasperated nuance).
vocab.example: この手続きはとてもややこしい。— This procedure is very complicated.

vocab.meaning: Melancholy, depression, a gloomy/dispirited mood (can range from mild blues to describing clinical depression in context).
vocab.example: 月曜日の朝はいつも憂鬱な気分になる。— I always feel melancholy on Monday mornings.

vocab.meaning: Brave, courageous (describing bold, fearless action or character).
vocab.example: 彼は勇敢に敵に立ち向かった。— He bravely stood up to the enemy.

vocab.meaning: Solely, exclusively, mainly (devoting oneself to one thing in particular; also "the word on the street is...").
vocab.example: 彼は専ら仕事に打ち込んでいる。— He devotes himself solely to his work.

vocab.meaning: Estimate, quotation (a calculated approximation of cost, time, or quantity, especially in business).
vocab.example: 工事費用の見積りを業者に依頼した。— I asked the contractor for an estimate of the construction cost.

vocab.meaning: Source, origin, fountainhead (of a river, or figuratively of an idea, problem, or tradition).
vocab.example: この川の源は山奥にある。— The source of this river is deep in the mountains.

vocab.meaning: Lingering attachment/regret, reluctance to let go (especially of a past relationship, decision, or lost opportunity).
vocab.example: 彼女にまだ未練があるみたいだ。— It seems he still has lingering feelings for her (his ex).

vocab.meaning: Scale marking, graduation (the marked increments on a measuring instrument, like a ruler, thermometer, or gauge).
vocab.example: この温度計の目盛りは細かくて読みやすい。— This thermometer's scale markings are fine and easy to read.

vocab.meaning: Blind spot (both the literal physiological blind spot in vision, and figuratively, an overlooked weakness or gap in reasoning/planning).
vocab.example: 彼の計画には大きな盲点があった。— There was a major blind spot in his plan.

vocab.meaning: Primary factor, (contributing) cause (of an event, outcome, or phenomenon, especially in analytical/academic contexts).
vocab.example: この成功の要因はいくつか考えられる。— Several factors can be considered behind this success.

vocab.meaning: Leisure hours, free time, spare time (time not occupied by work or obligations).
vocab.example: 余暇を利用して資格の勉強をしている。— I'm using my leisure time to study for a certification.

vocab.meaning: Extinction, ruin, downfall (typically of a nation, civilization, species, or dynasty — a dramatic, often historical collapse).
vocab.example: ローマ帝国はやがて滅亡した。— The Roman Empire eventually fell (met its ruin).

vocab.meaning: Temptation (an enticement to do something, often something one knows one shouldn't).
vocab.example: ダイエット中なのに甘いものの誘惑に負けてしまった。— Even though I'm on a diet, I gave in to the temptation of sweets.
彼は新しい車をみんなに見せびらかした。(He showed off his new car to everyone.)

vocab.meaning: (have) discord, trouble; to be in dispute
vocab.example: 遺産相続のことでもめている。(They're in discord over inheritance matters.)
この二つの商品には類似点が多い。(These two products have many similarities.)
この二つの漢字は形が紛らわしい。(These two kanji have confusingly similar shapes.)
政府は国民に節電を促した。(The government urged citizens to save electricity.)
大学の寮に住んでいる。(I live in the university dormitory.)
廊下を走ってはいけません。(You must not run in the hallway.)
昨夜、近所で火災が発生した。(Last night, a fire broke out in the neighborhood.)
彼は警察に抵抗した。(He resisted the police.)
彼は自分の仕事に誇りを持っている。(He takes pride in his work.)
北海道は酪農が盛んな地域だ。(Hokkaido is a region where dairy farming is thriving.)
友達が試験に落ちて落ち込んでいたので励ました。(My friend was down after failing the exam, so I encouraged her.)
今日は猛烈に暑い。(It's intensely hot today.)
手続きが煩わしくて嫌になる。(The procedures are so troublesome it's off-putting.)
赤ちゃんを裸にしてお風呂に入れた。(I undressed the baby and put them in the bath.)
良識ある大人なら、そんなことはしない。(A sensible adult wouldn't do such a thing.)
労働者たちは連帯して経営者に抗議した。(The workers united in solidarity to protest against management.)
彼は良心の呵責に苦しんでいる。(He is suffering from pangs of conscience.)
企業は利潤を追求する。(Companies pursue profit.)
夜更かしは体に悪い。(Staying up late is bad for your health.)
真剣に取り組めば、結果は自ずから付いてくる。(If you work at it earnestly, results will naturally follow.)
彼は頑固で人の意見を聞かない。(He's stubborn and won't listen to others' opinions.)
軽率な発言で信頼を失った。(He lost trust due to a rash remark.)
大きさが違って見えるのは目の錯覚だ。(The fact that the sizes look different is an optical illusion.)
所得税の申告をしなければならない。(I have to file an income tax return.)
二社は市場シェアを巡って対抗している。(The two companies are competing against each other over market share.)
スイスは永世中立国として知られている。(Switzerland is known as a permanently neutral country.)
田んぼに苗を植える。(We plant rice seedlings in the paddy field.)

vocab.meaning: solely, single-mindedly, intently (also written 只管)
vocab.example: 彼はひたすら謝り続けた。(He kept apologizing single-mindedly/profusely.)
身分証明書は、パスポートもしくは運転免許証を提示してください。(Please present either a passport or a driver's license as ID.)
彼女は子供たちに深い愛を注いでいる。— She pours deep love into her children.
相変わらず忙しい毎日を送っています。— I'm having busy days as usual.

vocab.meaning: a signal, a sign, a cue
vocab.example: 彼が手を上げたのを合図に、全員が走り出した。— At his raised-hand signal, everyone started running.
親は子供に深い愛情を持っている。— Parents have deep affection for their children.
東京と大阪の間には多くの都市がある。— There are many cities between Tokyo and Osaka.
二人はどういう間柄ですか。— What is the relationship between the two of them?

vocab.meaning: to happen in succession, occur one after another
vocab.example: 今年は自然災害が相次いでいる。— Natural disasters have been occurring one after another this year.

vocab.meaning: companion, partner, opponent, the other party
vocab.example: 試合の相手は去年の優勝チームだ。— Our match opponent is last year's champion team.
いいアイデアを思いついた。— I came up with a good idea.
生憎、今日は雨です。— Unfortunately, it's raining today.
彼の返事は曖昧でよくわからなかった。— His answer was vague and hard to understand.

vocab.meaning: an interval, a break, spare moments
vocab.example: 仕事の合間にコーヒーを飲んだ。— I drank coffee during a break between work tasks.
シャツにアイロンをかけた。— I ironed the shirt.
旅行中に事故に遭った。— I had an accident during my trip.
敢えて厳しいことを言わせてもらいます。— I'll dare to say something harsh.

vocab.meaning: to look up (physically); to look up to, respect, seek guidance from
vocab.example: 夜空を仰いで星を見た。— I looked up at the night sky and saw the stars.

vocab.meaning: to turn pale, go pale (from fear, shock, illness)
vocab.example: 彼はその知らせを聞いて青ざめた。— He turned pale upon hearing the news.
彼女は青白い顔をしていた。— She had a pale face.
お風呂に入って体の垢を落とした。— I took a bath and washed off the grime from my body.
努力の証しとして、賞をいただいた。— I received the award as proof of my effort.

vocab.meaning: a deficit, being in the red (financially)
vocab.example: 会社は今年赤字になった。— The company ran a deficit this year.

vocab.meaning: to disclose, confide, reveal (a secret); to spend (the night)
vocab.example: 彼はついに真実を明かした。— He finally revealed the truth.

vocab.meaning: to grow light, brighten (as in dawn breaking)
vocab.example: 東の空が明らんできた。— The eastern sky began to brighten.
部屋の明かりをつけた。— I turned on the light in the room.

vocab.meaning: proceeds, takings (e.g. from a sale); finishing, completion
vocab.example: バザーの上がりは全額寄付された。— All the proceeds from the bazaar were donated.

vocab.meaning: to rise, go up; to improve; to finish; to get nervous
vocab.example: 気温が上がってきた。— The temperature has been rising.
このアパートには空きがある。— This apartment has a vacancy.
彼が嘘をついているのは明らかだ。— It's clear that he's lying.

vocab.meaning: to give up, abandon, resign oneself
vocab.example: 彼は夢を諦めなかった。— He didn't give up on his dream.
彼の顔には諦めの表情が浮かんでいた。— A look of resignation appeared on his face.

vocab.meaning: to get tired of, lose interest in, become bored with
vocab.example: 毎日同じ食事で飽きてしまった。— I got tired of eating the same meal every day.

vocab.meaning: to be amazed, dumbfounded, exasperated, disgusted (at something foolish/outrageous)
vocab.example: 彼の無責任さには呆れてしまう。— I'm dumbfounded by his irresponsibility.
彼は悪に染まってしまった。— He became tainted by evil.
試合の後、両選手は握手を交わした。— After the match, both players shook hands.
アクセルを踏んで加速した。— I pressed the accelerator and sped up.

vocab.meaning: accent (pronunciation stress/pitch; also a stylistic highlight)
vocab.example: 彼女は関西のアクセントで話す。— She speaks with a Kansai accent.

vocab.meaning: vicious, wicked, unscrupulous (especially in business dealings)
vocab.example: あくどい商売をして儲けている。— He's making money through unscrupulous business dealings.
授業中にあくびが止まらなかった。— I couldn't stop yawning during class.
彼はまるで悪魔のような笑みを浮かべた。— He flashed a smile like that of a devil.

vocab.word: あくまで(も) (あくまで(も))
vocab.meaning: to the last, persistently, strictly (as in "this is only/strictly...")
vocab.example: これはあくまで私の個人的な意見です。— This is strictly just my personal opinion.

vocab.meaning: the next/following (day, year) — adnominal, used only before nouns
vocab.example: 明くる日、彼は何事もなかったように現れた。— The next day, he showed up as if nothing had happened.
明け方に雨が降り出した。— It started raining at dawn.

vocab.meaning: to dawn; to come to an end (of a period, year, season)
vocab.example: 夜が明けて鳥が鳴き始めた。— Night gave way to dawn and the birds began to sing.
国旗を揚げる式典が行われた。— A ceremony to hoist the national flag was held.
彼は顎に手を当てて考えた。— He put his hand to his chin and thought.
彼女は昔から海外生活に憧れを抱いていた。— She had long held a yearning for life abroad.

vocab.meaning: to long for, be attracted to, admire (an ideal)
vocab.example: 子供の頃からパイロットに憧れていた。— I've admired/longed to be a pilot since childhood.
この服は麻でできている。— This clothing is made of linen/hemp.
この川は浅いので泳げない。— This river is shallow, so you can't swim in it.

vocab.meaning: mean, shameful, contemptible, miserable (describing greedy/undignified behavior)
vocab.example: 金のために友人を裏切るなんて浅ましい。— Betraying a friend for money is contemptible.
彼は巧妙に人々を欺いた。— He skillfully deceived people.
鮮やかな青色の空が広がっていた。— A vivid blue sky stretched out.

vocab.meaning: to laugh at, ridicule, make fun of (with contempt)
vocab.example: 彼の失敗を嘲笑う人がいた。— There were people who ridiculed his failure.
アジア各国から観光客が訪れる。— Tourists visit from various Asian countries.
雪の上に足跡が残っていた。— Footprints remained on the snow.

vocab.meaning: please don't take offense; I'm sorry, but... (polite phrase softening a refusal)
vocab.example: 都合によりキャンセルとなりました。あしからずご了承ください。— Due to circumstances, this has been cancelled. Please don't take offense and kindly understand.

vocab.meaning: underfoot, at one's feet; (figuratively) one's immediate situation/footing
vocab.example: 足元に気をつけてください。— Please watch your step (be careful underfoot).
このお茶には独特の味わいがある。— This tea has a distinctive flavor.

vocab.meaning: to taste, enjoy, appreciate, savor (food or experience)
vocab.example: ゆっくり料理を味わって食べた。— I ate the meal slowly, savoring it.

vocab.meaning: to keep, look after, take charge of (something entrusted to you)
vocab.example: 友達の荷物を預かっている。— I'm looking after my friend's luggage.

vocab.meaning: to entrust, deposit, leave in someone's care
vocab.example: 荷物をホテルのフロントに預けた。— I left my luggage with the hotel front desk.
運動したら汗がたくさん出た。— I sweated a lot after exercising.

vocab.meaning: a certain, one, some (used before a noun to introduce it vaguely)
vocab.example: 或る日、彼は突然失踪した。— One day, he suddenly disappeared.
この洗剤はアルカリ性だ。— This detergent is alkaline.

vocab.meaning: an album (photo album or music album)
vocab.example: 旅行の写真をアルバムにまとめた。— I compiled the trip photos into an album.
大学生の時、カフェでアルバイトをしていた。— When I was a university student, I worked part-time at a café.

vocab.meaning: that (one) — distal demonstrative pronoun, referring to something far from both speaker and listener
vocab.example: あれは富士山ですか。— Is that Mt. Fuji (over there)?
あれこれ考えたが、結局結論は出なかった。— I thought about this and that, but in the end reached no conclusion.

vocab.meaning: to become rough/stormy; to fall into disorder/ruin; (skin) to become chapped
vocab.example: 海が荒れて船が出せなかった。— The sea became rough, so the boats couldn't set out.
石鹸をこすると泡が立った。— Rubbing the soap created foam.
色の合わせが絶妙だ。— The color combination/matching is exquisite.

vocab.meaning: to combine, put together, match, adjust (to align with something)
vocab.example: 二人の意見を合わせて計画を立てた。— We combined our opinions and made a plan.
年末は慌ただしい日々が続く。— Hectic days continue at the end of the year.
彼の哀れな姿に涙が出た。— His pitiful appearance brought me to tears.
新しい案を考えてみた。— I came up with a new proposal.

vocab.meaning: easy, easygoing, facile (often with a negative nuance of being too simplistic)
vocab.example: 安易な解決策に頼るべきではない。— One shouldn't rely on an easy/facile solution.
この問題は案外簡単だった。— This problem was surprisingly easy.
単語を暗記するのが苦手だ。— I'm not good at memorizing vocabulary.
顧客満足度についてアンケートを実施した。— We conducted a questionnaire on customer satisfaction.
観客はアンコールを求めて拍手を続けた。— The audience kept clapping, calling for an encore.
大統領が暗殺される事件が起きた。— An incident occurred in which the president was assassinated.

vocab.meaning: mental arithmetic, calculating in one's head
vocab.example: 彼は暗算が得意だ。— He's good at mental arithmetic.
彼の言葉には暗示が含まれていた。— His words contained an implication.

vocab.meaning: relief, peace of mind; to feel relieved/reassured
vocab.example: 無事に着いたと聞いて安心した。— I felt relieved to hear you arrived safely.
医者に安静にするよう言われた。— The doctor told me to rest/stay still.
経済の安定を目指して政策を進めている。— Policies are being advanced aiming for economic stability.
駅まで案内してもらった。— I was guided to the station.

vocab.meaning: implicitly, indirectly, secretly (suggesting something without stating directly)
vocab.example: 彼は暗に辞職をほのめかした。— He implicitly hinted at resigning.

vocab.meaning: as expected, sure enough (often regarding an anticipated negative outcome)
vocab.example: 案の定、彼は遅刻してきた。— Sure enough, he showed up late.

vocab.meaning: safety, well-being (of a person, especially after a disaster or during separation)
vocab.example: 地震の後、家族の安否が確認できず心配した。— After the earthquake, I was worried because I couldn't confirm my family's safety.
食べ過ぎて胃が痛い。— My stomach hurts from overeating.

vocab.meaning: an outline, summary, synopsis (of a story)
vocab.example: この映画の粗筋を教えてください。— Please tell me the synopsis of this movie.
二つの国の間で領土争いが続いている。— A territorial dispute between the two countries continues.
二人は優勝を争った。— The two competed for the championship.
新たな気持ちで仕事に取り組んだ。— I tackled the work with a renewed mindset.

vocab.meaning: to become formal/stiff; to be renewed, reformed
vocab.example: 彼は急に改まった態度になった。— He suddenly became formal in his attitude.
悪い習慣を改めるべきだ。— I should correct my bad habits.

vocab.meaning: once more, afresh, formally (doing something again with renewed attention)
vocab.example: 改めてお礼を申し上げます。— I would like to express my thanks once again (formally).

vocab.meaning: rough, coarse, violent (in manner or action)
vocab.example: 彼の運転は荒っぽい。— His driving is rough/reckless.
彼はアラブ出身の留学生だ。— He is an international student from an Arab country.
彼はあらゆる手段を使って目標を達成した。— He achieved his goal using every possible means.

vocab.meaning: hailstones (small, soft hail); also a rice-cracker snack cut into small cubes
vocab.example: 急に霰が降ってきて驚いた。— I was surprised when hail suddenly started falling.
このグラフは売上の変化を表している。— This graph shows the change in sales.
この行動は彼の優しさの表れだ。— This action is a manifestation of his kindness.
空に虹が現れた。— A rainbow appeared in the sky.

vocab.meaning: grateful, thankful; (of an offer/situation) welcome, appreciated
vocab.example: ご協力いただき、誠にありがたく存じます。— I am truly grateful for your cooperation.

vocab.meaning: a state, condition, the way things are (often with negative connotation)
vocab.example: 部屋は散らかり放題でひどい有様だった。— The room was a mess, in a terrible state.

vocab.meaning: the plain truth, as it is, just as things are, unembellished
vocab.example: ありのままの自分を受け入れることが大切だ。— It's important to accept yourself as you are.

vocab.meaning: commonplace, ordinary, everywhere to be found
vocab.example: それはどこにでもあるありふれた話だ。— That's a commonplace story you can find anywhere.

vocab.meaning: a move, relocation, transfer (of an office, business, residence)
vocab.example: 会社は来月、新しいオフィスに移転する。— The company will relocate to a new office next month.
彼の発言の意図がよくわからない。— I don't quite understand the intention behind his remark.
この都市は緯度が高く、冬は非常に寒い。— This city is at a high latitude, so winters are extremely cold.
電車で会社まで移動する。— I commute (move) to the office by train.
夏休みにいとこの家へ遊びに行った。— I went to visit my cousin's house during summer vacation.

vocab.meaning: to carry on (a business); to lead/conduct (a life, ceremony)
vocab.example: 祖父は小さな店を営んでいる。— My grandfather runs a small shop.
空に稲光が走った。— A flash of lightning streaked across the sky.

vocab.meaning: rice, a rice plant (as it grows in the field)
vocab.example: 秋になると稲が黄金色に実る。— In autumn, the rice plants ripen to a golden color.

vocab.meaning: dozing off, nodding off (while supposed to be awake, e.g., sitting up)
vocab.example: 授業中に居眠りをしてしまった。— I accidentally dozed off during class.

vocab.meaning: life (as in a living being's existence)
vocab.example: 命を大切にしてください。— Please treasure your life.
彼女は毎朝、祈りを捧げる。— She offers a prayer every morning.

vocab.meaning: to boast, brag, be proud, act domineering/bossy
vocab.example: 彼はいつも部下に威張っている。— He's always acting bossy toward his subordinates.
スピード違反で罰金を払った。— I paid a fine for a speeding violation.
夫のいびきがうるさくて眠れない。— My husband's snoring is so loud I can't sleep.
季節に合った衣服を選ぶことが大切だ。— It's important to choose clothing suited to the season.
家族は居間でテレビを見ている。— The family is watching TV in the living room.

vocab.meaning: (now) at this late stage, too late now, can't go back and change it now
vocab.example: 今更謝っても遅い。— It's too late to apologize now.

vocab.meaning: still, yet, so far (not yet happened)
vocab.example: 彼はいまだにその習慣を続けている。— He still keeps up that habit, even now.

vocab.meaning: soon, before long, one of these days (implying eventual, often inevitable, occurrence)
vocab.example: 今に後悔するぞ。— You'll regret this eventually, mark my words.

vocab.meaning: any minute now, at any moment (on the verge of happening)
vocab.example: 今にも雨が降り出しそうだ。— It looks like it's going to start raining any minute now.
多くの移民がこの国で新しい生活を始めた。— Many immigrants started a new life in this country.
この会社のイメージはとても良い。— This company's image is very good.
私の妹は高校生だ。— My younger sister is a high school student.

vocab.meaning: reluctantly, unwillingly; (as interjection) no, no / (shaking one's head)
vocab.example: 彼はいやいや仕事を引き受けた。— He reluctantly took on the job.
「一緒に行く?」「いや、やめておく。」— "Want to come together?" "No, I'll pass."

vocab.meaning: to dislike, hate, show reluctance/aversion (observable from outside)
vocab.example: 子供は注射を嫌がった。— The child showed resistance to getting the shot.

vocab.meaning: greedy, vulgar, mean, shabby, low (in status or character)
vocab.example: 彼の卑しい根性が嫌いだ。— I dislike his mean-spirited, greedy nature.

vocab.meaning: suspiciously, strangely, unusually (often implying something is off or excessive)
vocab.example: 今日はいやに静かだね。— It's strangely quiet today, isn't it.
いやらしい目つきで見ないで。— Don't look at me with that lewd/leering gaze.

vocab.meaning: more and more, increasingly; finally, at last; (in dialect) really, truly
vocab.example: 台風の影響でいよいよ風が強くなってきた。— Due to the typhoon, the wind is getting stronger and stronger.
彼は仕事に対する意欲を失ってしまった。— He lost his motivation for work.
卒業以来、彼とは会っていない。— I haven't seen him since graduation.

vocab.meaning: nervousness, jitters, irritation; to get irritated/on edge
vocab.example: 渋滞でいらいらしてしまった。— I got irritated because of the traffic jam.
店員が「いらっしゃいませ!」と元気よく挨拶した。— The shop clerk greeted customers energetically with "Welcome!"
この国の医療制度は充実している。— This country's healthcare system is well developed.

vocab.meaning: to roast, parch, toast (dry-heat cooking, e.g., beans, tea leaves, sesame)
vocab.example: ゴマをフライパンで煎ると香ばしくなる。— Roasting sesame seeds in a pan makes them fragrant.
このデパートは衣類売り場が充実している。— This department store has an extensive clothing section.
その意見に異論はない。— I have no objection to that opinion.

vocab.meaning: a rock, a crag, a boulder
vocab.example: 海岸には大きな岩がいくつもあった。— There were several large rocks along the coast.

vocab.meaning: celebration, a festival, congratulations; a celebratory gift
vocab.example: 合格のお祝いにケーキを買った。— I bought a cake to celebrate passing the exam.
みんなで彼の誕生日を祝った。— Everyone celebrated his birthday together.

vocab.meaning: so to speak, as it were, in other words
vocab.example: 彼は、言わばこの会社の顔のような存在だ。— He is, so to speak, the face of this company.

vocab.meaning: what is called, so-called, the so-called
vocab.example: これがいわゆる「ブラック企業」というやつだ。— This is what's called a "black company" (exploitative workplace).

vocab.meaning: member (suffix attached to nouns, e.g., 会社員, 銀行員)
vocab.example: 彼は大手銀行の行員だ。— He is a bank employee (bank member) at a major bank.

vocab.meaning: gloom, somberness, a dark/depressing atmosphere or personality
vocab.example: この部屋は陰気な雰囲気がある。— This room has a gloomy atmosphere.
プリンターのインクが切れてしまった。— The printer ran out of ink.
この書類を10部印刷してください。— Please print 10 copies of this document.

vocab.meaning: impression (the feeling/image left by something or someone)
vocab.example: 彼女は第一印象がとても良かった。— She made a very good first impression.
次のインターチェンジで高速を降りてください。— Please exit the highway at the next interchange.
彼女はインターナショナルスクールに通っている。— She attends an international school.
インターフォンが鳴ったので出てみた。— The intercom rang, so I went to answer it.
有名な俳優にインタビューをした。— I interviewed a famous actor.
彼はインテリ層に支持されている。— He is supported by the intellectual class.

vocab.meaning: wholeheartedly, with all one's heart, single-minded devotion
vocab.example: 彼は一心に勉強に打ち込んだ。— He devoted himself wholeheartedly to studying.

vocab.meaning: all together, simultaneously, unanimously (as a group, at once)
vocab.example: 合図とともに全員が一斉に走り出した。— At the signal, everyone started running all at once.

vocab.meaning: would rather, I'd rather (just do something more drastic)
vocab.example: 中途半端にやるより、いっそやめてしまおう。— Rather than do it half-heartedly, let's just quit altogether.

vocab.meaning: still more, all the more, even more so
vocab.example: 今後は一層努力するつもりだ。— I intend to work even harder from now on.

vocab.meaning: on earth, in the world, whatever (emphatic question word); also: one body, unity
vocab.example: 一体何が起こったんだ?— What on earth happened?

vocab.meaning: once, for a moment, temporarily (as a first step before something else)
vocab.example: 一旦家に帰ってから、また出かけます。— I'll go home once, and then head out again.
二人の意見が一致した。— The two people's opinions aligned.

vocab.meaning: fixed, definite, set, constant; to fix/standardize
vocab.example: 一定の条件を満たせば申請できる。— You can apply if you meet certain fixed conditions.

vocab.meaning: any time, always, at all times (whenever)
vocab.example: いつでも遊びに来てください。— Please come visit any time.

vocab.meaning: before one realizes it, without noticing, all too soon
vocab.example: いつの間にか日が暮れていた。— Before I knew it, the sun had set.

vocab.meaning: a cupful (of a drink); full, a lot of
vocab.example: コーヒーを一杯いただけますか。— Could I have a cup of coffee?

vocab.meaning: general, generally, average, ordinary; in general
vocab.example: 一般に、日本人は勤勉だと言われる。— Generally speaking, Japanese people are said to be hardworking.

vocab.meaning: a complete change, a total transformation (often sudden)
vocab.example: 彼の態度は一変した。— His attitude completely changed.

vocab.meaning: one side/party (of two); meanwhile, on the other hand
vocab.example: 彼は厳しい一方で、とても優しい人でもある。— While he's strict, he's also a very kind person.

vocab.meaning: forever, indefinitely, for as long as possible
vocab.example: いつまでも仲良くいようね。— Let's stay friends forever, okay?

vocab.meaning: to starve, be famished, be hungry (also figuratively: to crave/be starved for something)
vocab.example: 戦時中、多くの人々が飢えに苦しんだ。— During the war, many people suffered from starvation.
築地には有名なうお市場がある。— There's a famous fish market in Tsukiji.

vocab.meaning: gargling, rinsing out one's mouth/throat; to gargle
vocab.example: 帰宅したら、うがいと手洗いをしましょう。— When you get home, let's gargle and wash your hands.

vocab.meaning: to float, surface, appear, come to mind (flash into thought)
vocab.example: 空に浮かぶ雲を眺めた。— I gazed at the clouds floating in the sky.

vocab.meaning: to float (something), launch, visualize, show (an expression)
vocab.example: 船を池に浮かべて遊んだ。— We floated a boat on the pond and played.
第一志望の大学に受かった。— I got into (passed the exam for) my first-choice university.
留学生の受け入れ体制を整えた。— We prepared a system for accepting international students.

vocab.meaning: to receive, accept, grant, admit (people, conditions, ideas)
vocab.example: 彼は批判を素直に受け入れた。— He accepted the criticism honestly.

vocab.meaning: to hear, to receive, to comply with (humble form of 聞く/受ける/引き受ける)
vocab.example: ご注文を承りました。— I have received your order (humbly).

vocab.meaning: to take over, inherit, carry on (a tradition, role, trait)
vocab.example: 彼は父の技術を受け継いだ。— He inherited his father's skills.

vocab.meaning: to accept, receive (applications, requests); to listen to/tolerate
vocab.example: 申し込みは明日から受け付けます。— Applications will be accepted starting tomorrow.

vocab.meaning: to catch, stop, take (a physical or emotional impact); to come to terms with
vocab.example: 彼は批判を真剣に受け止めた。— He took the criticism seriously.
荷物の受け取りにはサインが必要です。— A signature is required to receive the package.

vocab.meaning: to receive, get, accept; to interpret (a remark) in a certain way
vocab.example: 荷物を受け取った。— I received the package.

vocab.meaning: passive voice (grammar); a passive/defensive stance or attitude
vocab.example: 日本語の受け身の文法は難しい。— Japanese passive voice grammar is difficult.

vocab.meaning: being in charge (of something); one's area of responsibility
vocab.example: 彼女は3年2組の受け持ちの先生だ。— She is the homeroom teacher in charge of class 3-2.

vocab.meaning: to be in charge of, handle, manage (a task, class, role)
vocab.example: 彼は新しいプロジェクトを受け持つことになった。— He ended up being in charge of the new project.

vocab.meaning: to move, shift, budge, operate (a machine); to affect/move (emotionally)
vocab.example: この機械の動かし方を教えてください。— Please teach me how to operate this machine.

vocab.meaning: movement, motion; a trend, sign, development
vocab.example: 市場の動きを注意深く観察する。— I carefully observe the movements of the market.
公園で白い兎を見かけた。— I saw a white rabbit in the park.
牧場にたくさんの牛がいる。— There are many cows in the pasture.
事故で記憶を失ってしまった。— He lost his memory in the accident.
川の合流地点に大きな渦ができていた。— A large whirlpool had formed where the rivers merged.
薄暗い部屋で本を読むと目が疲れる。— Reading in a dim room tires your eyes.

vocab.meaning: to thin, dilute, weaken (a liquid, flavor, etc.)
vocab.example: ジュースを水で薄めて飲んだ。— I diluted the juice with water and drank it.

vocab.meaning: to bury, to nestle into, to lay low
vocab.example: 彼女は枕に顔をうずめて泣いた。— She buried her face in the pillow and cried.
あいつは嘘つきだから、言うことを信じない方がいい。— That guy's a liar, so you'd better not believe what he says.

vocab.meaning: to doubt, to suspect, to question
vocab.example: 彼の話を疑うのは失礼だと思う。— I think it's rude to doubt his story.

vocab.meaning: a doze, a nap, dozing off
vocab.example: ソファでうたたねしてしまい、風邪をひいた。— I dozed off on the sofa and caught a cold.

vocab.meaning: in, within, among (a group); one's home/household
vocab.example: このうちのどれが一番好きですか。— Which one of these do you like best?

vocab.meaning: to confide, to confess, to tell the truth (about something hidden)
vocab.example: 彼女に秘密を打ち明けた。— I confided my secret to her.

vocab.meaning: arrangements, a (business) meeting to coordinate plans
vocab.example: 明日の午後、クライアントと打ち合わせがある。— I have a meeting with the client tomorrow afternoon.

vocab.meaning: to arrange/discuss beforehand, to knock together
vocab.example: 会議の前に進行について打ち合わせておこう。— Let's arrange the proceedings before the meeting.

vocab.meaning: to cut off, to break off, to discontinue
vocab.example: 視聴率が低迷し、そのドラマは打ち切られた。— Ratings stagnated, and the drama was cancelled.
日本語の打ち消しの表現にはいくつかの種類がある。— There are several types of negative expressions in Japanese.

vocab.meaning: to deny, negate, drown out (a sound)
vocab.example: 彼は関与を打ち消した。— He denied his involvement.

vocab.meaning: to beat/drive in, to dedicate oneself to, to type in (data)
vocab.example: 彼は毎日練習に打ち込んでいる。— He dedicates himself to practice every day.

vocab.meaning: while..., in the course of..., before... (changes)
vocab.example: 温かいうちに食べてください。— Please eat it while it's warm.
彼は宇宙に関する本をたくさん読んでいる。— He reads a lot of books about the universe.

grammar.meaning: "No sooner had X happened than Y" / "Just as X happened, Y happened" — describes two events occurring in rapid, often surprising succession, as observed from outside.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 + （か）と思うと／（か）と思ったら
grammar.example: 空が暗くなったと思うと、突然雨が降り出した。 — No sooner had the sky gone dark than it suddenly started raining.
grammar.file: grammar-(か)と思うと・思ったら.md

grammar.pattern: ～(よ)うと～まいと／～(よ)うが～まいが
grammar.meaning: "Whether X or not" — expresses that it doesn't matter whether something happens/is done or not; the outcome or the speaker's stance is unaffected either way.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞意向形（う・よう形） + と／が ＋ 動詞辞書形 + まい + と／が
grammar.example: 田中先生は、学生たちが理解しようとするまいと、どんどん難しい話を続けた。 — Whether the students understood or not, Professor Tanaka kept pushing on with increasingly difficult material.
grammar.file: grammar-(よ)うと(まいと)・(よ)うが(まいが).md

grammar.meaning: "No matter what/how ~" / "Even if ~" — states that whatever the preceding condition turns out to be, it has no bearing on the speaker's judgment, decision, or determination expressed afterward.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞う・よう形／イ形-かろう／ナ形-だろう・であろう／名詞-だろう・であろう ＋ と(も)／が
grammar.example: たとえ大地震が起ころうと、このビルは安全なはずだ。 — Even if a huge earthquake were to strike, this building should be safe.

grammar.pattern: ～(より)ほか(は)ない／～ほかしかたがない
grammar.meaning: "Have no other choice but to X," "there's nothing to do except X" — expresses that, after considering the situation, only one option remains; a resigned acknowledgment of limited choice.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + (より)ほか(は)ない
grammar.example: 終電を逃したので、タクシーで帰るほかない。 — I missed the last train, so there's no choice but to go home by taxi.
grammar.file: grammar-(より)ほか(は)ない・ほかしかたがない.md

grammar.meaning: "After much ~, (in the end, as a bad result)" — describes the negative or disappointing outcome that results after a long process of effort, deliberation, or trouble.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 + あげく(に) — 例: 悩んだあげく (after much agonizing)
grammar.example: 長時間悩んだあげく、結局彼に別れを告げた。 — After agonizing for a long time, I ended up telling him we were through.

grammar.meaning: Expresses that something can only exist or succeed precisely because the preceding thing exists — "it's only thanks to X that Y is possible," emphasizing X as indispensable.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + あっての + 名詞
grammar.example: 結婚は、相手あってのことだから、相手がいなければどうしようもない。 — Marriage only exists because you have a partner — without one, there's nothing to be done.

grammar.meaning: "N exists because of X / N owes its existence to X" — states that a following noun (often an achievement or relationship) is only possible thanks to the preceding element; without it, the noun wouldn't exist.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + あっての + 名詞
grammar.example: お客様あっての商売だということを忘れてはいけない。 (We must not forget that our business exists only because of our customers.)

grammar.meaning: "Also, additionally" — a casual conjunction adding a point, often as an afterthought.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/clause to the next.
grammar.example: 牛乳買ってきて。あと、卵もお願い。 — Please buy milk. Oh, and eggs too, please.

grammar.meaning: "So much ~ that / to the extent that (as a result of excess)" — indicates that an extreme degree of some emotion or state directly causes an (often unusual or extreme) result.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形/た形 + あまり(に) — 例: 驚いたあまり (being so surprised that)
grammar.example: 驚いたあまり、言葉を失ってしまった。 — I was so surprised that I lost the ability to speak.

grammar.meaning: "It's fine/lucky that X (happened), but..." — acknowledges that a bad outcome was narrowly avoided thanks to X, while implying that things could easily have gone badly and the speaker still feels uneasy or critical about it.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形容詞・な形容詞・名詞 の普通形 (plain form) + からいいようなものの
grammar.example: ぎりぎり間に合ったからいいようなものの、もし遅れていたら、今回のT社との取引はなかっただろう。 — It's fine that we made it just in time, but if we'd been late, this deal with T Company would never have happened.

grammar.meaning: "It all depends on X" — expresses that whether something happens, or how a situation turns out, hinges entirely on the nature or condition of the preceding noun.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + いかんだ（名詞+の+いかんだ／いかんで／いかんでは、の形でもよく使われる）
grammar.example: 世界選手権大会をこの国で開催できるかどうかは、国民の協力いかんだ。 — Whether this country can host the world championship depends entirely on the cooperation of its people.

grammar.pattern: ～いかんにかかわらず／～いかんによらず／～いかんを問わず
grammar.meaning: "Regardless of ~" / "No matter what ~ may be" — states that the outcome or situation in question is not affected or influenced by how some variable factor (content, result, condition, etc.) turns out. A formal, stiff expression typically found in written notices, rules, and announcements.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞（＋の）＋いかんにかかわらず／いかんによらず
grammar.example: 内容のいかんにかかわらず、個人情報の問い合わせにはお答えしておりません。 — Regardless of the content, we do not respond to inquiries about personal information.
grammar.file: grammar-いかんにかかわらず・いかんによらず・いかんを問わず.md

grammar.pattern: ～いかんによらず／いかんにかかわらず／を問わず
grammar.meaning: Regardless of X / no matter what X is — a merged cluster of "regardless of" variants that are tested interchangeably.
grammar.conjugation: [名詞]+の+いかん(によらず／にかかわらず) ; [名詞]+を問わず
grammar.example: 理由のいかんによらず、殺人は許されないことだ。(Regardless of the reason, murder is unforgivable.)
grammar.file: grammar-いかんによらず・いかんにかかわらず・をとわず.md

grammar.pattern: ～といったらない／～ありゃしない
grammar.meaning: "Indescribably X" / "there's nothing like how X it is" — emphasizes an extreme degree of something, usually with a tone of exasperation, amazement, or complaint.
grammar.conjugation: N/adjective + といったらない
grammar.example: 最近残業続きで疲れる(とい)ったらないよ。 — With all this overtime lately, I'm indescribably exhausted.
grammar.file: grammar-いったらない・ありゃしない.md

grammar.meaning: Two related uses: (1) "after doing ~ (and then)" — sequencing an important step before another action; (2) "in the process of ~ / when it comes to ~" — indicating the context/basis in which something is relevant or necessary.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 + 上で — 例: よく考えた上で (after thinking it through carefully)
grammar.example: よく考えた上で、返事をします。 — I will reply after thinking it over carefully.

grammar.pattern: ～(よ)うが／(よ)うと～まいと／(よ)うが～まいが
grammar.meaning: "Whether X happens or not, (it doesn't matter)" — expresses that regardless of whether an action occurs or not, the outcome or the speaker's stance remains unaffected.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞意向形（よう／おう）+ が／と + 動詞まい形 + と／が
grammar.example: 彼が来ようが来まいが、会議は予定通り行う。 (Whether he comes or not, the meeting will proceed as scheduled.)

grammar.meaning: "While ~ / before ~ (changes) / take the opportunity during a limited window" — expresses that an action should be done within a certain state or time period before that state ends or changes.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ている形 + うちに — 例: 温かいうちに (while it's still warm)
grammar.example: 温かいうちに、どうぞ召し上がってください。 — Please eat it while it's still warm.

grammar.meaning: "Let's ~, shall we? / why don't we ~" — a formal, rhetorical volitional invitation, often used to rally or persuade a group toward collective action, with a somewhat dramatic or speech-like tone.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞意向形 (volitional form) + ではないか — 例: 頑張ろうではないか (let's do our best, shall we!)
grammar.example: さあ、みんなで力を合わせて頑張ろうではないか。 — Come now, let's all join forces and do our best together!

grammar.meaning: "Thanks to [your help/everyone's support/circumstances]" — a humble, polite expression used to attribute one's good fortune or successful outcome to the help, concern, or goodwill of others, often used in response to well-wishes or inquiries about one's wellbeing.
grammar.conjugation: Stands alone as a set phrase, often sentence-initial: おかげさまで + [positive outcome]
grammar.example: 「お元気ですか。」「はい、おかげさまで元気にしております。」 — "How have you been?" "Yes, thanks to everyone, I've been doing well."

grammar.meaning: "Thanks to X" — attributes a good result to a positive cause or helper. Can also be used ironically to sarcastically blame something for a bad result ("thanks a lot to X...").
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + の + おかげで
grammar.example: 先生のおかげで、試験に合格しました。 — Thanks to my teacher, I passed the exam.

grammar.meaning: "I don't recall doing X / I have no reason to be X" — denies having done something or having a reputation, often defensively, asserting no memory or basis for an accusation.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／た形 + 覚えはない
grammar.example: 彼が怒るようなことを言った覚えはありません。 (I don't recall saying anything that would make him angry.)

grammar.meaning: "And; as well as" — a very formal conjunction used to connect items in official lists.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous clause to the next. Most frequently, however, it links two nouns/noun phrases mid-sentence (A および B) rather than two full sentences, functioning much like a formal "and."
grammar.example: 本制度は正社員およびパート社員に適用されます。 — This system applies to full-time employees as well as part-time employees.

grammar.meaning: "Almost before X happens / just as X is happening" — expresses extreme near-simultaneity between two events, stronger than ordinary "as soon as."
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／た形 + か + 同じ動詞のない形 + かのうちに
grammar.example: ベルが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、生徒たちは教室を飛び出した。 — Almost before the bell rang, the students dashed out of the classroom.

grammar.meaning: "It's worth/not worth doing X" — expresses whether an effort or action yields a rewarding/meaningful result.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 + 甲斐がある／ない (した甲斐がある, common)
grammar.example: 努力した甲斐があって、見事合格した。 (Thanks to the worthwhile effort, I passed brilliantly.)

grammar.meaning: "Extremely X" — used with emotion adjectives to express the speaker's own feeling at its peak (うらやましい限りだ, "I'm extremely envious"; 嬉しい限りだ, "I'm so happy").
grammar.conjugation: い-adjective/な-adjective + 限りだ
grammar.example: 働かなくても生活できるなんて、うらやましい限りだ。 — Being able to live without working — how extremely enviable.

grammar.meaning: "In the middle of doing ~ / half-done / partway through" — indicates an action was started but left incomplete or interrupted partway through.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb stem) + かけ — 例: 食べかけ (half-eaten), 読みかけ (partway read)
grammar.example: テーブルの上に食べかけのケーキが置いてある。 — There's a half-eaten cake on the table.

grammar.meaning: While also doing X — combining two purposes into one single trip or action, often a formal greeting or errand (e.g. お見舞いかたがた = "while also paying a hospital visit, [I did Y]").
grammar.conjugation: 名詞(スル動詞の語幹) + かたがた
grammar.example: お見舞いかたがた休職中の上司を訪ねた。(I visited my boss, who is on leave, both to check in on him and pay a visit.)

grammar.meaning: "While also doing ~ / alongside ~" — indicates that someone carries out a secondary, ongoing activity (often a job, study, or hobby) in parallel with a main activity, usually over a long period of time.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 (verb dictionary form) + かたわら
grammar.example: 会社員として働くかたわら、小説を書いている。 — While working as a company employee, he also writes novels.

grammar.meaning: "Might well (do something bad) / there's a risk of X" — expresses concern that an undesirable or dangerous outcome could occur.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形（stem）+ かねない
grammar.example: そんな運転は事故を起こしかねない。 — Driving like that could well cause an accident.

grammar.meaning: "Cannot bring oneself to do X" — a polite, formal way of expressing inability or unwillingness, frequently used to politely decline, refuse, or express difficulty, especially in business and service contexts.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形（stem）+ かねる
grammar.example: その件についてはお答えしかねます。 — I'm unable to answer regarding that matter.

grammar.meaning: "As if, as though" — likens a real situation to something that is not actually the case, often used for vivid or figurative description.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞／い形容詞普通形 + かのようだ
grammar.example: 彼女はまるで何も知らないかのように振る舞った。 — She behaved as if she knew nothing.

grammar.meaning: Emphasizes that a quantity, weight, size, or price is remarkably large — "as much/large as X" (e.g., 100万からする "costs as much as a million yen"; 100キロからある "weighs as much as 100 kilos").
grammar.conjugation: [Number + Noun] + からある — used for quantity/size/weight emphasis
grammar.example: この絵は50万円からするそうだ。 — I hear this painting costs as much as 500,000 yen.

grammar.pattern: ～からある・～からする・～からの
grammar.meaning: Indicates a quantity, weight, size, price, or number of people that is "at least that much, or more" — used to emphasize how surprisingly large the figure is.
grammar.conjugation: 数詞 + からある／からする／からの + 名詞
grammar.example: 2トンからあるこの岩を、昔の人はどうやって運んだんだろう。 — I wonder how people in the past managed to move this rock, which weighs a full two tons or more.
grammar.file: grammar-からある・からする・からの.md

grammar.meaning: "Judging from just this one example / even X alone (suggests the rest follows suit)" — cites a single representative example as evidence for a broader (often critical) judgment.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + からして
grammar.example: あの態度からして、彼はやる気がないのだろう。 — Judging just from that attitude, he probably has no motivation.

grammar.meaning: "Just because X (doesn't necessarily mean Y)" — rejects an assumption that would otherwise seem to naturally follow from a stated reason.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 + からといって／からとて, usually followed by a negating phrase such as ～わけではない／～とは限らない／～ことはない
grammar.example: お金があるからといって、幸せだとは限らない。 — Just because you have money doesn't mean you're happy.
grammar.file: grammar-からといって・からとて.md

grammar.meaning: "Since X (one has committed to this / this is the situation), Y (must/should) follow" — expresses strong resolve or obligation that naturally follows from a stated circumstance.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞普通形（どの時制でも）+ からには, typically followed by a statement of determination or obligation (～べきだ／～なければならない／意志形)
grammar.example: 引き受けたからには、最後までやり遂げます。 — Since I've taken this on, I'll see it through to the end.

grammar.pattern: ～から見ると／～から言うと／～からすると
grammar.meaning: "Judging from X / from the standpoint of X" — indicates the basis or evidence from which a conclusion or inference is drawn.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + から見ると／から言うと／からすると + 判断・推量の表現
grammar.example: 彼の話し方から見ると、相当怒っているようだ。 — Judging from the way he talks, he seems quite angry.
grammar.file: grammar-から見ると・言うと・すると.md

grammar.meaning: "Whether very A or very B, the same thing is true" — pairs two antonymous adjective stems to say that the conclusion holds regardless of degree or direction (e.g. "more or less," "for better or worse," "sooner or later").
grammar.conjugation: 形容詞語幹 + かれ + （対になる形容詞語幹）+ かれ　※例外: 悪い → 悪しかれ
grammar.example: 多かれ少なかれ、みんな悩みを抱えている。 — Everyone has worries, to a greater or lesser degree.

grammar.meaning: Two usages: (1) "instead of X" — substitution; (2) "in return for X / while, on the other hand" — expresses a trade-off or balancing contrast between two facts about the same subject.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + の + かわりに
grammar.example: 今日は会議に出席できないので、かわりに部下を行かせます。 — I can't attend the meeting today, so I'll send my subordinate instead.

grammar.meaning: "Worth doing X" — expresses that an action is rewarding or meaningful to do, as in やりがい (worth doing), 生きがい (reason/worth for living), or 〜甲斐がある/ない (there is/isn't value in doing X).
grammar.conjugation: Verb-ます形 (stem) + がい + がある／がない (生きがいがある, 努力したかいがあって)
grammar.example: 努力した甲斐があって、見事合格した。 — Thanks to the effort I put in, I passed brilliantly — the effort was worth it.

grammar.meaning: "Hard to do ~ / difficult to ~ (emotionally or morally, not physically)" — expresses that something is very difficult to do due to psychological, moral, or emotional reasons, often used with verbs like 信じる, 許す, 理解する.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb stem) + がたい — 例: 信じがたい (hard to believe), 許しがたい (hard to forgive)
grammar.example: 彼が嘘をついたなんて、信じがたい。 — It's hard to believe that he told a lie.

grammar.meaning: "Tends to ~ / prone to ~ (often with a negative nuance)" — describes a recurring tendency, often an undesirable habit or frequent occurrence.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb stem) + がち — 例: 忘れがち (tends to forget)
grammar.example: 最近、忙しくて朝食を抜きがちだ。 — Lately I've been busy and tend to skip breakfast.

grammar.meaning: "While/on the occasion of doing X, also do Y" — describes combining two actions/purposes into a single trip or occasion, where Y is accomplished incidentally while primarily doing X.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb ます-stem) + がてら
grammar.example: 散歩がてら、買い物に行きませんか。 — Why don't we go shopping while we're out for a walk?

grammar.meaning: "Because of X / owing to X" — a literary causal connector explaining a reason, often for an unusual or noteworthy result.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞（＋である）＋（が）ゆえに
grammar.example: 若さゆえの過ちだったと、彼は反省していた。 (He reflected that it had been a mistake born of youth.)

grammar.meaning: "No sooner than X, Y happens" — describes two actions occurring in near-instantaneous succession, with Y following X almost simultaneously. Literary, in the same family as ～そばから and ～なり.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 (verb dictionary form) + が早いか
grammar.example: 彼は授業終了のベルが鳴るが早いか、教室を飛び出してトイレへ向かった。 — The moment the end-of-class bell rang, he dashed out of the classroom to the bathroom.

grammar.meaning: "Once X happens, inevitably Y follows" — typically describes an irreversible chain of events, often with a negative or extreme outcome, emphasizing that there is no turning back once the triggering action occurs.
grammar.conjugation: Verb-た形 + が最後
grammar.example: 彼はいったん寝入ったが最後、雷が鳴ろうが、地震が来ようが、絶対に目を覚まさないんです。 — Once he falls asleep, that's it — whether thunder roars or an earthquake hits, he absolutely will not wake up.

grammar.meaning: "Has a tendency to ~ (which is not desirable)" — points out an undesirable tendency, trait, or habit that someone (usually a third person) has, often softened with a hedging adverb.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／ない形・名詞＋の ＋ きらいがある
grammar.example: 彼はどうも物事を悲観的に考えるきらいがある。 — He does tend to think about things rather pessimistically.

grammar.meaning: Two related usages: (1) "only/just X" — a plain limiting function; (2) "ever since X, nothing has happened since / that was the last time" — marks a single past instance with no expected continuation since.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + きり（二人きり — "just the two of us"）
grammar.example: 彼とはあの日会ったきり、一度も連絡がない。 — I haven't heard from him once since I saw him that day.

grammar.meaning: "There's no end/limit to X" — expresses that if one kept going, an activity, list, or complaint would never conclude.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形（たら／と／ば形でも可） + きりがない
grammar.example: 失恋したことですか？数えたらきりがないですね。 (Heartbreaks? If I started counting, there'd be no end to it.)

grammar.meaning: "To do completely / to the end / fully" — attached to a verb stem to emphasize completion or an extreme degree of the action.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形（stem）+ きる
grammar.example: 出された料理を全部食べきった。 — I ate everything that was served.

grammar.meaning: "Extremely X, in the extreme" — intensifies a na-adjective to its utmost degree, often describing a strongly negative quality (失礼極まる態度, "an extremely rude attitude"). Despite the "ない" in きわまりない, it is NOT a literal negation — both forms mean the same intensified "extremely X."
grammar.conjugation: な-adjective stem + 極まる
grammar.example: コンビニで店員に失礼極まる態度をとられ、頭にきた。 — I got angry after being treated with extremely rude behavior by a convenience store clerk.
grammar.file: grammar-きわまる・きわまりない.md

grammar.meaning: "Even though / despite X" — used with a critical, contemptuous, or mocking tone to highlight a contradiction between a fact and someone's behavior or attitude.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞／い形容詞普通形 + くせに
grammar.example: 下手なくせに、人に教えたがる。 — Even though he's bad at it, he insists on teaching others.

grammar.meaning: "I would rather ~ than ~" — expresses that the speaker finds a situation so undesirable that another (often also undesirable) alternative would be preferable. Strong subjective judgment, often with frustration or rhetorical emphasis.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 (verb dictionary form) + くらいなら + [preferred alternative, often ～方がいい／～ほうがましだ／命令形]
grammar.example: え、これ要らないんですか。捨てるくらいなら、私にください。 — Oh, you don't need this? If you're going to throw it away, give it to me instead.

grammar.meaning: "It's only limited to about ~ / that's about the only case" — expresses that something is restricted to a very narrow, specific case, often with a nuance of it being surprisingly few or rare.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞/い形容詞普通形 (verb/i-adjective plain form) + くらいのものだ
grammar.example: 着物は日本の伝統衣装ですが、実際に着るのは結婚式のときくらいのものです。 — Kimono is Japan's traditional clothing, but the only time people actually wear it is really just at weddings.

grammar.meaning: "To the extent that / so much that (as to reach this degree)" — illustrates the intensity of something by citing an extreme or representative example.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞／い形容詞普通形 + くらい（だ）
grammar.example: 恥ずかしくて死にたいくらいだった。 — I was so embarrassed I felt like I wanted to die.
grammar.file: grammar-くらい・ぐらい(だ).md

grammar.meaning: "But, however, although" — a polite-neutral contrastive conjunction, softer in tone than でも.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next. Also very commonly attaches directly to the end of a clause mid-sentence (plain/polite form + けれども) to join two contrasting clauses in one sentence, which is its most frequent use.
grammar.example: このレストランは美味しいけれども、値段が高い。 — This restaurant is delicious, but it's expensive.

grammar.meaning: "Looking/seeming X" — attached to adjective stems to describe an outward appearance or impression that someone or something seems to have a certain quality, typically based on visual observation.
grammar.conjugation: い形容詞語幹（drop い）+ げ
grammar.example: 彼女は何か言いたげな顔をしていた。 — She had a look on her face as if she wanted to say something.

grammar.meaning: "Precisely/especially X" — an emphatic particle that singles out the preceding word as the one true/important thing, often in contrast to other possibilities. Also used in set phrases like こちらこそ ("the pleasure is mine, too") and だからこそ ("precisely because of that").
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + こそ
grammar.example: 今年こそ、日本語能力試験に合格するぞ。 — This year, of all years, I will pass the JLPT!

grammar.meaning: "If anything, X (but never Y)" — a concessive-emphatic construction that emphasizes the stated (often positive/neutral) outcome while categorically denying an opposite, usually negative, outcome.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb stem/masu-stem form) + こそすれ
grammar.example: あなたの行為には感謝こそすれ、誰も迷惑だなんて思っていませんよ。 — If anything, we're grateful for what you did — nobody thinks it's a bother.

grammar.meaning: A sentence-final こと used as a formal/written command, instruction, or rule — equivalent to "Do X." / "Must X." / "Do not X." in notices, regulations, instructions, and official announcements.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + こと。 (must do X)
grammar.example: 携帯電話の電源は必ず切ること。 — Be sure to turn off your cell phone.

grammar.meaning: "How (much)...!" — a rhetorical exclamatory expression used with question words like 何度, どんなに, どれほど to emphasize the high degree of an emotion or situation, without expecting an actual answer.
grammar.conjugation: 何度／どんなに／どれほど + Verb/い-adj (plain form) + ことか
grammar.example: 何度注意したことか、彼はまだ遅刻してくる。 — How many times have I warned him, and yet he still comes late!

grammar.meaning: "Judging from the fact that X / because of the fact that X" — used to explain the reason, origin, or basis for a conclusion, name, or naming convention.
grammar.conjugation: Verb/い-adj (plain form) + ことから
grammar.example: この花は朝だけ咲くことから「朝顔」と呼ばれている。 — Because this flower only blooms in the morning, it is called "morning glory."

grammar.meaning: "Extremely X, beyond compare" — a literary intensifier stating that a quality reaches its utmost extreme, with nothing surpassing it.
grammar.conjugation: な形容詞語幹 + な + こと + この上ない
grammar.example: 遺産を巡る肉親同士の言い争いは見苦しいことこの上ない。 (The dispute among family members over the inheritance is unsightly in the extreme.)

grammar.meaning: "The (best) thing to do is...; you should..." — used to give advice, strong recommendations, or admonitions based on the speaker's judgment of what's necessary or wise.
grammar.conjugation: Verb (dictionary form) + ことだ → affirmative advice
grammar.example: 健康でいたいなら、毎日運動することだ。 — If you want to stay healthy, you should exercise every day.

grammar.meaning: "Because it's (characteristic of) X / knowing X as we do" — used to make a prediction or judgment about someone's likely behavior based on well-known personality traits or past patterns.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞(人) + の + ことだから

grammar.meaning: "Given the fact that X..." — a mild, casual reason-giving expression, often used just before announcing a decision or suggestion, softening the justification rather than stating it bluntly.
grammar.conjugation: Verb/い形容詞/な形容詞の普通形 + ことだし
grammar.example: もう遅いことだし、そろそろ帰ろうか。 — It's getting late, so let's start heading home, shall we?

grammar.meaning: "Since it is a matter of X" — offers a mitigating explanation or excuse for a situation, implying the listener should be understanding/forgiving because of the circumstances described.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形容詞・な形容詞・名詞 の名詞修飾型 (noun-modifying/attributive form) + こととて
grammar.example: 子供のしたこととて、お許しください。 — Please forgive it, since it was something a child did.

grammar.meaning: "Without doing X" — describes performing an action while completely avoiding or never experiencing another action; formal equivalent of ～ないで.
grammar.conjugation: Verb (dictionary form) + ことなく
grammar.example: 彼は一度も諦めることなく、最後まで走り続けた。 — He ran until the end without ever giving up.

grammar.pattern: ～ことなしには／ことなしに(は)
grammar.meaning: Without doing X — it's impossible or very difficult to achieve Y without first doing/experiencing X.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + ことなしに(は)
grammar.example: 日本語の勉強は、実際に習った言葉を使ってみることなしには、なかなか上達しません。(Studying Japanese doesn't really improve much without actually trying to use the words you've learned.)
grammar.file: grammar-ことなしには・ことなしに(は).md

grammar.meaning: "To one's (surprise/regret/relief, etc.)" — placed at the beginning of a sentence before the main clause to express the speaker's emotional reaction to what follows.
grammar.conjugation: い-adj / な-adj(な) / Verb (た form) + ことに（は）
grammar.example: 驚いたことに、彼は試験に満点を取った。 — To my surprise, he got a perfect score on the exam.

grammar.meaning: "It has been decided that X (by circumstance or others, not the speaker's own will)" (ことになる); "It is the rule/custom that X" (ことになっている) — describes decisions, arrangements, or established rules, often ones the speaker had little direct control over.
grammar.conjugation: Verb (dictionary form / ない form) + ことになる
grammar.example: 来年、海外支社で働くことになりました。 — It has been decided that I will work at the overseas branch next year.
grammar.file: grammar-ことになる・なっている.md

grammar.meaning: "There's no need to do X / you don't have to do X" — reassures the listener that an action is unnecessary, often used to comfort or ease worry.
grammar.conjugation: Verb (dictionary form) + ことはない
grammar.example: そんなに謝ることはないよ、気にしていないから。 — There's no need to apologize so much — I'm not bothered by it.

grammar.meaning: "It is true that X, but..." — a concessive construction that first acknowledges a fact (often by repeating the same verb/adjective) before pivoting to a contrasting point with が.
grammar.conjugation: Verb/い形容詞/な形容詞の普通形 + ことは + (same or related verb/adjective) + が
grammar.example: 高いことは高いが、品質を考えれば妥当な値段だと思う。 — It is expensive, true, but considering the quality, I think the price is reasonable.

grammar.meaning: "Nothing in particular / nothing special (to mention)" — denies there being any notable or specific thing worth pointing out.
grammar.conjugation: これといって + 名詞／形容詞 + ない
grammar.example: 今の仕事にこれといって不満はありません。 (I have no particular complaints about my current job.)

grammar.meaning: Classical/literary equivalent of ～ように ("as if, like," adverbial) and ～ような ("like a ~," attributive) — expresses similarity or manner in a formal, bookish register.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／た形 + (が)ごとく(に) — adverbial, modifies a verb
grammar.example: 下記のごとく、規則を定める。 — The rules are established as follows below.

grammar.meaning: "As if X / like X" — a classical literary simile marker, equivalent to ように／よう, often carrying a disparaging or humbly self-deprecating nuance depending on context.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞＋の／動詞辞書形・た形 + ごとし（終止形）
grammar.example: 光陰矢の如し。時間を大切に使いなさい。 (Time flies like an arrow. Use your time wisely.)

grammar.meaning: "Even X" — emphasizes an extreme or surprising example to imply that if even this case applies, other (more expected) cases apply even more strongly.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + さえ

grammar.meaning: "If only X / as long as just X" — expresses that a single minimum condition is sufficient for a result to hold; emphasizes that nothing more than that condition is needed.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + さえ + Verb/adj (ば form)
grammar.example: 時間さえあれば、もっと勉強できるのに。 — If only I had time, I could study more.

grammar.meaning: "As one would expect (of X) / that's X for you" — an expression of admiration acknowledging that someone or something has lived up to its reputation, skill, or expected high standard.
grammar.conjugation: さすが + 名詞 (+は) (admiring a person/thing directly): さすが田中さんですね
grammar.example: さすが田中さんだ、どんな質問にもすぐ答えられる。 — That's Tanaka for you — he can answer any question immediately.

grammar.meaning: "Not at all / no good whatsoever" — used with a negative predicate to emphatically state complete failure, lack of understanding, or absence of a quality. (さっぱり also has a separate, unrelated sense meaning "refreshed, clean, light" as in food or feeling after a shower, e.g. さっぱりした味 "a light/clean taste" — this card focuses on the negative-emphasis usage most relevant to JLPT grammar.)
grammar.conjugation: さっぱり + 〜ない (negative predicate required for the "not at all" sense)
grammar.example: この問題の解き方がさっぱり分からない。 — I have absolutely no idea how to solve this problem.

grammar.meaning: "Furthermore, moreover" — adds an escalating point, stronger in degree than plain addition.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next.
grammar.example: 台風で電車が止まった。さらに、強風で停電も起きた。 — The typhoon stopped the trains. Furthermore, the strong wind also caused a power outage.

grammar.meaning: "Cannot help but do X / have no choice but to do X" — expresses that the speaker is forced into an action against their own will due to circumstances, often with a reluctant nuance.
grammar.conjugation: Verb (ない form, dropping ない) + ざるを得ない
grammar.example: 台風のため、イベントは中止せざるを得なかった。 — Due to the typhoon, we had no choice but to cancel the event.

grammar.meaning: "However, but" — a standard conjunction introducing a contrast or counterpoint to the preceding statement.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next. Occasionally appears mid-sentence after a comma for emphasis, but its default position is at the start of a new sentence.
grammar.example: 彼は一生懸命勉強した。しかし、試験に落ちてしまった。 — He studied hard. However, he failed the exam.

grammar.meaning: "Have no choice but to X / there's nothing to do but X / only X" — expresses that, given the circumstances, a single option remains and must be taken.
grammar.conjugation: Verb (dictionary form) + しかない
grammar.example: 電車がないので、歩いて帰るしかない。 — Since there's no train, I have no choice but to walk home.

grammar.meaning: "Moreover, what's more" — adds a surprising or notable additional fact, often making the situation even more so (more impressive, more severe, etc.).
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next.
grammar.example: この店の料理は美味しい。しかも、値段も手頃だ。 — This restaurant's food is delicious. What's more, the prices are reasonable too.

grammar.meaning: "Therefore, accordingly, consequently" — a formal conjunction presenting the following statement as a logical conclusion drawn from the preceding one.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/clause to the next. It is essentially always used sentence-initially in formal writing rather than mid-sentence; a mid-sentence equivalent would normally be rephrased with ため or ので instead.
grammar.example: 今年度の売上は前年を大きく下回った。したがって、来期は経費削減が急務である。 — This year's sales fell significantly below last year's. Therefore, cutting costs is an urgent priority for next term.

grammar.meaning: "Ended up in the (bad) state of X" — describes the regrettable final outcome of a chain of escalating bad events or behavior, often with exasperation.
grammar.conjugation: V辞書形 + 始末だ (typically after a list of escalating bad events, often preceded by こんな/あんな)
grammar.example: きょうは最悪の日だった。朝は社長に叱られ、午後はコーヒーをこぼしてスーツを汚し、最後は帰りの電車にかばんを忘れる始末だった。 — Today was the worst day. I got scolded by the president in the morning, spilled coffee and stained my suit in the afternoon, and finally ended up forgetting my bag on the train home.

grammar.meaning: "Well then, okay then" — the casual spoken contraction of では, used to transition from the preceding topic/statement to a new action, decision, or next step.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/situation to the next action or topic. Like では, it is also used as a short stand-alone transitional phrase before a command/invitation (じゃ、行こう "okay then, let's go") rather than linking two clauses within a single sentence.
grammar.example: じゃ、そろそろ行こうか。 — Well then, shall we get going?

grammar.meaning: "It's not like X, so..." — points out that the listener/subject is not in a particular (often implausible or excusable) category, and therefore a certain behavior or excuse doesn't make sense, usually delivered with mild scolding or sarcasm.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + ではあるまいし／じゃあるまいし
grammar.example: 子供じゃあるまいし、そんなわがままを言うのはやめなさい。 (You're not a child, so stop being so selfish.)

grammar.meaning: "There's no method/means to X" — expresses that no way exists to accomplish or resolve something, after other options have been exhausted.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + 術がない (する verbs often become 〜するすべ, e.g., 連絡するすべがない)
grammar.example: あらゆる方法を使ってみたが、うまくいかなかった。これ以上できる術がない。 (I tried every method, but nothing worked. There's no more I can do.)

grammar.meaning: Used to give an extreme example and imply that, since even this extreme case holds true, everything less extreme naturally holds true too — close to English "even." A stiff, literary-sounding expression similar to ～さえ but more formal.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞(+助詞) + すら
grammar.example: 彼のうそには、怒りだけではなく悲しみすら覚えた。 — His lie made me feel not just anger, but even sadness.

grammar.meaning: "Entirely/all X" — describes something as being composed entirely of one quality or item, e.g., いいことずくめ ("nothing but good things"), 黒ずくめ ("dressed entirely in black").
grammar.conjugation: N + ずくめ
grammar.example: 今年は昇進や結婚など、いいことずくめの一年だった。 — This year was full of nothing but good things, like a promotion and getting married.

grammar.meaning: "Is bound to (cause X)" / "won't let X not happen" — describes an inevitable natural consequence, or a strong determination/emotion that guarantees a particular outcome will occur.
grammar.conjugation: V-ない形(remove ない) + ずにはおかない
grammar.example: あんなことをされたんだから、仕返しをしないではおかないぞ。 — After what they did to me, I'm bound to get revenge.

grammar.pattern: ～ずには済まない／～ないでは済まない
grammar.meaning: "Can't get away without doing X" — social, moral, or practical pressure makes it impossible to avoid doing X; the matter won't be considered resolved/settled unless X is done.
grammar.conjugation: V-ない形(remove ない) + ずには済まない
grammar.example: 今回の件はこちらが全面的に悪いのだから、謝らないではすまない。 — Since we're entirely at fault this time, we can't get away without apologizing.
grammar.file: grammar-ずにはすまない・ないではすまない.md

grammar.meaning: "Because of X" — attributes a negative result or outcome to a cause, often with a nuance of blame or fault.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + の + せいで
grammar.example: 雨のせいで、試合が中止になった。 — Because of the rain, the match was cancelled.

grammar.meaning: "So, at that point, thereupon" — a conjunction narrating a deliberate decision or action taken by the subject in response to a situation just described.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence (describing a situation or problem) to the next one describing the action taken in response. It is used to open a new sentence narrating the responsive action and is not generally used to link clauses within a single sentence.
grammar.example: 会議で誰も意見を言わなかった。そこで、私が口火を切ることにした。 — No one spoke up at the meeting. So, at that point, I decided to break the ice.

grammar.meaning: "Please, somehow... / I know, but please..." — a polite yet insistent request used when pushing back against someone's refusal or stated difficulty, asking them to make an exception or find a way despite the obstacle they've just mentioned.
grammar.conjugation: そこを何とか + お願いします／していただけませんか (fixed request pattern, typically following the other person's refusal or statement of difficulty)
grammar.example: 「今日はもう予約でいっぱいです」「そこを何とかお願いできませんか」 — "We're fully booked today." "Please, is there any way you could somehow fit me in?"

grammar.meaning: "On top of that, in addition" — adds a notable extra point, similar to しかも but more neutral in tone.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next.
grammar.example: この部屋は広い。そのうえ、日当たりもいい。 — This room is spacious. On top of that, it gets good sunlight too.

grammar.meaning: "One of these days / eventually / before long" — a vague, non-committal way of referring to an unspecified future time, often used to make a casual promise or prediction without pinning down exactly when it will happen.
grammar.conjugation: そのうちに + [future clause] (often paired with volitional forms, intentions, or predictions)
grammar.example: また今度、そのうちにご飯でも食べに行きましょう。 — Let's go grab a meal together sometime, one of these days.

grammar.meaning: "Because of that, for that reason, as a result" — a neutral-to-formal conjunction presenting the following statement as the result or purpose stemming from the preceding one.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/clause to the next. It can also appear mid-sentence as そのために or as 〜、そのため〜 within a longer written sentence to link a cause-clause to a result-clause without starting a new sentence.
grammar.example: この地域は降水量が非常に少ない。そのため、農業にはあまり適していない。 — This region gets very little rainfall. Because of that, it is not well suited to agriculture.

grammar.meaning: "No sooner does X happen than Y happens" — expresses that Y occurs immediately after X, often with a nuance that the effort put into X is immediately undone or repeated endlessly (commonly negative, cyclical, frustrating actions).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 (verb dictionary form) + そばから
grammar.example: この子は片付けたそばから、おもちゃを広げてしまう。 — As soon as this child tidies up, he spreads his toys out again.
