grammar.meaning: "So, and so, that's why" — a casual-neutral conjunction that narrates the next event or reason as the natural outcome of what was just said; also used as a short interjection meaning "and then? / so?" prompting someone to continue.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/clause to the next. It does not typically appear mid-sentence linking two clauses within one sentence the way だから can; それで is almost always its own sentence-initial connector, including as a one-word question (それで？).
grammar.example: 電車が遅れたんです。それで、会議に遅刻してしまいました。 — The train was delayed. So, I ended up being late for the meeting.

grammar.meaning: "Well then, now then" — a polite/formal transitional conjunction used to move from the preceding topic/statement to a new action or segment, often used by hosts, announcers, teachers, or presenters to open or close a formal segment.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous situation/statement to the next action or topic being introduced. Like では, it typically stands alone before an invitation/command (それでは、始めましょう "well then, let's begin") rather than linking clauses within a single sentence.
grammar.example: それでは、本日の講演を始めさせていただきます。 — Well then, I will now begin today's lecture.

grammar.meaning: "Even so, even then, still" — a concessive/contrastive conjunction stating that despite the preceding fact, the following statement remains true.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/fact to the next statement that holds true despite it. It is almost always used sentence-initially rather than linking clauses mid-sentence; a mid-sentence equivalent would typically use のに or けれども instead.
grammar.example: 何度失敗しても、それでも彼は諦めなかった。 — No matter how many times he failed, he still didn't give up.

grammar.meaning: "And yet, despite that" — a contrastive conjunction that adds an emotional nuance of surprise, frustration, or unfairness, stronger than plain "however."
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next.
grammar.example: 彼女は何度も謝った。それなのに、彼は許してくれなかった。 — She apologized many times. And yet, he wouldn't forgive her.

grammar.meaning: "If that's the case, then; in that case" — a conditional/suppositional conjunction that takes the preceding statement as a premise and draws a practical conclusion or suggestion from it.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous statement (treated as a given premise) to the conclusion, suggestion, or question that follows. It is almost always used sentence-initially as a reactive response to something just said, rather than linking clauses within a single sentence.
grammar.example: A: 明日は雨らしいよ。 B: それなら、予定を変更しよう。 — A: It seems it'll rain tomorrow. B: If that's the case, let's change our plans.

grammar.meaning: "That's the end of it" / "if X happens, everything is over/pointless" — expresses finality or futility, commonly used in the pattern "no matter how much effort is put in, if Y happens, それまでだ (it's all for nothing)."
grammar.conjugation: Clause (often 〜ば/〜たら/〜ても) + それまでだ
grammar.example: いくら貯金ばかりしても、死んでしまえばそれまでのことだよ。 — No matter how much you save money, if you die, that's the end of it.

grammar.meaning: "And what's more..." — adds emphatic, often exasperated or surprised reinforcement to the immediately preceding statement.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/clause to the next. Frequently used to tack on a short, punchy clarifying detail right after the main statement, almost like an exclamation.
grammar.example: 彼、また遅刻したんだって。それも、三十分も。 — I heard he was late again. And get this, by thirty minutes.

grammar.meaning: "Therefore, hence, for that reason" — a very formal, literary conjunction marking the following clause as a reasoned consequence of the preceding one.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/clause to the next. It can also appear as それゆえに mid-sentence or at a clause boundary (〜であり、それゆえに〜) in highly formal writing, but even then it functions as a connector between two logically linked statements rather than a conjugating element.
grammar.example: 人間は過ちを犯す生き物である。それゆえ、寛容の精神が必要とされる。 — Human beings are creatures that err. For that reason, a spirit of tolerance is necessary.

grammar.meaning: "To treat/pretend as if X had (or hadn't) happened" — a deliberate, often contrary-to-fact pretense in which the speaker(s) agree to act as though some event did or did not occur, regardless of reality.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 + ことにする (to decide to treat it as though X happened)
grammar.example: さっきの失言は聞かなかったことにしてください。 — Please pretend you didn't hear that slip of the tongue I just made.

grammar.meaning: "Even if, even though" — a concessive construction where たとえ emphasizes a hypothetical or extreme condition before the concessive ても/でも clause.
grammar.conjugation: たとえ + 動詞て形 + も
grammar.example: たとえ失敗しても、諦めずに挑戦し続けるつもりだ。 — Even if I fail, I intend to keep trying without giving up.

grammar.meaning: "When I did X, (as a result I discovered/found) Y" — connects a completed action to an ensuing, often unexpected, discovery or result; not a plain temporal "when."
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 (verb, past plain form) + ところ
grammar.example: 先生に聞いたところ、宿題は来週までということだった。 — When I asked the teacher, it turned out the homework was due next week.

grammar.meaning: "Even if/even having done X, (it won't change anything)" — a low-expectation conditional that presents an action as ultimately futile or insufficient to change the outcome.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 (verb た-form) + ところで
grammar.example: 彼女、すごく怒っているから、謝ったところで、僕を許してくれないだろう。 — She's so angry that even if I apologize, she probably won't forgive me.

grammar.meaning: "The instant that..., no sooner had X happened than Y" — emphasizes immediacy and often surprise between two closely sequential events.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 (verb, past plain form) + とたん(に)
grammar.example: ドアを開けたとたんに、猫が飛び出してきた。 — The instant I opened the door, the cat jumped out.

grammar.meaning: "If (I/you) had done ~ (things would have been different)" — a counterfactual past conditional expressing regret or hypothetical reflection about a past action that didn't happen, implying a different (usually better) outcome would have resulted.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 (verb past form) + なら
grammar.example: あの時すぐ手術を受けていたなら、助かったのに。 — If I had undergone surgery right away back then, I would have been saved.

grammar.meaning: "Every time, whenever X happens, Y also happens" — describes a recurring correlation between two events.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 (verb, dictionary form) + たびに
grammar.example: この曲を聞くたびに、学生時代を思い出す。 — Every time I hear this song, I remember my school days.

grammar.meaning: A dated, authoritative command form ("do this") typically used by an older or higher-status man addressing a younger or subordinate person — a mild, somewhat paternal imperative.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 + 給え
grammar.example: 銀行で働いているなら、新聞ぐらい読みたまえ。 (If you work at a bank, at least read the newspaper, won't you.)

grammar.meaning: "X has never once happened" — emphasizes that despite repeated opportunity or expectation, a particular outcome has never occurred even a single time.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 + ためしがない (past-tense verb + ためしがない)
grammar.example: 伊藤さんは約束の時間通りに来たためしがない。 (Mr. Ito has never once come at the promised time.)

grammar.meaning: "Once ~ happens, it's over / something terrible inevitably follows" — describes an action that, once it takes place, is guaranteed to lead to a bad, often irreversible, outcome.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 ＋ ら最後／が最後
grammar.example: 兄は大酒飲みだから、飲み始めたら最後、酔いつぶれるまで飲んでしまう。 — My brother is a heavy drinker, so once he starts drinking, that's it — he keeps going until he's completely drunk.
grammar.file: grammar-たら最後・たが最後.md

grammar.meaning: "Not even X (however small/brief)" — emphasizes that not even the smallest unit or briefest instance of something is permitted or occurs, typically paired with a negative predicate.
grammar.conjugation: 数量を表す名詞（一瞬、一刻、一人など）+ たりとも + ～ない
grammar.example: 試合中は一瞬たりとも気を抜けない。 (During the match, you can't let your guard down even for a single instant.)

grammar.meaning: "Not even one [minimal unit]..." / "not at all" — cites the smallest possible unit of a quantity to emphatically stress that something does not happen or is not allowed in the slightest.
grammar.conjugation: 1 + 助数詞 + たりとも + …ない
grammar.example: あなたのことは1日たりとも忘れたことはありません。 — I have not forgotten you for even a single day.

grammar.meaning: "Being in the position/status of X (and thus should behave accordingly)" — describes someone as holding a particular status or role, with the implication that they carry a corresponding duty or expected standard of behavior.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + たる + 名詞 (most often 者/もの, "person")
grammar.example: 政治家たる者が、そんな無責任な発言をするなんて、信じられない。 — It's unbelievable that someone in the position of a politician would make such an irresponsible statement.

grammar.meaning: States that someone who holds a responsible or superior position/role ought to behave in a manner befitting that status — used to describe the ideal, expected conduct for such a person.
grammar.conjugation: 名 + たるもの（は）
grammar.example: 経営者たるものは、一般的な法律や年金制度について知っておかなければならない。 — Anyone who is to be a manager must have a working knowledge of general law and the pension system.

grammar.meaning: A casual, somewhat old-fashioned masculine sentence-final question particle — だい follows a noun/na-adjective predicate ("what time is it?"), while かい attaches more broadly for yes/no or softened questions.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／な形容詞語幹 + だい (replacing plain だ in a question)
grammar.example: 今、何時だい？ (What time is it now?)

grammar.meaning: "So, therefore, that's why" — a casual conjunction stating that the preceding statement is the reason/cause for what follows.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next. It can also appear mid-sentence after a clause ending in plain/だ form (e.g. 雨だから、行かない) to directly link a reason-clause to its result within a single sentence.
grammar.example: 今日は雨だから、傘を持って行った方がいいよ。 — It's raining today, so you'd better bring an umbrella.

grammar.meaning: "But, however" — a terse, literary contrastive conjunction.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next.
grammar.example: 努力はした。だが、結果は出なかった。 — I made the effort. But the results didn't show.

grammar.meaning: "Only, just, as much as" — a basic limiter marking exclusivity or extent.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + だけ
grammar.example: このケーキは一つだけ残っている。 — Only one piece of this cake remains.

grammar.meaning: "Being worthy of X, as one would expect from X" — praises a result that matches or justifies a person's reputation, status, or effort.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + だけあって
grammar.example: さすが一流レストランだけあって、料理の味も盛り付けも素晴らしい。 — As expected of a top-class restaurant, both the taste and presentation are wonderful.

grammar.meaning: "But, though" — a very casual, colloquial contrastive conjunction.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/clause to the next. Also frequently attaches directly after a plain-form clause or noun+だ (〜だけど) mid-sentence in casual speech.
grammar.example: 行きたいんだけど、お金がないんだよね。 — I want to go, but I don't have any money.

grammar.meaning: "Precisely because X, all the more so" — indicates that a known fact or situation intensifies the following result, which can be either positive or negative.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + だけに
grammar.example: 長年努力しただけに、合格の喜びはひとしおだった。 — Precisely because he'd worked hard for years, the joy of passing was all the greater.

grammar.meaning: "But, because..." — a very casual, often petulant or defensive conjunction used to give an excuse or justification, frequently in response to being questioned or criticized.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous remark (usually someone else's question or criticism) to the speaker's excuse/justification that follows. It is essentially always sentence-initial in dialogue and is not used to link two clauses within a single sentence.
grammar.example: A: なんでまた遅刻したの? B: だって、バスが全然来なかったんだもん。 — A: Why were you late again? B: But the bus just wouldn't come!

grammar.meaning: Not even X — an emphatic negative expressing extreme degree (e.g. 想像だにできない = "can't even imagine").
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + だにしない ／ 動詞辞書形 + だに, restricted to a small set of fixed collocations such as 想像だに、予想だに、微動だに.
grammar.example: 人類が月に行ける日が来るなんて、百年前には想像だにしなかったことだ。(A hundred years ago, people couldn't even imagine that a day would come when humanity could go to the moon.)

grammar.meaning: "Covered in, full of X" — usually carries a negative or messy connotation (e.g., mistakes, dirt, debt).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + だらけ
grammar.example: この作文は間違いだらけだ。 — This essay is full of mistakes.

grammar.meaning: Casual sentence-final particle used to confirm or recall forgotten information — "wasn't it...?", "was it...?"
grammar.conjugation: 動詞／い形容詞 plain form (past or non-past) + っけ
grammar.example: 明日は何時に集合だったっけ? — What time were we supposed to meet tomorrow again?

grammar.meaning: Casual, strong negation of possibility — "there's no way that X," "X will never happen."
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb, ます-stem) + っこない
grammar.example: こんな難しい問題、私に解けっこない。 — There's no way I can solve such a difficult problem.

grammar.meaning: An extremely emphatic degree expression meaning "indescribably/to an extreme degree" — used to stress that a feeling, state, or quality is so intense it defies ordinary description, usually about something striking, extreme, or exasperating.
grammar.conjugation: い形容詞語幹 + といったらない / ったらない: 嬉しいといったらない / 嬉しいったらない (indescribably happy)
grammar.example: 久しぶりに親友に会えて、嬉しいったらない。 — Being able to see my best friend after so long — I'm indescribably happy.

grammar.meaning: "Leaving X in an ongoing/neglected state" — an action is performed and then left without the expected follow-up or correction, often implying carelessness (つけっぱなし, "left turned on").
grammar.conjugation: V-ます形(stem) + っぱなし
grammar.example: 弟はいつもテレビをつけっぱなしにして出かける。 — My little brother always leaves the TV on when he goes out.

grammar.meaning: Describes an unusual or improper state that is continuing — typically an action left undone that should have been reversed, or a one-sided position endured for too long.
grammar.conjugation: 動ます形 + っぱなしだ
grammar.example: 昨日は電気をつけっぱなしで寝てしまった。 — Yesterday I fell asleep with the light left on.

grammar.meaning: Two closely related uses: (1) attached to a verb stem or noun, describes the "manner/way of doing X" (e.g., 食べっぷり, "the way one eats," often admiringly); (2) attached to a time-duration noun, ぶり means "for the first time in [duration]" (e.g., 三年ぶり, "for the first time in three years").
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb ます-stem) + っぷり／ぶり (manner-of-doing sense)
grammar.example: 彼の食べっぷりは見ていて気持ちがいい。 — The way he eats is satisfying just to watch.

grammar.meaning: "-ish, seems like, prone to" — a casual suffix attached to nouns, adjective stems, or verb stems to indicate a tendency or resemblance.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／な形容詞語幹／い形容詞語幹／動詞ます形 + っぽい (conjugates like an い-adjective: っぽくない、っぽかった)
grammar.example: 彼はまだ子供っぽいところがある。 — He still has a childish side to him.

grammar.meaning: Describes two reciprocal or opposite actions happening repeatedly, back and forth (e.g. "going and coming," "overtaking and being overtaken"). It attaches only to a small, fixed set of verb pairs and functions almost entirely as set idiomatic expressions rather than a freely productive pattern.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 + つ + 動詞ます形（対になる動詞）+ つ
grammar.example: あの人はさっきから店の前を行きつ戻りつしている。 — That person has been going back and forth in front of the shop for a while now.

grammar.meaning: "While at it, taking the opportunity to also do Y" — performing a secondary, incidental action while doing a main action.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／た形 (verb, dictionary or past form) + ついでに
grammar.example: スーパーに行くついでに、牛乳を買ってきてくれる? — Since you're going to the supermarket, could you buy some milk while you're at it?

grammar.meaning: Two related uses: (1) "while doing X" — two actions happening simultaneously by the same subject; (2) "although/even while X, Y" — a concessive sense where the main clause contradicts or qualifies what the つつ-clause would suggest.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 + つつ (verb stem + つつ)
grammar.example: 彼は景色を眺めつつ、故郷のことを思い出していた。 (Gazing at the scenery, he was recalling thoughts of his hometown.)

grammar.meaning: "In the process of gradually happening/changing" — describes an ongoing change-of-state, formal register.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb, ます-stem) + つつある (mainly with change-of-state verbs like 増える、減る、進む、回復する)
grammar.example: 地球の気温は年々上昇しつつある。 — The earth's temperature is gradually rising year by year.

grammar.meaning: With the intention of / as if pretending to X — acting as though something were done or true, often for self-discipline or framing purposes.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 + つもりで (the "pretend" nuance specifically uses た形, e.g. 買ったつもりで "as if I had bought it")
grammar.example: 冬のコートを買ったつもりで、5万円貯金した。(I saved 50,000 yen, treating it as if I had bought a winter coat.)

grammar.meaning: "Now X, now Y / alternately doing X and Y" — describes two opposite or alternating actions happening repeatedly, back and forth.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 + つ + 対になる動詞ます形 + つ (verb stem + つ + opposite-meaning verb stem + つ)
grammar.example: しばらく入り口の前で行きつ戻りつしていたが、意を決してドアを開けた。 (He paced back and forth in front of the entrance for a while, then resolved himself and opened the door.)

grammar.meaning: "Can't afford to keep on doing X" — expresses that due to a lack of time or emotional composure, one cannot remain in a certain state or keep doing a certain thing; implies the need to act immediately instead.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + は + いられない
grammar.example: やると決めたら、のんびりしてはいられない。今すぐ準備を始めよう。 — Once I've decided to do it, I can't just relax. Let's start preparing right now.

grammar.meaning: "This is not the time for X" — urges that a current action is inappropriate or irresponsible given more pressing circumstances.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ている形 + 場合ではない
grammar.example: 冗談を言っている場合ではありません。早く対応策を考えないと。 (This is not the time for joking. We need to think of a countermeasure quickly.)
grammar.file: grammar-ているばあいではない.md

grammar.pattern: ～てからでないと／てからでなければ
grammar.meaning: "Unless one does X first, not until after doing X" — states that Y cannot happen until X is completed first, framing X as a required precondition.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 (verb, te-form) + からでないと／からでなければ + (negative-potential consequence)
grammar.example: 医者に相談してからでないと、薬を変えることはできない。 — You can't change the medication unless you consult a doctor first.
grammar.file: grammar-てからでないと・なければ.md

grammar.pattern: ～てからというもの／というもの
grammar.meaning: "Ever since X (things have been dramatically different) / for X (duration), continuously (in a negative state)" — emphasizes a lasting, noticeable change that began at a specific point, or a prolonged period of continuous negative experience.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + からというもの
grammar.example: 結婚してからというもの、彼はすっかり落ち着いた。 (Ever since getting married, he has settled down completely.)

grammar.meaning: "Ever since X..." — describes how, following a particular turning-point event, some new change or condition set in and has continued steadily ever since, often looking back reflectively over a span of time.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + からというもの（は）
grammar.example: 娘が大学に入り家を出ていってからというもの、家の中が寂しくなった。 — Ever since my daughter entered university and left home, the house has felt lonely.

grammar.meaning: (Please) do X for me — a blunt, masculine imperative request.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + くれ
grammar.example: ちょっと待ってくれ。(Wait a moment for me.)

grammar.pattern: ～てたまらない／～て仕方がない／～てしょうがない
grammar.meaning: "Unbearably X, cannot help feeling X" — intensifies an emotion or physical sensation to the point of being unbearable or uncontrollable.
grammar.conjugation: い形容詞 (くて) + たまらない／しかたがない／しょうがない
grammar.example: 久しぶりに家族に会えて、嬉しくてたまらない。 — I'm unbearably happy to see my family after so long.
grammar.file: grammar-てたまらない・しようがない・しかたがない.md

grammar.meaning: There's no way I'll let X happen! / I absolutely refuse to accept X — a strong refusal or indignant exclamation.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + たまるか (also directly after some predicates without て, as in 負けてたまるか which still uses て形 of 負ける)
grammar.example: 失恋ぐらいで泣いてたまるか。(As if I'd cry over something like a broken heart!)
grammar.file: grammar-てたまるか・たまるか.md

grammar.meaning: "Cannot help feeling X" — similar to てたまらない but more literary/written in register.
grammar.conjugation: い形容詞 (くて) + ならない
grammar.example: 彼が何か隠しているような気がしてならない。 — I can't help feeling like he's hiding something.

grammar.meaning: "To manage to do ~ (impressively/surprisingly, without apparent difficulty)" — describes accomplishing something difficult, bold, or unexpected with surprising ease, often impressing or surprising onlookers.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 (verb te-form) + のける
grammar.example: 5歳の弟はわたしや兄が解けなかった数学の問題をたった1分でやってのけた。 — My 5-year-old brother solved, in just one minute, the math problem that neither my older brother nor I could solve.

grammar.meaning: Expresses a repeated or habitual action-reaction cycle — "does X, and then (repeatedly) Y happens" — often used in doubled form (Aては B、Bては A) to depict an endless back-and-forth or iterative process.
grammar.conjugation: Verb-て form + は (contraction often pronounced/written じゃ in casual speech: 食べては → 食べちゃ)
grammar.example: 波が寄せては返す。 — The waves come in and then recede, over and over.

grammar.meaning: Describes a single action (or short sequence of actions) being repeated over and over, often conveying a sense of persistence, habit, or restless repetition — "keeps doing A, then A again, then A again."
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + は + （結果・続く行動）、動詞て形 + は + ...（繰り返し）
grammar.example: 書いては消し、書いては消して、手紙を書き上げた。 — He finished the letter by writing and erasing it, over and over again.

grammar.meaning: "I can't stand/bear it if X (keeps happening)" — complains that a recurring or continuing action/state is intolerable.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + は + かなわない (Vて + はかなわない)
grammar.example: こう毎日暑くてはかなわないなあ。 (I can't stand it being this hot every single day.)

grammar.meaning: "Doesn't hesitate to (boldly say/do) X" — describes someone stating or doing something bold, often arrogant or provocative, without any reservation.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + はばからない (Vて + はばからない)
grammar.example: 吉田課長は「次に部長になるのは自分だろう」と言ってはばからない。 (Section Chief Yoshida boldly declares, without hesitation, "I'll surely be the next department head.")

grammar.meaning: "Given the circumstances/in front of (others)" — expresses a face-saving obligation: the speaker must act (or refrain from acting) a certain way because of appearances, position, or a prior statement made in front of others.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞普通形 (verb plain form) + てまえ
grammar.example: 夫がH自動車に勤めている手前、T自動車の車を買うわけにはいかないでしょう。 — Given that my husband works at H Motors, we obviously can't buy a car from T Motors.

grammar.meaning: Will do X to prove it / show someone that one can do X — expresses strong personal determination.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + みせる
grammar.example: 今回は負けてしまったけど、次の試合では必ず勝ってみせるさ。(I lost this time, but I will definitely win next time, you'll see.)

grammar.meaning: Try doing X / go ahead and do X — an imperative challenge or dare directed at the listener.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + みろ
grammar.example: 部長の前でそんなこと言ってみろ、3時間は説教されるぞ。(Just try saying that in front of the department head — you'll get a three-hour lecture.)

grammar.meaning: "It's fine/no problem even if X" — politely grants permission or reassures that an action causes no inconvenience or issue.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 + も差し支えない
grammar.example: その資料は捨てても差し支えありませんよ。 (It's fine to throw that document away.)

grammar.meaning: "Never stop doing X" / "continue to feel X without end" — expresses that a feeling (hope, wish, respect, love) persists endlessly and unabated. Used almost exclusively with emotion/wish verbs like 願う, 祈る, 愛する, 尊敬する.
grammar.conjugation: V-て形 + やまない
grammar.example: 早く先輩の病気が良くなることを願ってやみません。 — I never stop hoping that my senior's illness will get better soon.

grammar.meaning: Benefactive auxiliary meaning "do (something) for someone" from a position of equal or higher status than the recipient; can also express a confrontational/determined "I'll show you/do X to you" nuance, often used to express spite, determination, or defiance.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 (verb て-form) + やる
grammar.example: こんな会社、いつでも辞めてやるわ！ — A company like this — I'll quit it anytime I please!

grammar.meaning: "So, and then, and" — a casual contraction of それで used to prompt or continue a conversation, often asking "so then what?"
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence/utterance boundary, connecting the previous remark to the next. Unlike most conjunctions in this set, で is used almost exclusively mid-conversation (not between written sentences/paragraphs) to prompt the listener to continue their story or to transition to the next point in one's own speech.
grammar.example: 「昨日彼女に会ったよ。」「で、どうだった?」 — "I met her yesterday." "So, how was it?"

grammar.pattern: ～であれ…であれ・～であろうと…であろうと
grammar.meaning: "Whether it's X or Y, the same thing holds true regardless" — lists representative examples within one category and asserts that something applies to all of them equally, irrespective of which one it is.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + であれ／であろうと
grammar.example: 地震であれ火事であれ、緊急の場合に冷静になれる人は少ないだろう。 — Whether it's an earthquake or a fire, few people can stay calm in an emergency.
grammar.file: grammar-であれ…であれ・であろうと…であろうと.md

grammar.pattern: ～であれ～であれ／かれ～かれ／であろうと(が)
grammar.meaning: "Whatever A or B / no matter whether it's A or B" — presents two or more contrasting possibilities as equally irrelevant to a stated conclusion, emphasizing the conclusion holds regardless.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + であれ + 名詞 + であれ
grammar.example: 大人であれ子供であれ、ルールは守らなければならない。 (Whether adult or child, the rules must be followed.)

grammar.meaning: "Even if it's X" / "No matter what X is" — states that even under the given condition or identity, nothing changes; the condition has no bearing on the outcome.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞・疑問詞 + であれ／であろうと
grammar.example: たとえあらしの夜であれ、わたしは仕事のためなら外出する。 — Even if it's a stormy night, I'll go out if it's for work.
grammar.file: grammar-であれ・であろうと.md

grammar.meaning: "Even X" — emphasizes an extreme or unexpected example to highlight how broadly a statement applies, often implying "if even this surprising case is true, then certainly everything else is too."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞（＋は）＋ ですら
grammar.example: この問題は専門家ですら解けないそうだ。 (Apparently, even experts can't solve this problem.)

grammar.meaning: A rhetorical expression meaning "if this isn't X, then what is?" — used to strongly assert that something can only be described as X, typically to convey admiration, emotion, or exasperation. A stiff, literary expression.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + でなくてなんだろう（か）
grammar.example: 毎日仕事が楽しくてしかたがない。これこそ天職でなくてなんだろう。 — I find my work enjoyable every single day without fail — if this isn't my true calling, then what is?
grammar.file: grammar-でなくてなんだろう（か）.md

grammar.meaning: "If this isn't X, what is!" — a rhetorical, emphatic assertion that something is unmistakably X, used for dramatic effect.
grammar.conjugation: N + でなくてなんであろう(か) — a fixed literary rhetorical-question form, often preceded by これが/それこそが to point at the thing being emphatically named
grammar.example: 美しい妻とかわいい子供のいる生活、これが幸せでなくてなんであろう。 — A life with a beautiful wife and an adorable child — if this isn't happiness, what is!
grammar.file: grammar-でなくてなんであろう.md

grammar.meaning: "Well then, in that case" — a transitional conjunction used to move from the preceding topic/statement to a new action, topic, or next step.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/situation to the next action or topic being introduced. It is also commonly used as a short stand-alone transitional phrase before a command/invitation (では、始めましょう "well then, let's begin") rather than linking two clauses within one sentence.
grammar.example: では、次の議題に移りましょう。 — Well then, let's move on to the next agenda item.

grammar.meaning: "It's not as if X" — points out that since the situation is clearly not X, the reaction or behavior under discussion doesn't make sense; often used to criticize or give advice. Spoken-language style.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + ではあるまいし
grammar.example: 子供ではあるまいし、眠かったり空腹だったりするだけでそんなに不機嫌な顔をするものではない。 — You're not a child — you shouldn't make such a sour face just because you're sleepy or hungry.

grammar.meaning: "But, however" — the most common everyday casual conjunction for contrast.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence/clause to the next.
grammar.example: 疲れてた。でも、最後まで頑張った。 — I was tired. But I pushed through to the end.

grammar.meaning: "Not X at all / is nothing of the sort" — flatly refutes that something/someone is a particular noun/category, usually correcting a false assumption.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／な形容詞 + でもなんでもない
grammar.example: 違いますよ。川口さんは私の恋人でもなんでもありません。 (That's wrong. Mr. Kawaguchi is not my boyfriend at all.)
grammar.file: grammar-でもなんでもない.md

grammar.meaning: "Ever since doing X" — marks a point in the past after which a situation has continued up to the present.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 (verb, te-form) + 以来
grammar.example: 日本に来て以来、ずっと一人暮らしをしている。 — Ever since coming to Japan, I've been living alone the whole time.

grammar.meaning: "Since it's the special circumstance of X" — explains that, because the situation described is unusual or special, a correspondingly special/notable result naturally followed.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞・普通形 + とあって
grammar.example: 久しぶりの快晴の連休とあって、行楽地はどこも人でいっぱいだった。 — Since it was a rare sunny holiday after a long spell of bad weather, every tourist spot was packed with people.

grammar.pattern: ～とあって／とあっては／あれば
grammar.meaning: "Because it is a special case of ~ / given that it is ~" — explains a noteworthy result or situation as being due to a special, unusual, or significant circumstance. とあれば can also mean "if it's a case of ~ (then of course)."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞/普通形 (noun/plain form) + とあって (reason, result follows)
grammar.example: 連休最後の日曜日とあって、行楽地はどこも家族連れの観光客でにぎわいました。 — Since it was the last Sunday of the long holiday, resort areas everywhere were bustling with tourists and families.
grammar.file: grammar-とあって・とあっては・あれば.md

grammar.meaning: "If it's a matter of ~" / "Given the special circumstance that ~" — presents a particular condition as noteworthy or special, and the following clause expresses what the speaker is willing to do or believes will be the case under that condition.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／普通形 ＋ とあれば
grammar.example: 子供のためとあれば、わたしはどんなことでも我慢しますよ。 — If it's for my child's sake, I'll put up with anything.

grammar.meaning: "Looking at X, and also at Y, the same impression holds" — gives two examples of aspects of something and states an overall judgment or evaluation about it based on them.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + といい
grammar.example: この映画は映像の美しさといい音楽の素晴らしさといい、最高の作品だ。 — Between the beauty of the visuals and the wonderful music, this film is a masterpiece.

grammar.meaning: Both X and Y / whether you look at X or Y — citing two illustrative examples to support an evaluative statement about the whole.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + といい、名詞 + といい
grammar.example: あのレストランは味といい、サービスといい、最高級だ。(That restaurant is top-notch, whether you consider the taste or the service.)

grammar.meaning: "Every single N / N after N (emphatic totality)" — repeats the same noun on both sides of という to emphasize that without exception, all instances of that noun are affected.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + という + 同じ名詞 (N というN)
grammar.example: 激しい地震で街中のビルというビルが崩れ落ちた。 (In the violent earthquake, every single building throughout the town collapsed.)

grammar.meaning: "You could call it X, or maybe Y" — hedges between two (or more) possible descriptions when the speaker isn't sure which single word best captures something.
grammar.conjugation: 形容詞／名詞／動詞普通形 + というか + 形容詞／名詞／動詞普通形 + というか、+ まとめの表現
grammar.example: 母は人がよすぎるというか、単純というか、他人が言うことをすぐ信じてしまう。 (My mother is, how should I put it, too good-natured, or maybe just simple — she believes whatever other people tell her right away.)

grammar.meaning: (1) "I heard that..." — reporting information from a secondhand source (hearsay, news, something someone said). (2) "It means that..." — restating or drawing a conclusion/paraphrase from something previously said.
grammar.conjugation: Plain form of verb/adjective + ということだ
grammar.example: ニュースによると、台風は明日上陸するということだ。 — According to the news, I heard that the typhoon will make landfall tomorrow.

grammar.pattern: ～というと／といえば／といったら
grammar.meaning: "Speaking of X," "when you mention X," "if we're talking about X" — used to pick up a topic just mentioned (or closely associated) and comment on it, often introducing an association, reminder, or tangent.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + というと／といえば／といったら
grammar.example: 京都というと、やっぱり紅葉がきれいな場所ですね。 — Speaking of Kyoto, it's really known for its beautiful autumn leaves.
grammar.file: grammar-というと・といえば・といったら.md

grammar.meaning: "The reason is that..., what I mean is..." — a conjunction that introduces an explanation or elaboration clarifying/justifying the statement just made.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the explanatory sentence that follows (often itself ending in 〜からだ/〜のだ, similar to なぜなら, though this ending is optional rather than obligatory). It can also appear mid-sentence after a noun or quoted term (「残業代」というのは〜 "what is meant by 'overtime pay' is...") to introduce a definition or clarification of that term, a distinct but related usage from its sentence-connecting role.
grammar.example: 今日は休ませてもらいます。というのは、昨夜からずっと熱があるんです。 — I'll be taking the day off today. The reason is, I've had a fever since last night.

grammar.meaning: "That's exactly what X is," "that's just the nature of X" — an emphatic statement of the speaker's judgment or a general truth, often expressing common sense or a strongly held opinion.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form of verb/adjective) + というものだ
grammar.example: 困っている人を助けるのが友達というものだ。 — Helping a friend in need — that's exactly what a friend is for.

grammar.meaning: "It's not necessarily the case that X" / "It's not as simple as saying X" — used to refute or soften an overly simplistic assumption, often after presenting a common belief.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form) + というものではない／というものでもない
grammar.example: お金があれば幸せになれるというものではない。 — Having money doesn't necessarily mean you'll be happy.
grammar.file: grammar-というものでは・もない.md

grammar.meaning: "Rather than X, it's more like Y" / "more accurately, Y" — corrects or refines a preceding description by presenting a more fitting characterization.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form) + というより + むしろ + Y
grammar.example: この映画は怖いというよりむしろ悲しい話だった。 — Rather than scary, this movie was more of a sad story.

grammar.meaning: "Even though X / although X" — a literary concessive connector acknowledging a fact or status, then asserting that an exception or qualification still applies despite it.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／普通形 + と言えど（も）
grammar.example: 専門家と言えども、間違えることはある。 (Even experts can make mistakes.)

grammar.meaning: "Such as X (and similar things)" — introduces one or more representative examples of a broader category, similar to English "such as" or "like."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞（、名詞）+ といった + 名詞
grammar.example: この近海では、鰯や鯛といった魚が釣れます。 (In these coastal waters, you can catch fish such as sardines and sea bream.)

grammar.meaning: "That's about the extent of it" — gives a modest, approximate assessment of a quantity, degree, or situation; implies "no more, no less than roughly X."
grammar.conjugation: N/数量表現 + といったところだ
grammar.example: 留学生のアルバイトだったら、時給は800円から1000円といったところだ。 — For a foreign student's part-time job, the hourly wage is about 800 to 1000 yen, give or take.

grammar.meaning: Expresses that something is to such an extreme degree that words fail to capture it — "indescribably ~," "~ beyond words." Spoken language, used for strong emotional reactions.
grammar.conjugation: イ形い／ナ形(だ)／名 + といったらない
grammar.example: あいつはだらしないといったらない。物はよくなくすし、時間にルーズだし……。 — That guy is sloppy beyond words — he's always losing things, and he's never on time...

grammar.meaning: "It wouldn't be an exaggeration to say X" — asserts a strong claim while framing it as reasonable rather than hyperbolic.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形（動詞／い形容詞／な形容詞＋だ／名詞＋だ）+ と言っても過言ではない
grammar.example: このワインは世界一だといっても過言ではないでしょう。 (It wouldn't be an exaggeration to say this wine is the best in the world.)
grammar.file: grammar-といっても過言ではない.md

grammar.meaning: "Without distinguishing between X and Y, the situation is the same everywhere / all the time" — emphasizes that something applies indiscriminately across the board, often describing a messy state or a constant occurrence.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + といわず
grammar.example: 砂浜で遊んでいた子供たちは、手といわず足といわず全身砂だらけだ。 — The children who'd been playing on the beach were covered in sand from head to toe — hands, feet, everywhere.
grammar.file: grammar-といわず…といわず.md

grammar.meaning: "Whether it's X or Y" / "both X and Y alike" — indicates that a described state or action applies equally and indiscriminately across two (often representative, body-part or location) examples, implying it actually applies everywhere.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞A + といわず、名詞B + といわず
grammar.example: けんかした子供は手といわず足といわず、引っかき傷だらけだった。 — The child who'd been in a fight was covered in scratches — hands, feet, everywhere alike.
grammar.file: grammar-といわず〜といわず.md

grammar.meaning: "Combined with X (producing an enhanced effect)" — describes two or more factors interacting together to produce a combined, often amplified, result.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + と相まって
grammar.example: 原油高と円安が相まって、物価はさらに上昇した。 (Combined with the yen's depreciation, high crude oil prices pushed consumer prices up even further.)

grammar.meaning: "Speaking of X (in such an extreme/bad case)" — introduces an extreme or exasperating example as the final straw in a list of complaints, often leading to a dramatic conclusion.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／普通形 + ときた日には
grammar.example: 家事は全然だめ、趣味はパチンコ、その上性格も悪いときた日には、姉さんは当分嫁に行けないね。 (Hopeless at housework, pachinko for a hobby, and on top of that a bad personality — with a guy like that, my sister won't be getting married anytime soon.)

grammar.meaning: "Speaking of X..." — introduces a topic to make a critical or exasperated remark about it (occasionally also to praise it as the best example), setting up a judgment that follows.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + ときたら
grammar.example: うちの子ときたら、全然勉強しようとしない。 (Speaking of my kid, he just won't study at all.)

grammar.meaning: "Just as X was happening," "right when X" — describes an ongoing situation or moment that is interrupted or coincided with by another event (often unexpectedly).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ている／た形 + ところに／へ／を
grammar.example: お風呂に入ろうとしたところに、宅配便が届いた。 — Just as I was about to take a bath, a delivery arrived.

grammar.meaning: (1) "At a moment when X" — describing being seen/caught in a particular (often awkward or vulnerable) state. (2) An apologetic/polite concessive use: "even though it's X (busy, inconvenient, etc.)," often in set phrases of gratitude or apology.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ている形／名詞修飾 + ところを + 見られる／捕まる等 (caught/seen doing): 居眠りしているところを先生に見つかった。(I was caught by the teacher dozing off.)
grammar.example: 彼女は泣いているところを友達に見られてしまった。 — She was seen crying by her friend.

grammar.meaning: Is said/considered/held to be X — reporting an established definition, convention, or widely accepted rule.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形・な形・名詞の普通形 + とされている
grammar.example: このあたりの宗教では頭を触るのはタブーとされています。(In the religion practiced around here, touching someone's head is considered taboo.)

grammar.meaning: "X, of all people/things" — expresses surprise and mild self-reproach/criticism at an uncharacteristic mistake made by someone (often oneself) who is normally competent or careful.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun, typically a person or role) + としたことが
grammar.example: こんな初歩的なミスをするなんて、プロの君としたことが一体どうしたんだい？ — Making such a basic mistake — what on earth happened to you, of all people, a professional?

grammar.meaning: "If (we) assume X," "supposing that X" — introduces a hypothetical premise and considers its logical consequence; often used for hypothetical reasoning rather than real/likely conditions.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 + としたら／とすれば
grammar.example: もし生まれ変わるとしたら、何になりたいですか。 — If you were to be reborn, what would you want to become?
grammar.file: grammar-としたら・とすれば.md

grammar.meaning: "As X" — marks the capacity, role, position, qualification, or category in which something acts or is treated. ～としては narrows this to "speaking as X / from X's standpoint," while ～としても adds a concessive nuance, "even as/even in the capacity of X."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + として(は)/(も)
grammar.example: 彼は医者として、多くの患者を救ってきた。 — As a doctor, he has saved many patients.

grammar.meaning: "Even if ~ / even though ~" — a firm, literary concessive expression indicating that even given a certain condition or excuse, the expected outcome still won't follow. Carries a somewhat old-fashioned, dramatic nuance.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形/普通形 (verb past/plain form) + とて
grammar.example: 今さら謝ったとて、許してもらえないだろう。 — Even if you apologize now, you probably won't be forgiven.

grammar.meaning: "Together with X" (accompaniment) or "As X happens, Y also happens" (simultaneous change/proportional co-occurrence).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + とともに — 家族とともに (together with family)
grammar.example: 彼は家族とともに新しい町へ引っ越した。 — He moved to a new town together with his family.

grammar.meaning: When it comes to X / if it's truly the case that X, then... — draws a serious conclusion or implication from a hypothetical or newly-revealed situation.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形・な形・名詞の普通形 + となると
grammar.example: 銀行に融資を断られたとなると、この会社もそろそろ危ないな。(If it's really come to the point where the bank has refused to lend to them, this company must be in trouble soon.)

grammar.meaning: "To think that X! / How surprising/shocking that X" — expresses strong surprise, disbelief, or emotional reaction to a fact just stated or learned, often left trailing without a main clause.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 + とは（＋驚いた／思わなかった、often omitted）
grammar.example: まさか彼が優勝するとは、誰も予想していなかった。 (No one had predicted that he, of all people, would win the championship.)

grammar.meaning: Expresses the speaker's strong surprise, admiration, or exasperation at a fact just stated — "to think that ~," "what a ~."
grammar.conjugation: 普通形（ナ形(だ)・名(だ)） + とは
grammar.example: 鳥の足が2本であることさえ知らない子供がいるとは驚きだ。 — It's astonishing that there are children who don't even know birds have two legs.

grammar.meaning: "Having said that / even so" — acknowledges a preceding fact or statement, then introduces a qualification or contrast showing the situation isn't as simple/complete as that statement implies.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形容詞・な形容詞・名詞 の普通形 + とはいえ(ども)
grammar.example: 春(だ)とはいえ、まだ寒い日もある。 — Even though it's spring, there are still some cold days.

grammar.meaning: "Completely different from X (as before)" — describes a sudden, striking contrast between a current state and a previous one.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + とは打って変わって
grammar.example: きのうの大雨とはうってかわって、きょうは快晴になりましたね。 (In complete contrast to yesterday's heavy rain, today turned out to be gloriously clear.)

grammar.meaning: "As if to say '~'" — describes someone's attitude or action that silently but clearly conveys an unspoken thought or message, without them actually saying it out loud.
grammar.conjugation: 発話文（「 」がつくこともある） ＋ とばかり(に)
grammar.example: ケーキを買って帰ったら、「待ってました」とばかり、みんながテーブルに集まった。 — When I brought the cake home, everyone gathered at the table as if to say, "We've been waiting for this!"

grammar.meaning: As if to say X / as though implying X — describes an unspoken attitude or thought conveyed through someone's action or expression (a quasi-quotation of an implicit feeling).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞普通形／命令形 + とばかり(に)
grammar.example: 彼女は何も聞きたくないとばかりに、ぷいと横を向いた。(As if to say she didn't want to hear anything, she abruptly turned away.)

grammar.meaning: "It's not necessarily the case that ~ / not always true that ~" — used to soften a generalization, acknowledging exceptions to an otherwise commonly held belief.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form) + とは限らない — 例: 高いとは限らない (it's not necessarily expensive)
grammar.example: 高い物がいつも質がいいとは限らない。 — Expensive things aren't always high quality.

grammar.meaning: "In exchange for X" — describes a transactional or reciprocal relationship where one thing is given/received/sacrificed in return for another.
grammar.conjugation: [Verb/い形容詞/な形容詞 の名詞修飾形] + の + とひきかえに
grammar.example: 犯人は誘拐した子どもとひきかえに身代金一億円を親に要求した。 — The kidnapper demanded a 100-million-yen ransom from the parents in exchange for the kidnapped child.

grammar.meaning: Is regarded/viewed as X — a passive construction reporting a general analytical or predictive consensus view, often used in news reporting.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形・な形・名詞の普通形 + とみられている
grammar.example: 今後韓国語を学ぶ日本人の数は増加するとみられている。(The number of Japanese people learning Korean is expected to increase going forward.)

grammar.meaning: Expresses surprise, criticism, or disbelief that a person of such fine ability, reputation, or responsible position would do something so unbefitting of that status — or, conversely, expresses a wish that such a person behave in a manner that matches their standing.
grammar.conjugation: 名 + ともあろう + 名
grammar.example: 国会議員ともあろう人が、差別的な発言をするなんて信じられない。 — I can't believe that someone who is supposed to be a member of the Diet would make a discriminatory remark.

grammar.meaning: "Someone/something of such standing as X (should not have done this)" — expresses strong criticism directed at a subject with high status, reputation, or responsibility, for behaving in a way unbefitting that status.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun denoting a status/role/organization) + ともあろう + 名詞（者／人／会社など）+ が
grammar.example: 母親ともあろう者が赤ん坊の世話も忘れてパチンコに夢中になるなんて、信じられない。 — That someone who is supposed to be a mother would forget to care for her baby and get absorbed in pachinko instead is unbelievable.

grammar.meaning: "Without particularly meaning/intending to ~" — describes an action done unconsciously, vaguely, or without clear purpose or awareness. Often used with verbs of perception (見る, 聞く, 待つ) to mean one did something absent-mindedly.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 (verb dictionary form) + ともなく／ともなしに
grammar.example: 見るともなく窓の外を見ていたら、彼が歩いているのが見えた。 — Looking out the window without particularly meaning to, I saw him walking by.
grammar.file: grammar-ともなく・ともなしに.md

grammar.meaning: "Once it reaches the stage/level of X, (then naturally...)" — expresses that once a situation reaches a certain significant status, age, scale, or role, a corresponding natural consequence follows.
grammar.conjugation: [動-辞書形][名] + ともなると
grammar.example: 社会人ともなれば、自分の言葉に責任を持つべきだ。 — Once you're a working member of society, you should take responsibility for your own words.
grammar.file: grammar-ともなると・ともなれば.md

grammar.meaning: "Anyway, in the end, no matter what" — expresses a resigned, defeatist attitude that the outcome will be the same regardless of effort, implying it's pointless to try to change it.
grammar.conjugation: どうせ + [clause], often paired with a negative, futile, or inevitable conclusion
grammar.example: どうせ告白しても振られるから、言わないでおく。 — I'll get rejected anyway even if I confess my feelings, so I won't say anything.

grammar.meaning: "Far from X," "let alone X" — strongly denies a modest premise and asserts a much more extreme (often opposite) reality, emphasizing the gap between expectation and truth.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／普通形 + どころか + (contrasting/extreme statement)
grammar.example: 彼はお礼を言うどころか、謝りもしなかった。 — Far from saying thank you, he didn't even apologize.

grammar.meaning: "It's not the time/situation for X," "far from being able to do X" — expresses that circumstances make a certain action impossible or inappropriate, usually due to a more pressing concern.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／名詞 + どころではない
grammar.example: 締め切りが近くて、休むどころではない。 — The deadline is close — this isn't the time to be resting.

grammar.meaning: "Thought/expected X, but actually Y" — expresses a reversal of expectation: the speaker (or a general assumption) anticipated one outcome, but reality turned out differently.
grammar.conjugation: [動・い形・な形・名] の普通形 + とおもいきや
grammar.example: 1級レベルの漢字テストだから難しいと思いきや、案外簡単でよかった。 — I thought the kanji test would be hard since it's N1 level, but it turned out to be surprisingly easy.

grammar.meaning: Combined with ~, interacting together with ~, resulting in an intensified effect or synergy — "coupled with ~," "together with ~."
grammar.conjugation: 元の動詞：相俟つ（あいまつ、現代では使わない古語）
grammar.example: あの白い建物は美しい緑と相まって、絵本に出てくるお城のように見える。 — That white building, combined with the beautiful greenery around it, looks like a castle out of a picture book.

grammar.meaning: It seems/appears that X — an inference drawn from visible evidence or circumstances.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形・な形・名詞の普通形 + とみえて
grammar.example: 隣のうちは留守と見えて、先週からずっとカーテンが閉まったままだ。(The house next door seems to be empty — the curtains have been closed ever since last week.)

grammar.meaning: "Unless/without first doing X, (Y cannot happen)" — expresses that a negative condition must be resolved before the main clause can be realized; the main clause is usually negative too.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ない形 + ことには — 練習しないことには (unless one practices)
grammar.example: 実際に食べてみないことには、味はわからない。 — Unless you actually try eating it, you can't know the taste.

grammar.meaning: "It's not that X doesn't happen" / "It's not like X isn't possible" — a double-negative construction that produces a soft, hedged affirmation ("I suppose it's possible," "there's some chance of X").
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ない形 + ことは(も)ない — 行かないことはない (it's not that I won't go / I could go)
grammar.example: 忙しいが、手伝えないことはない。 — I'm busy, but it's not that I can't help — I could.

grammar.pattern: ～ないではすまない・～ずにはすまない
grammar.meaning: Given the circumstances or social/moral norms, it's unthinkable not to do ~, or one cannot get away without doing ~. ～ずにはすまない is the more formal/literary variant.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ない形 + ではすまない
grammar.example: 人の心を傷つけてしまったなら、謝らないではすまない。 — If you've hurt someone's feelings, you can't get away without apologizing.
grammar.file: grammar-ないではすまない・ずにはすまない.md

grammar.pattern: ～ないでは／ずにはいられない
grammar.meaning: "Cannot help but do X / cannot resist doing X" — expresses that the speaker's emotions or natural impulses make it impossible to refrain from a certain action, often involuntary emotional/physical reactions.
grammar.conjugation: Verb (ない form) + ではいられない
grammar.example: その話を聞いて、笑わずにはいられなかった。 — Hearing that story, I couldn't help but laugh.
grammar.file: grammar-ないでは・ずにはいられない.md

grammar.meaning: "It's not necessarily true that X won't happen / X might possibly happen" — a cautious double-negative hedge acknowledging a low but nonzero possibility, often used to justify precaution.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ない形 + とも限らない
grammar.example: 将来重い病気にならないとも限らないから、保険に加入しようと考えている。 (You never know — I might end up with a serious illness someday, so I'm thinking of getting insurance.)
grammar.file: grammar-ないともかぎらない.md

grammar.meaning: "Although not going so far as to ~, at least ~" — acknowledges that a higher-level action/standard isn't being met, but asserts that a lesser, more minimal version of it should still be done.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ない形 (verb negative form) + までも
grammar.example: 結婚式には出席できないまでも、お祝いぐらいは贈るものだよ。 — Even if you can't attend the wedding, you should at least send a gift.

grammar.meaning: "Isn't there some way to...? / If only there were a way to..." — a rhetorical, wishful question expressing the speaker's strong desire for a solution or better outcome, often implying frustration that none is currently apparent.
grammar.conjugation: Verb-ない形 + ものか
grammar.example: この問題をなんとか解決できないものか、ずっと考えている。 — I keep wondering if there isn't some way to solve this problem.

grammar.meaning: "Unless ~ / as long as ~ not" — states that a result will not occur unless a particular negative condition changes; the negative mirror of ～限り(は).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ない形 + 限り — 例: 謝らない限り (unless you apologize)
grammar.example: 彼が謝らない限り、私は許すつもりはない。 — Unless he apologizes, I don't intend to forgive him.

grammar.meaning: (1) "While doing X" — two actions performed simultaneously by the same subject. (2) "Although/even though X" (concessive, often ながらも) — expresses a contrast between a state and an unexpected outcome.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形(stem) + ながら: 音楽を聞きながら勉強する (study while listening to music)
grammar.example: テレビを見ながら、晩ご飯を食べた。 — I ate dinner while watching TV.

grammar.meaning: "While remaining in the state of ~" / "Just as ~ is, without change" — describes a state that stays exactly as it is while some action or situation takes place, often highlighting that something happens without needing to leave or change that state.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形／名詞 ＋ ながらに(して)
grammar.example: この子は生まれながらに優れた音感を持っていた。 — This child was born with an excellent sense of pitch.

grammar.meaning: "While/as still being in the state of X" — describes doing something in, or possessing something from, an unchanged original state (e.g., "since birth," "with tears still in one's eyes"). In some uses it can also shift to a concessive sense equivalent to けれども ("although").
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + ながらに／ながらの + 名詞 (common fixed expressions: 生まれながらに, 涙ながらに, 昔ながらの)
grammar.example: 彼の音感は生まれながらに備わった才能だ。 (His sense of pitch is a talent he was born with.)

grammar.meaning: "Although X, nonetheless Y" — a concessive connector acknowledging one state or action while the main clause presents a contrasting or unexpected outcome.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形／い形容詞／な形容詞語幹 + ながらも
grammar.example: 体に悪いとわかっていながらも、たばこをやめられない。 (Even though I know it's bad for my health, I can't quit smoking.)

grammar.meaning: "Without X, (Y would not be possible / Y cannot happen)" — a formal way of saying that something is an indispensable precondition for something else, almost always paired with a negative-potential predicate at the end (～ことはできない, ～ない, etc.).
grammar.conjugation: [Noun] + なくして(は) + ～ない/～ことはできない
grammar.example: 愛なくして結婚生活を続けることはできないよ。 — Without love, you can't keep a marriage going.

grammar.meaning: "Without doing/having X" — describes performing an action without a preceding step or accompanying element; the ～なしには～ない variant emphasizes that without X, the stated outcome is difficult or impossible.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + なしに（＋動詞）
grammar.example: 事前の連絡なしに訪問するのは失礼だ。 (Visiting without prior contact is rude.)

grammar.meaning: "Because, the reason is..." — a formal conjunction that introduces the explicit reason or justification for the statement just made, typically completed with 〜からだ or 〜のだ at the end of the following sentence.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the explanatory sentence that follows. Unlike pure cause-conjunctions, なぜなら requires its own sentence to end in からだ/のだ (or ためだ) to grammatically "close the loop," so it functions as a paired construction (なぜなら〜からだ) rather than a conjunction used alone mid-sentence.
grammar.example: 私はこの政策に反対だ。なぜなら、長期的には財政を圧迫するからだ。 — I am against this policy. Because it will strain public finances in the long run.

grammar.meaning: "Things like X, and so on" — used for non-exhaustive listing or vague reference. なんて and なんか additionally express disdain, surprise, or self-deprecating modesty ("X of all things," "something like X [which is unimpressive]").
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + など／なんか + (particle): 果物など好きです (I like things like fruit)
grammar.example: 休日は読書や映画鑑賞など楽しんでいます。 — On days off, I enjoy things like reading and watching movies.
grammar.file: grammar-など・なんて・なんか.md

grammar.meaning: "On par with/equivalent to X" — expresses that something matches the standard, level, or quality of X, often used to describe something reaching an average or typical standard.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + なみ
grammar.example: せめて世間並みの生活ができれば充分だと思っています。 — I think it would be enough if we could just live an average, ordinary life.

grammar.meaning: "That may be one thing, but..." — sets up a contrast where the first-mentioned case (often a past or hypothetical situation) is conceded as possibly true/acceptable, but the actual present/real case is different and treated more seriously or critically.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + はいざ知らず／ならいざ知らず
grammar.example: 昔はいざ知らず、彼は今やCD売上№1の大スターなんだから、簡単には会えませんよ。 — In the past, maybe, but he's now the top-selling CD superstar, so you can't easily meet him anymore.

grammar.meaning: "Uniquely attributable to X, only possible because of X" — praises X as the special reason something excellent or distinctive is possible; emphasizes exclusivity in a positive, complimentary sense.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + ならでは (～ない) — used predicatively, often with an implied or explicit negative ("not possible without X")
grammar.example: その土地ならではの料理を食べるのは、旅の楽しみの一つですね。 — Eating food that's unique to that region is one of the joys of travel.

grammar.meaning: "If it were just X, that would be bearable/acceptable, but (Y, the actual case, is not)" — sets a threshold of tolerance at X and indicates the real situation (Y) exceeds or fails to meet it, triggering complaint or disapproval.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + はまだしも／ならまだしも
grammar.example: 平日はまだしも、忙しい週末にアルバイトに休まれると、困るんだが。 — If it were a weekday, that'd be one thing, but having my part-timer take the day off during a busy weekend is a real problem.

grammar.meaning: The instant X happens, Y happens immediately afterward (a sudden, immediate next action).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + なり
grammar.example: 校長先生はスピーチをしようとマイクを持つなり、倒れてしまった。(The principal collapsed the instant he picked up the microphone to give his speech.)

grammar.meaning: Suggests doing one thing or another (or anything else of the kind), presenting two or more examples as acceptable, interchangeable options without pinning down which one — "whether it's X or Y, just do something."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞(+助詞)・動詞辞書形 + なり
grammar.example: 昼休みは40分しかないんだから、おにぎりなりサンドイッチなり何か買って早く食べたほうがいい。 — We only have 40 minutes for lunch, so you'd better buy something — a rice ball, a sandwich, whatever — and eat quickly.

grammar.meaning: Either X or Y — whichever one chooses; a non-exhaustive, illustrative listing of options/alternatives.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + なり、動詞辞書形 + なり (also usable with nouns: 名詞 + なり、名詞 + なり)
grammar.example: 分からないときは、先生に聞くなり、辞書を引くなりしてください。(When you don't understand something, either ask the teacher or look it up in a dictionary.)

grammar.meaning: "In one's own way, given one's ability/situation" — describes doing something to the best of one's own capacity, acknowledging limitations while still making an earnest effort.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／代名詞 + なりに（＋動詞）
grammar.example: 子どもなりに一生懸命考えて答えを出した。 (The child thought hard in his own way and came up with an answer.)

grammar.meaning: "Really/thoroughly ~ed" — an emphatic construction where the same verb's ます-stem is repeated with に before the past-tense form, intensifying the meaning (e.g., 待ちに待った = "waited and waited," i.e., long-awaited).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb ます-stem) + に + 同じ動詞のた形 (same verb's た-form)
grammar.example: 待ちに待った帰国の日がついにやってきた。 — The long-awaited day of returning home finally arrived.

grammar.meaning: "A combination of A and B" — uses に to link two nouns that naturally go together as a set or pairing, often describing a meal, outfit, or typical combination of items.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞A (noun A) + に + 名詞B (noun B)
grammar.example: 朝食はいつもパンにコーヒーです。 — Breakfast is always bread with coffee.

grammar.meaning: "Want to do X, but can't" — expresses that although the speaker wants to do something, some circumstance (psychological or physical) makes it impossible.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + に + 可能動詞の否定形
grammar.example: 野菜をたくさんもらったが、食べきれない。捨てるに捨てられず困っている。 — I was given so many vegetables I can't eat them all. I want to throw them out, but I just can't bring myself to — it's a real dilemma.
grammar.file: grammar-に-ない・(よ)うにも-ない.md

grammar.meaning: "At the time of," "on the occasion of," "in undertaking X" — marks a significant, often formal, event or juncture as the moment for the following action (commonly used for beginnings, important tasks, or ceremonies).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にあたり／にあたって
grammar.example: 新しいプロジェクトを始めるにあたり、皆様のご協力をお願いいたします。 — As we begin this new project, I ask for everyone's cooperation.

grammar.meaning: In the midst of / under the circumstances of X — typically an unusual, difficult, or noteworthy situation.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にあって
grammar.example: 水も食糧も不足した状況にあって、もっとも大事なのはお互いに助け合うことだ。(In the midst of a situation where both water and food are scarce, the most important thing is to help one another.)

grammar.pattern: ～にいたっても／にいたるまで
grammar.meaning: にいたっても: even reaching the extreme point of X (still the outcome is surprising/unchanged); にいたるまで: all the way up to and including X (emphasizing the full extent of a range).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／名詞 + に至る(って／るまで)
grammar.example: 妻が離婚を決意するに至って初めて夫は自分の非に気がついた。(It was only when his wife reached the point of deciding on divorce that the husband finally realized his own fault.)
grammar.file: grammar-にいたっても・にいたるまで.md

grammar.meaning: "In X's view / if you ask X" — introduces a personal opinion or perspective, often one that contrasts with a more common or expected view.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に言わせれば
grammar.example: この店の料理はすばらしいと言われているけど、私に言わせればこれぐらい家庭でも作れますよ。 (This restaurant's food is said to be wonderful, but if you ask me, you could make something like this at home.)

grammar.meaning: "In," "at," "regarding" — a formal marker for location, time, field, or domain, used in place of で/に in formal or written contexts. における is the attributive (pre-noun) form.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + において (adverbial): 現代社会において (in contemporary society)
grammar.example: 現代社会において、インターネットは欠かせない存在だ。 — In contemporary society, the internet is an indispensable presence.

grammar.meaning: An ultra-formal honorific topic marker used to respectfully refer to a superior, client, or esteemed party as the topic of a letter, speech, or greeting — roughly "as for [esteemed person/entity]..."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞（人・組織など） (noun referring to a person or organization, usually one the speaker respects/is subordinate to) + におかれましては
grammar.example: 貴社におかれましては、益々ご清栄のこととお慶び申し上げます。 — We are delighted to hear that your company continues to prosper.

grammar.meaning: "N in/at X" — marks a domain, location, time, or field within which a following noun is being discussed; functions as a formal attributive version of "in X."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + における + 名詞 (noun + における + noun)
grammar.example: 個人情報をいかに守るかは情報通信社会における重要な課題だ。 (How to protect personal information is an important issue in the information and communication society.)

grammar.meaning: "When it comes to X('s hands/skill/power)" — expresses that once something falls under the influence, skill, or control of X, a particular (often surprising, impressive, or ironic) outcome inevitably follows.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun, typically a person or their "hands"/skill) + にかかっては
grammar.example: 泥棒の手にかかってはこんな鍵、簡単に開けられてしまうでしょうね。 — In the hands of a thief, a lock like this would surely be opened easily.

grammar.pattern: ～にかかわらず／にもかかわらず
grammar.meaning: にかかわらず = "regardless of X" (X being a range/choice, often paired items like 有無/晴雨); にもかかわらず = "despite X," "in spite of X" (expressing an unexpected or contrary result given the preceding fact).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／疑問詞＋か＋どうか + にかかわらず: 天気にかかわらず (regardless of the weather); 参加するかどうかにかかわらず (regardless of whether you participate)
grammar.example: 年齢にかかわらず、誰でも応募できます。 — Regardless of age, anyone can apply.
grammar.file: grammar-にかかわらず・にもかかわらず.md

grammar.meaning: "Affects/concerns X (often seriously, a matter of X)" — describes something that has a significant bearing on a serious matter, often implying high stakes (life, honor, safety, credibility).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に関わる + 名詞／動詞
grammar.example: これは会社の信用に関わる重大な問題だ。 (This is a serious matter that affects the company's credibility.)

grammar.meaning: "It's not limited to X / this isn't unique to X" — points out that a phenomenon described applies more broadly, not just to the specific case just mentioned.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に限ったことではない
grammar.example: 若者のマナーが悪くなりつつあるのはこの国に限ったことではない。 (The decline in young people's manners isn't limited to this country.)
grammar.file: grammar-にかぎったことではない.md

grammar.meaning: Two related usages: (1) ～にかけては — "when it comes to X / concerning X (a skill or ability)," expressing excellence in a particular area; (2) ～から～にかけて — "from X to Y," marking an approximate (not precise) range of time or place.
grammar.conjugation: Usage 1: 名詞 + にかけては + 評価の表現（praise/evaluation predicate）
grammar.example: 料理の腕にかけては、彼女に勝てる人はいない。 — When it comes to cooking skill, no one can beat her.

grammar.meaning: "When it comes to X (one's area of skill/forte)" — praises someone's particular expertise or strength. The も variant means "even in terms of X" (adding another area where a quality holds, often negatively: "even in X, he's no good").
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にかけては — 料理にかけては (when it comes to cooking)
grammar.example: 彼は絵を描くことにかけては、クラスで一番だ。 — When it comes to drawing, he's the best in the class.

grammar.meaning: "Using X as an excuse/pretext" — describes doing something by exploiting an unrelated or loosely related circumstance as a convenient justification.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にかこつけて
grammar.example: 大学院進学に託けて今の会社を辞めてしまった。 (Using graduate school as a pretext, he quit his current job.)

grammar.meaning: "Being preoccupied with X (and neglecting other things)" — describes focusing so much on one task or matter that other responsibilities, often people, are neglected.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にかまけて
grammar.example: 夫は仕事にかまけて、子どもと遊んでやろうとしない。 (My husband is so preoccupied with work that he won't play with the children.)

grammar.meaning: "In place of X / on behalf of X" — indicates that someone/something takes over a role, action, or position previously held by another.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にかわって — 社長にかわって (in place of the president)
grammar.example: 入院中の社長にかわって、副社長が挨拶をした。 — In place of the hospitalized president, the vice president gave the greeting.

grammar.meaning: "It's best to X / nothing beats X" — recommends a particular choice as clearly the best or safest option, though not strictly mandatory.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形（動詞／い形容詞／な形容詞＋である／名詞＋である）+ に越したことはない
grammar.example: 体は丈夫であるに越したことはありません。 (There's nothing better than having a strong, healthy body.)

grammar.meaning: Two main uses: (1) "In accordance with X / following X (a rule, instruction)," and (2) "As X happens, Y proportionally happens too" — a gradual, correlated change.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に従って — 規則に従って (in accordance with the rules)
grammar.example: 係員の指示に従って、避難してください。 — Please evacuate in accordance with the staff's instructions.

grammar.meaning: "Even in the case of X / even granting X, [it would still be powerless/meaningless/no different]" — concedes that even the person or thing in question, who might seem like an exception, is ultimately no different or no more capable than anyone else.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にしたところで
grammar.example: 厳しい批判をしてしまったが、わたしにしたところでいい案を持っているわけではない。 — I was harsh in my criticism, but it's not as if I myself have a good solution either.

grammar.meaning: "From the standpoint of X / if it were X('s perspective)" — presents a situation as it would appear from a particular person's point of view, often used to show empathy or explain why someone might feel a certain way.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (person) + にしたら — 親にしたら (from a parent's standpoint)
grammar.example: 親にしたら、子供がいくつになっても心配なものだ。 — From a parent's standpoint, they worry about their children no matter how old they get.

grammar.pattern: ～にして（評価・事の起こり方）
grammar.meaning: States an evaluation of how a situation turned out, or describes the manner/speed in which an event occurred — e.g. 幸いにして "fortunately" (evaluates the outcome as lucky) and 一瞬にして "in an instant" (describes how quickly something happened). This is a distinct, more adverbial sense of ～にして from the "even as X" / "only at the stage of X" concessive usage covered elsewhere (see Lesson 17-④).
grammar.conjugation: Attaches to a limited set of fixed words/expressions as a set adverbial phrase (the textbook gives no general connection rule — treat each item as idiomatic).
grammar.example: 幸いにして、体調はすぐに回復した。 — Fortunately, his health recovered quickly.

grammar.meaning: Indicates that something matches (or fails to match) a high level, special stage, or exceptional condition described by the preceding noun — often translated as "even at/for X" or "only at the stage of X."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にして
grammar.example: 結婚してすぐに子供が欲しかったが、8年目にしてようやく授かった。 — We wanted a child right after marrying, but it was only in our 8th year that we were finally blessed with one.

grammar.meaning: "For X, (surprisingly)..." — expresses that the following statement is unexpected or inconsistent given what one would normally assume about X; implies a mild contrast or surprise.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にしては — 初心者にしては (for a beginner, [surprisingly well])
grammar.example: 彼は初心者にしては、とても上手にピアノを弾く。 — For a beginner, he plays the piano very well.

grammar.meaning: "Only at/as X (did something become true) / even as X / precisely because of being at the stage/status of X" — marks a specific point, status, age, or stage as the decisive condition under which something becomes true, often emphasizing that it took that long or that level to achieve.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にして（＋初めて）
grammar.example: 彼は五十歳にして初めて自分の本当にやりたいことに気づいた。 (Only at fifty did he first realize what he truly wanted to do.)

grammar.meaning: "Can't bring myself to X / can't bear to X" — expresses emotional reluctance to do something, usually because of attachment or sympathy, even though it may be rational or necessary.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + に忍びない
grammar.example: これは汚れているけれど思い出の物だから、捨てるに忍びないなあ。 (It's dirty, but it's something full of memories, so I can't bring myself to throw it away.)

grammar.meaning: "Even if / whether it be X..." — a concessive construction, often paired to list contrasting alternatives ("whether A or B, [Y is still true]"), or used singly to mean "granting X, nevertheless..."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞/普通形 + にしろ・にしても・にせよ — 行くにしろ行かないにしろ (whether you go or not)
grammar.example: 行くにしろ行かないにしろ、早く返事をしてほしい。 — Whether you go or not, I'd like a quick answer.
grammar.file: grammar-にしろ・にしても・にせよ.md

grammar.meaning: "Merely/nothing more than X" — downplays something as being only to a limited extent, often used to minimize significance or correct an overestimation.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にすぎない — 噂にすぎない (it's nothing more than a rumor)
grammar.example: これはほんの一例にすぎない。 — This is merely one example among many.

grammar.meaning: "Based on/in line with X" — describes acting, judging, or explaining in close conformity with a particular standard, reality, or set of facts, rather than abstractly or ideally.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に即して
grammar.example: 現実に即した対策を立てる必要がある。 (We need to formulate countermeasures grounded in reality.)

grammar.meaning: 堪える = "worth/able to bear/endure (watching, listening, reading, etc.)" — of sufficient quality to be worth experiencing. 堪えない = "cannot bear to (watch/listen)" — either because the quality is too poor, or because the content is too emotionally moving to endure.
grammar.conjugation: V辞書形/N + に堪える (鑑賞に堪える作品 — "a work worth viewing")
grammar.example: あの人の話は下品で聞くにたえない。 — That person's talk is so vulgar it's unbearable to listen to.
grammar.file: grammar-にたえる・にたえない.md

grammar.meaning: "Worthy/deserving of X" (に足るN) or "not worth X / unworthy of X" (に足りない) — evaluates whether something or someone meets the standard required to merit a particular description or treatment.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／名詞 + に足る + 名詞
grammar.example: 彼は信頼に足る人物だと、みんなが認めている。 (Everyone acknowledges that he is a person worthy of trust.)

grammar.meaning: "About / regarding / concerning X" — marks the topic being discussed, written about, or asked about. に関して is more formal/written and often used for broader or more serious topics; について is the general-purpose everyday equivalent.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + について — 日本の歴史について (about Japanese history)
grammar.example: 来週の会議では、新製品の価格について話し合います。 — At next week's meeting, we will discuss the pricing of the new product.

grammar.meaning: "Whenever / every time X happens" — marks a recurring trigger (often sensory or situational) that reliably brings about a certain thought or feeling; frequently doubled as 何かにつけ or Xにつけ、Yにつけ ("whether X or Y...").
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + につけ (例: この曲を聞くにつけ)
grammar.example: この写真を見るにつけ、昔の思い出が蘇る。 — Every time I see this photo, old memories come back to me.

grammar.meaning: "As X, Y (gradually)..." — describes two changes that progress in parallel, where one change accompanies or is caused by the other, both unfolding gradually over time.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 (change/progress verb) + につれて (例: 年を取るにつれて)
grammar.example: 年を取るにつれて、体力が衰えていく。 — As one gets older, physical strength gradually declines.

grammar.meaning: "Compared against/checked against X (a standard)" — evaluates or judges something by measuring it against an established standard, rule, or precedent.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に照らして
grammar.example: 常識に照らして考えれば、いいことかどうかぐらいわかるだろう。 (If you think about it in light of common sense, you should be able to tell whether it's good or not.)

grammar.meaning: "For X / from X's standpoint" — evaluates a situation, object, or event from the perspective of a particular person or entity, usually followed by a judgment (good/bad/important/difficult, etc.).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (person/entity) + にとって (例: 私にとって、学生にとって、日本にとって)
grammar.example: この試験は私にとって非常に重要だ。 — This exam is extremely important to me.

grammar.meaning: "Not limited to X (but extends further to Y)" — indicates that the scope or impact of something exceeds a stated boundary.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にとどまらず
grammar.example: ウイルス感染の被害は国内のみにとどまらず、海外にも広がっていった。 (The damage from the viral infection wasn't limited to within the country — it spread overseas as well.)

grammar.meaning: "Accompanying X / as a result of X" — indicates that one change or event occurs together with, or as a consequence of, another change, often on a larger/societal scale.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (change-implying noun) + に伴って (例: 人口の増加に伴って)
grammar.example: 人口の増加に伴って、住宅不足が深刻化している。 — As the population increases, the housing shortage is becoming more serious.

grammar.meaning: In accordance with / based on (rules, precedent, tradition, or an established spirit/code).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にのっとって
grammar.example: 我々はスポーツマン精神にのっとって、正々堂々と戦うことを誓います。(We vow to fight fair and square, in accordance with the spirit of sportsmanship.)

grammar.meaning: "It doesn't amount to/warrant X" — used to downplay a reaction (surprise, praise, blame, criticism) as unwarranted or excessive given the circumstances.
grammar.conjugation: V辞書形/N + には当たらない (commonly with 驚く, 批判する, 称賛する, 感心する, etc.)
grammar.example: 彼女が試験に合格したからといって驚くには当たらない。 — Just because she passed the exam doesn't mean it warrants being surprised — she always studied hard.

grammar.meaning: "There's no need to X / it's not necessary to go that far" — politely tells someone that an action, often one done out of courtesy, isn't necessary.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + には及ばない
grammar.example: 大丈夫です。すぐ近くですから、送っていただくには及びません。 (It's fine. It's very close by, so there's no need for you to walk me there.)

grammar.meaning: Says that something isn't serious or significant enough to warrant a strong emotional reaction or evaluation — "there's no need to X" / "it doesn't warrant X-ing," used to restrain an excessive response like surprise, pessimism, or blame.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／名詞する + には当たらない
grammar.example: 山田さんは通勤に1時間半かかるそうだが、驚くには当たらない。これは日本では珍しくない。 — I hear Yamada-san's commute takes an hour and a half, but there's no need to be surprised — that's not unusual in Japan.

grammar.meaning: "In contrast to X" — highlights a stark contrast between two things, often with an implicit value judgment (one is better/worse, more/less than the other).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形容詞・な形容詞 の名詞修飾型 + の + にひきかえ (i.e., the noun-modifying form of verbs/adjectives + の + にひきかえ)
grammar.example: シンガポールではサッカーにひきかえ、野球の人気は今ひとつだ。 — In contrast to soccer in Singapore, baseball's popularity is lackluster.

grammar.meaning: "Is nothing other than X / is precisely X" — strongly asserts that something is exactly and only one thing, ruling out any other explanation; emphatic identification of the true cause or nature of something.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にほかならない (例: これは努力の結果にほかならない)
grammar.example: 彼が成功したのは、日々の努力の結果にほかならない。 — His success is nothing other than the result of his daily effort.

grammar.meaning: "Related to/associated with X (legend, rumor, story)" — attaches to a noun to describe a story, legend, rumor, or memory connected to it.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にまつわる + 名詞
grammar.example: 村の人々は白蛇池にまつわる伝説を信じていて、誰も近づかないそうだ。 (The villagers believe the legend associated with White Snake Pond, and apparently no one goes near it.)

grammar.meaning: "There's a limit to ~ / ~ is really going too far" — expresses strong criticism or exasperation that something (a behavior, statement, or quality) has far exceeded acceptable or reasonable limits.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + にもほどがある
grammar.example: 自分でやりたいと言ったのに、途中で仕事を投げ出すなんて、無責任にもほどがある。 — Even though you said you wanted to do it yourself, giving up halfway through — there's a limit to how irresponsible you can be!

grammar.meaning: "More than X / even more than X" — compares a current degree or state against a stated reference point, asserting it surpasses even that.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にも増して
grammar.example: 今年の夏はいつにも増して暑い。 (This summer is hotter than ever before.)
