grammar.meaning: "Depending on X (in some cases)" — highlights that, among various possible instances of X, certain specific ones may lead to a different or exceptional outcome; emphasizes variability/exceptions rather than a general rule.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + によっては (例: 場合によっては、人によっては、地域によっては)
grammar.example: 場合によっては、キャンセル料がかかることがあります。 — Depending on the situation, a cancellation fee may apply.

grammar.meaning: Multi-purpose formal connector with three main senses depending on context: (1) "by means of X" (method/agent, often passive-voice actor), (2) "due to X / because of X" (cause), (3) "depending on X / according to X" (varying basis).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + によって／により (例: 台風によって、専門家によって、場合によって)
grammar.example: この橋は江戸時代に建てられた職人たちによって作られた。 (agent/method) — This bridge was built by craftsmen during the Edo period.

grammar.meaning: "Over the course of X / spanning X" — indicates that an event, condition, or process continuously covers an extensive range of time, space, or scope.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (duration/range noun) + にわたって (例: 10年にわたって、全国にわたって、3回にわたって)
grammar.example: この工事は3年にわたって行われた。 — This construction project was carried out over the course of three years.

grammar.meaning: "Prior to X / in advance of X" — indicates that an action is carried out before a more important or larger event, often as preparation for it.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に先立って — 開会式に先立って (prior to the opening ceremony)
grammar.example: 試合に先立って、両チームの選手が挨拶を交わした。 — Prior to the match, players from both teams exchanged greetings.

grammar.meaning: To act by following a standard, norm, rule, law, or tradition as the governing basis — "in accordance with / following X."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に則って／に則った＋名詞 (base verb: 則る)
grammar.example: スポーツマンシップに則って試合をする。 — Play the match in accordance with sportsmanship.

grammar.meaning: "In addition to X" — adds a further element on top of something already mentioned, often intensifying or compounding a situation.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に加えて — 雨に加えて (in addition to the rain)
grammar.example: 大雨に加えて、強風も吹いていたため、電車が止まった。 — In addition to heavy rain, strong winds were also blowing, so the trains stopped.

grammar.meaning: "In accordance with / based on X" — to handle, judge, or plan something in a way that precisely matches or conforms to a given standard, rule, or actual real-world condition.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に即して／に即した＋名詞 (base verb: 即す)
grammar.example: 規定に即して出張費が出ます。 — Travel expenses are paid in accordance with the regulations.

grammar.meaning: "Contrary to X" — indicates that an actual outcome goes against or differs from an expectation, prediction, rule, or wish.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (expectation/rule-type noun) + に反して (例: 予想に反して、期待に反して、規則に反して)
grammar.example: 天気予報に反して、今日は朝から晴れている。 — Contrary to the weather forecast, it has been sunny since this morning.

grammar.meaning: "Based on X" — indicates that an action, decision, or creation is grounded in or derived from a particular source, such as data, law, experience, or a principle.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (source/basis noun) + に基づいて (例: データに基づいて、法律に基づいて、経験に基づいて)
grammar.example: この政策は、最新の調査データに基づいて作られた。 — This policy was created based on the latest survey data.

grammar.meaning: Attached to a limited set of emotion nouns, expresses that a feeling is so strong it cannot be suppressed — "cannot help but feel ~," "overwhelmed with ~." Formal register.
grammar.conjugation: 名 + に堪えない
grammar.example: お忙しいところを多くの方にお集まりいただき、感激に堪えません。 — I am overwhelmed with gratitude that so many of you have gathered here despite your busy schedules.

grammar.meaning: に堪える = good enough to withstand being ~ed, i.e., "worthy of ~ing" (e.g. worthy of being appreciated/discussed); に堪えない = in such a poor or terrible state that it cannot bear being ~ed — "not worth ~ing," "unbearable to ~."
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形・名詞する + に堪える／に堪えない
grammar.example: 優れた児童文学は、大人の鑑賞にも堪えるものだ。 — Excellent children's literature is good enough to withstand being appreciated by adults too.
grammar.file: grammar-に堪える・に堪えない.md

grammar.meaning: "Towards X / in regard to X / in contrast to X" — indicates the target or direction of an action, attitude, or feeling, or sets up a contrast between two things.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + に対して
grammar.example: 彼は後輩に対して、いつも優しく接している。 — He always treats his juniors kindly.

grammar.meaning: "I can't bring myself to do X" — describes an action that is so emotionally painful or distressing to the speaker that they cannot bear to carry it out, usually out of compassion, sentimentality, or attachment.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + に忍びない
grammar.example: 古い本はもう読まないとは思うが、処分するに忍びない。 — I don't think I'll ever read these old books again, but I can't bring myself to get rid of them.

grammar.meaning: "In response to X" — indicates an action taken to meet, fulfill, or answer an expectation, request, demand, or wish.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に応えて — 期待に応えて (in response to/meeting expectations)
grammar.example: 観客の声援に応えて、選手たちは全力でプレーした。 — In response to the crowd's cheers, the players gave their all.

grammar.meaning: "According to," "in response to," "depending on" — indicates that an action, amount, or treatment varies or is adjusted to match a given condition, situation, or request.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に応じて
grammar.example: 成績に応じて、クラスが分けられる。 — Classes are divided according to grades.

grammar.meaning: "Worthy of X / not shameful in light of X" — describes a person's conduct, work, or achievement as living up to a name, title, reputation, or standard without disgracing it.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に恥じない (+ 名詞)
grammar.example: 五つ星レストランの名に恥じない料理を出す。 — They serve food worthy of a five-star restaurant's name.

grammar.meaning: "Compared to X" — introduces a point of comparison, contrasting the following clause's state/degree against X.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に比べて — 去年に比べて (compared to last year)
grammar.example: 今年の夏は去年に比べて、かなり暑い。 — This summer is considerably hotter compared to last year.

grammar.meaning: "It's surely/definitely X" / "X is bound to be the case" — expresses the speaker's strong, confident conviction based on common sense or obvious reasoning, often used to dismiss doubt.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form, verb/adjective) + に決まっている — 彼が勝つに決まっている (he's bound to win)
grammar.example: そんな高い商品、売れるわけがない、失敗するに決まっている。 — Such an expensive product — there's no way it'll sell, it's bound to fail.

grammar.meaning: "Along X" (physical: a river, road) or "In line with X" (abstract: a plan, policy, guideline) — indicates following a course, direction, or set of guidelines without deviation.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に沿って — 川に沿って (along the river); 方針に沿って (in line with the policy)
grammar.example: この道は川に沿って続いている。 — This road continues along the river.

grammar.meaning: "In light of / judging from X" — to evaluate or judge a matter by comparing it against a standard such as law, rules, experience, or precedent.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に照らして／に照らした＋名詞 (base verb: 照らす)
grammar.example: 自分の経験に照らして後輩にアドバイスした。 — I gave advice to my junior, judging from my own experience.

grammar.meaning: "There is no doubt that X / X must certainly be the case" — a formal expression of strong logical certainty, close in meaning to に違いない but more literary/formal.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 + に相違ない — 彼が犯人に相違ない (there's no doubt he's the culprit)
grammar.example: この筆跡は彼のものに相違ない。 — This handwriting is undoubtedly his.

grammar.meaning: "When it comes to this extreme example (among several)..." — singles out the most extreme case within a broader negative trend and comments on how bad or striking that specific case is.
grammar.conjugation: 名 + に至っては
grammar.example: デパートの閉店が相次いでいる。Aデパートに至ってはすでに三つの支店が閉店した。 — Department stores are closing one after another. Department Store A, in particular, has already closed three of its branches.

grammar.meaning: ～に至って: only once a situation had progressed as far as X did a certain state finally come about (often implying "too late"). ～に至っても: even though the situation progressed as far as X, a certain state still failed to come about.
grammar.conjugation: 名・動辞書形 + に至って・に至っても
grammar.example: 死者が出るに至って、国は初めて病気の感染拡大の深刻さに気がついたのだ。 — It was only once deaths occurred that the government finally recognized the seriousness of the disease's spread.
grammar.file: grammar-に至って・に至っても.md

grammar.meaning: "Even down to X" / "all the way to X" — emphasizes that the range or scope of something extends even to an unexpected, extreme, or surprising example, underscoring just how broad that range is.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に至るまで
grammar.example: わたしの学校は服装に厳しい。制服の着方はもちろん、ヘアスタイルやスカートの長さに至るまで注意される。 — My school is strict about appearance. Not just how we wear the uniform, but even our hairstyles and skirt length are checked.

grammar.meaning: Indicates that something or someone is sufficiently worthy to merit a particular action or evaluation — "worthy of ~," "enough to ~," "deserving of ~."
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形・名詞する + に足る
grammar.example: 次の首相は国民の代表と言うに足る人物であってほしい。 — I hope the next prime minister will be someone worthy of being called a representative of the people.

grammar.meaning: "Must be / surely is" — expresses the speaker's strong, confident conjecture based on available evidence or reasoning, almost certain though not directly confirmed.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に違いない (例: 犯人は彼に違いない)
grammar.example: あの慌てぶりを見ると、何かあったに違いない。 — Judging by how flustered he is, something must have happened.

grammar.meaning: "Especially in the case of ~ / of all times/people" — expresses irony or frustration that something unfortunate happens precisely in the one situation where it was least expected or wanted.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に限って — 例: こんな日に限って (of all days, on a day like this)
grammar.example: 傘を持っていない日に限って、雨が降る。 — Of all days, it rains on the day I don't have an umbrella.

grammar.meaning: "Not limited to ~ / not only ~ (but also)" — indicates that a statement applies beyond the specific item mentioned, extending to a broader category.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に限らず — 例: 日本に限らず (not only in Japan)
grammar.example: この問題は日本に限らず、世界中で起きている。 — This problem is occurring not only in Japan but around the world.

grammar.meaning: "Without X / omitting X" — indicates that something is done with a particular element left out or excluded, often something normally expected to be present.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + 抜きで (例: 冗談抜きで、朝食抜きで、前置き抜きで)
grammar.example: 今日は冗談抜きで、真剣に話したいことがあります。 — Today, joking aside, there's something I want to talk about seriously.

grammar.meaning: "To do X all the way through / to the very end" — attached to a verb stem, expresses completing a difficult or demanding action thoroughly, persevering until the end despite hardship.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (stem) + 抜く (例: 生き抜く、走り抜く、やり抜く、考え抜く)
grammar.example: 彼は戦争の時代を生き抜いた。 — He survived through the era of war, enduring to the end.

grammar.meaning: "The utmost extreme of X" — a humble, often self-referential expression that a feeling (honor, shame, gratitude) has reached its absolute peak. Frequently appears in fixed ceremonial phrases like 光栄の至り ("the height of honor") and 汗顔の至り ("the height of embarrassment").
grammar.conjugation: N(感情を表す名詞) + の至り
grammar.example: 私の作品が認めていただけるとは、感激の至りです。 — That my work has been recognized is the height of my gratitude/emotion.

grammar.meaning: "Tends to have the (negative) tendency of X" — describes a mild, chronic character flaw or recurring undesirable tendency, usually stated as a gentle criticism.
grammar.conjugation: Nの + きらいがある
grammar.example: 彼女はやや自分勝手で人の意見を無視するきらいがありますね。 — She's a bit selfish and tends to ignore other people's opinions.

grammar.meaning: "The ultimate extreme of X" — describes an emotional or physical state (joy, exhaustion, luxury) as having reached its absolute peak.
grammar.conjugation: N(感情・状態を表す名詞) + の極み
grammar.example: あの有名なスポーツ選手と握手できたなんて、感動の極みだ。 — Getting to shake hands with that famous athlete is the height of excitement.

grammar.meaning: "X and all sorts of excuses/things like that" — lists a dismissive or exasperated series of complaints/excuses, implying there were many such remarks, often with a critical undertone.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 + のなんの + と + 言う／文句を言う etc.
grammar.example: 遅刻したアルバイトの学生はバスが遅れたのなんのと店長に言い訳をした。 (The part-time student who was late made excuses to the manager about the bus being delayed and all sorts of other things.)

grammar.meaning: "Not only X, but also Y" — an additive, emphatic construction stating that something goes beyond the stated scope.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形容詞・な形容詞・名詞 の普通形 (plain form of verbs/i-adjectives/na-adjectives/nouns) + のみならず
grammar.example: 彼は俳優であるのみならず、今や作家としても活躍している。 — He is not only an actor, but now is also active as a writer.

grammar.meaning: "Under X (guidance, supervision, influence, or condition)" — indicates that an action or situation takes place under the influence, authority, guidance, or stated condition of something/someone. のもとで emphasizes the setting/environment of an ongoing action; のもとに often emphasizes the condition or basis under which something is done.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (person/authority/condition) + のもとで／のもとに (例: 先生の指導のもとで、法のもとに、同じ条件のもとで)
grammar.example: 彼は有名な教授の指導のもとで、研究を続けている。 — He continues his research under the guidance of a famous professor.
grammar.file: grammar-のもとで・のもとに.md

grammar.meaning: "It's reasonable/no wonder that X" — expresses understanding and justification for someone's reaction or state, given the circumstances.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 + の + も無理はない
grammar.example: 彼の同じミスは3回目だったので、課長が怒るのも無理はありません。 (Since it was his third time making the same mistake, it's no wonder the section chief got angry.)

grammar.meaning: "After (much deliberation/effort) / at the end of X, finally" — marks the conclusion of a long, often difficult or effortful process, emphasizing that the result came only after considerable time or struggle.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + の末に (例: 長い議論の末に、苦労の末に)
grammar.example: 長い話し合いの末に、両社は合意に達した。 — After lengthy discussions, the two companies reached an agreement.

grammar.meaning: "The height/utmost of X" — a very formal expression used to convey an extreme emotional state (such as honor, embarrassment, or gratitude) at its utmost degree.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞（感情・評価を表す限られた語） + の至りだ
grammar.example: 大統領にお目にかかれて、実に光栄の至りです。 — Being able to meet the President is truly the height of honor.

grammar.meaning: "Needless to say X, (Y also applies)" / "not to mention X" — states that X is so obviously included/true that it doesn't even need mentioning, before adding further information.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + は言うに及ばず
grammar.example: あのレストランは料理の味は言うに及ばず、ケーキの種類も多く、女性に人気がある。 — That restaurant is needless to say delicious, and also has a wide variety of cakes, making it popular with women.
grammar.file: grammar-はいうにおよばず.md

grammar.meaning: "Not to mention X, not even Y" — states that a lesser or more basic case (Y) is also not fulfilled, after dismissing a more obviously expected greater case (X) as not even worth mentioning.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + は疎か + 名詞 + さえ／すら／も + ～ない
grammar.example: 今月は旅行はおろか、外出する余裕さえない。 (This month, forget about traveling — I don't even have the time to go out.)

grammar.meaning: "Setting X aside" / "leaving X for later" — used to table a topic temporarily in order to move on to another, usually more pressing, topic.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + はさておき
grammar.example: 挨拶はさておき、例の件ですが… — Setting greetings aside, regarding that matter...

grammar.meaning: "Due to the sudden impact/momentum of ~ / in the unexpected course of ~" — describes an unwanted or unintended result caused by a sudden physical impact, momentum, or impulsive moment.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 (verb past form) + 弾みで／に
grammar.example: 駅で男の人とぶつかった弾みにかばんを落としてしまった。 — In the sudden impact of bumping into a man at the station, I ended up dropping my bag.

grammar.meaning: "End up in a (rough/unwanted) situation" — describes falling into an undesirable predicament, usually as an unintended consequence of events.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + 羽目になる
grammar.example: 買い物中に財布を盗まれて、深夜に歩いて帰る羽目になってしまった。 (My wallet was stolen while shopping, and I ended up having to walk home late at night.)

grammar.meaning: "Needless to say X," "not to mention X," "of course X (and Y too)" — presents an obvious baseline case and then adds that something further/additional also applies.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + はもちろん(のこと)、〜も
grammar.example: この店はランチはもちろん、ディナーも人気がある。 — Needless to say lunch, this restaurant's dinner is popular too.

grammar.meaning: "Not only X, but also Y" — emphasizes that something goes beyond what is expected, adding a further (often more surprising or extreme) fact on top of the first. Similar to ばかりでなく but slightly more literary/emphatic.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form of verb/adjective) + ばかりか
grammar.example: 彼は料理が上手なばかりか、掃除や洗濯まで完璧にこなす。 — Not only is he good at cooking, he even handles cleaning and laundry perfectly.

grammar.meaning: "All that's left is to ~ / nothing remains but to ~" — indicates that all preparations are complete and only one final step or event remains. Can also mean a situation is continuously progressing in one direction (e.g., worsening).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 (verb dictionary form) + ばかりだ
grammar.example: パーティーの準備は全て整いました。あとは客の到着を待つばかりです。 — All the preparations for the party are complete. All that's left now is to wait for the guests to arrive.

grammar.meaning: "Precisely because X" — an emphatic reason construction stressing that X is the sole, essential reason for Y (often implying that without X, Y would not be true).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞・い形容詞・な形容詞・名詞 の条件形 (conditional/ば-form) + こそ
grammar.example: あなたの将来を心配すればこそ、ご両親は厳しく言うのです。 — It's precisely because they worry about your future that your parents speak so strictly.

grammar.meaning: Says that if a certain thing happens, everything else becomes meaningless or futile, and nothing more can be done about it — "if X happens, that's the end of it" / "once X, it's all over."
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ば形 + それまでだ
grammar.example: 人間、死んでしまえばそれまでだ。生きているうちにやりたいことをやろう。 — Once a person dies, that's the end — let's do what we want to do while we're alive.

grammar.meaning: Formal prohibition: "must not do X." べからず is the terminal (sentence-ending) form commonly seen on notices/signs; べからざる is the attributive form used to modify a following noun ("that must not be done").
grammar.conjugation: V辞書形 + べからず (する → すべからず, irregular)
grammar.example: 関係者以外入るべからず。 — Persons not concerned must not enter.
grammar.file: grammar-べからず・べからざる.md

grammar.meaning: "Should," "ought to" — expresses a moral, normative, or logical obligation: what is the correct/proper thing to do based on common sense, rules, or ethics (not a personal preference).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + べきだ (する → すべきだ／するべきだ, both accepted; すべきだ is the traditional form)
grammar.example: 約束は必ず守るべきだ。 — You should always keep your promises.

grammar.meaning: "In order to" — expresses that an action is performed with a particular goal in mind; a literary way of indicating purpose. Written-language style.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + べく（例外：する → するべく・すべく）
grammar.example: 彼はサッカー選手になるべく、毎日厳しい練習をしている。 — In order to become a soccer player, he trains rigorously every day.

grammar.meaning: "X happened because it was bound/destined to happen" — emphasizes, in hindsight, that an outcome was the natural, inevitable result of what preceded it, not mere chance.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + べくして + 同じ動詞のた形
grammar.example: 我々は勝つべくして勝った。 — We won because victory was the inevitable result.

grammar.meaning: "In order to X" (べく, purpose) / "should/must do X, worthy of X" (べし, classical obligation/recommendation) — a classical auxiliary with two related but distinct uses: べく expresses purpose ("in order to"), while べし (and its modern descendant べきだ) expresses obligation or strong recommendation.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + べく (purpose clause, する→すべく)
grammar.example: 彼は試験に合格すべく、毎日猛勉強している。 (In order to pass the exam, he studies intensely every day.)

grammar.meaning: "It is completely impossible/out of the question to X" — strongly denies the possibility of something, often something hoped for.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + べくもない (する verbs: する→すべくもない or するべくもない)
grammar.example: どんなにがんばっても、これ以上の成績は望むべくもない。 (No matter how hard I try, hoping for better results than this is simply impossible.)

grammar.pattern: ～ほうが（まだ）ましだ／だけ（まだ）ましだ
grammar.meaning: "X would be (relatively) better / at least glad it's not worse" — compares two undesirable options and marks one as the lesser evil, or acknowledges a bad situation could have been worse.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／た形 + ほうが（まだ）ましだ (comparing two options)
grammar.example: こんなに苦しいなら、死んだほうがましです。 (If it's this painful, I'd rather be dead.)

grammar.meaning: "To the extent that," "so much that" — expresses degree by giving a concrete example/comparison that illustrates just how intense a state or action is. Also used in the comparative pattern ～ば～ほど ("the more... the more...").
grammar.conjugation: 動詞普通形／い形容詞／な形容詞 + ほど (degree): 疲れて死ぬほど眠い。(So tired I could die — extremely sleepy.)
grammar.example: 今日は歩けないほど足が疲れた。 — Today my legs got so tired that I could barely walk.
grammar.file: grammar-ほど・ほどの・ほどだ.md

grammar.meaning: "Will surely not," "probably won't" (negative conjecture) or "let's not," "I will not" (negative volitional) — a literary/formal auxiliary expressing strong negative intention or negative supposition, depending on person.
grammar.conjugation: Group 1 (u-verbs) + まい using dictionary form: 行くまい (will probably not go / won't go)
grammar.example: 彼は二度とこの町には戻るまいと誓った。 — He swore he would never return to this town again.

grammar.meaning: Describes behavior "that must not be done, unbecoming of X" — a formal, strongly disapproving judgment that an action is inexcusable given someone's position, role, or the context.
grammar.conjugation: Verb-辞書形 + まじき + Noun (always modifies a following noun, e.g. まじき行為 "unforgivable conduct")
grammar.example: 自殺の方法など、授業で話すまじきことだ。 — Talking about methods of suicide is something that should never be discussed in class.

grammar.meaning: "Also, additionally" — a neutral conjunction listing parallel items or facts.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next.
grammar.example: この公園は広い。また、緑も豊かだ。 — This park is spacious. It's also rich in greenery.

grammar.meaning: "It's simply a matter of doing X / that's all there is to it" — expresses that if a certain circumstance arises, the speaker will simply take a particular (often resolute, minimal, or last-resort) action; it downplays the action as nothing special, just the natural/only thing to do.
grammar.conjugation: Verb-た形 + まで(のこと)だ (describing a past reason/justification: "I only did X because...")
grammar.example: 君にはあまり関係ない事かもしれないが、念のため知らせたまでのことだ。 — This may not concern you much, but I just told you as a precaution — that's all.

grammar.meaning: "To go so far as to ~ / to the extent of doing ~" — expresses that an action is an extreme, often inappropriate or surprising measure, usually framed negatively (implying the speaker finds it excessive or distasteful to go that far).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞て形 (verb te-form) + まで
grammar.example: 客を騙してまで売上成績を伸ばしたいとは思いません。 — I don't want to increase my sales figures to the extent of deceiving customers.

grammar.meaning: (A) Expresses the speaker's resolve that, if there's no other option, they will simply go ahead and do ～ — "if all else fails, I'll just do X." (B) Expresses that an action the speaker took was simply ～ and nothing more, downplaying its significance — "I just did X, that's all, no deeper meaning to it."
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + までだ／までのことだ (meaning A — resolve)
grammar.example: その日に全部作業が終わらなければ、次の日に続きをやるまでだ。 — If I can't finish all the work that day, I'll simply continue it the next day.
grammar.file: grammar-までだ・までのことだ.md

grammar.meaning: Says that something is so minor or obvious that it isn't worth the effort of doing — "there's no need to go so far as to X" / "it's not even necessary to X."
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + までもない
grammar.example: このぐらいの雨なら、傘をさすまでもない。 — With rain this light, there's no need to even bother with an umbrella.

grammar.meaning: "Without even needing to go so far as to X" / "there's no need to even X" — states that performing a given action would be excessive or unnecessary because the matter is already obvious or trivial.
grammar.conjugation: V辞書形 + までもなく
grammar.example: あの映画はわざわざ映画館まで見に行くまでもないよ。 — You don't need to go all the way to the theater to see that movie.

grammar.meaning: As it is / passively following along with something (a circumstance, another person's words, one's own feelings) without exercising one's own initiative.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／た形 + ままに; also 受身形 + るままに (e.g. 言われるままに)
grammar.example: 思うままに、意見を述べてください。(Please state your opinion freely, just as you feel it.)

grammar.meaning: "Covered in/with X" — describes something or someone thoroughly covered by a messy, unpleasant, or negative substance (dirt, blood, sweat, debt), with a strongly negative connotation.
grammar.conjugation: [Noun] + まみれ
grammar.example: 交通事故で全身血まみれの怪我人が病院に運び込まれた。 — An injured person covered in blood from head to toe was brought to the hospital after the traffic accident.

grammar.meaning: "Has a touch of X / looks/feels like X" — a verb-forming suffix attached to nouns to indicate that something takes on the character or appearance of that noun, without fully being it.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + めく → 五段動詞化 (becomes a godan verb; conjugates like 咲く)
grammar.example: 少しずつ春めいてきましたね。 (It's gradually starting to feel like spring, isn't it.)

grammar.meaning: "Both X and Y" — lists two parallel qualities, examples, or facts about the same subject, often to emphasize versatility or balance (can include both positive-positive, negative-negative, or a mix of related points).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞Aも + 動詞/形容詞Aのば形、名詞Bも + 動詞/形容詞B
grammar.example: この店は値段も手頃なら、味もいい。 — This restaurant's prices are reasonable, and the taste is good too.

grammar.meaning: "Not caring about X," "regardless of X," "heedless of X" — describes an action done while deliberately ignoring or disregarding some consideration (appearance, danger, others' feelings, social norms, etc.), often implying recklessness or boldness.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + もかまわず: 人目もかまわず泣いた。(He/she cried, not caring about the eyes of others.)
grammar.example: 彼は周りの目もかまわず、大声で泣き出した。 — Not caring about the eyes around him, he burst out crying loudly.

grammar.meaning: "Not to mention X, Y is also true" / "X is notable, but Y is even more so" — acknowledges that X is impressive/true, but emphasizes that Y deserves equal or greater attention.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + もさることながら
grammar.example: 結婚するには愛情もさることながら、経済力のある人を選ぶべきだ。 — When it comes to marriage, love matters, but you should also choose someone with financial stability.

grammar.meaning: "Without even doing X" — emphasizes that someone failed to do even the most basic/expected action, often carrying a critical or reproachful nuance.
grammar.conjugation: Verb-ます形 (stem) + もしないで
grammar.example: 彼は挨拶もしないで、部屋を出て行った。 — He left the room without even saying hello.

grammar.meaning: "Perfectly suited for / ideal for" — describes something as being exactly right or perfectly fitting for a particular purpose, situation, or person.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + にもってこいだ
grammar.example: 今日は天気もいいし、ハイキングにもってこいの日だ。 — The weather's great today — it's a perfect day for hiking.

grammar.meaning: "There is a certain quality of X," "there's something that..." — expresses the speaker's subjective emotional impression or deep feeling that a certain quality is present, without stating it as a flat objective fact. Often used for nuanced, hard-to-fully-articulate impressions.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + ものがある
grammar.example: 彼女の歌声には聞く人の心を打つものがある。 — There is something in her singing voice that moves the hearts of those who hear it.

grammar.meaning: "Definitely not!" "As if I would!" — a strong rhetorical question expressing emphatic negation/denial, often with defiance, frustration, or stubborn refusal. もんか is the casual contracted form.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + ものか／もんか
grammar.example: 二度とあんな人に頼るものか。 — As if I'd ever rely on someone like that again!

grammar.meaning: "That's just how things are" (general truth/common sense) or "used to do..." (nostalgic habitual past) — expresses either a universal truth/social norm about how things naturally are, or a wistful recollection of a repeated past habit.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + ものだ (general truth): 人は誰でも間違えるものだ。(People are bound to make mistakes — that's just how it is.)
grammar.example: 人間、誰でも年を取れば衰えるものだ。 — Human beings, no matter who, decline as they age — that's just how it is.

grammar.meaning: "Because..." (explaining/excusing a result) — a casual reason-giving structure used to justify or explain one's own behavior or a resulting situation, often with a tone of excuse-making ("it's because of this that... [so please understand/forgive me]").
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 + ものだから
grammar.example: 道が混んでいたものだから、約束の時間に遅れてしまいました。 — Because the roads were congested, I ended up being late for our appointment.

grammar.meaning: "One should not do X," "it's not the kind of thing you should do" — a moral admonition or piece of social advice, stating that an action goes against common sense, decency, or proper conduct.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + ものではない
grammar.example: 年上の人に向かって、そんな口の利き方をするものではない。 — You shouldn't speak to your elders in that kind of tone.

grammar.meaning: "It shall be deemed/stipulated that X" — a formal convention used to establish a rule, regulation, or official stipulation, common in legal and contractual language.
grammar.conjugation: Verb-辞書形 + ものとする
grammar.example: 本規約の変更は、会員への事前通知をもって有効とするものとする。 — Changes to these terms shall be deemed effective upon prior notice to members.

grammar.meaning: "I take it as given/natural that X is the case" — expresses the speaker's confident personal assumption or firm belief, often one that later turns out to be confirmed or overturned.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞／形容詞普通形 + ものと思う
grammar.example: 落としたものと思っていた指輪が出てきた。 — The ring I had assumed was lost turned up.

grammar.meaning: "It is thought/presumed that X" — an impersonal, objective-sounding expression of inference or speculation that distances the statement from the speaker's personal opinion.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞普通形 + ものと思われる
grammar.example: 連休はかなりの渋滞になるものと思われる。 — It is expected that there will be considerable traffic congestion during the holiday period.

grammar.meaning: "Although..., even though..." — a formal concessive conjunction. States a fact, then notes a following fact that contrasts with what would normally be expected from it.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form of verbs/adjectives) + ものの
grammar.example: 試験に合格したものの、思ったほど嬉しくなかった。 — Although I passed the exam, I wasn't as happy as I'd expected.

grammar.meaning: "Although X (would have been better/true)" — expresses regret or mild reproach that a better alternative existed but was not taken, often implying "if only..." or "you should have..." with an undertone of frustration.
grammar.conjugation: [動・い形・な形] の名詞修飾形 + ものを
grammar.example: え？これ、食べたかったの？それなら食べたいと言ってくれればいいものを。 — What? You wanted to eat this? If only you'd just said so.

grammar.meaning: "Because, you know..." — a casual, explanatory/justifying sentence-final particle used to give a reason, often with a slightly whiny, defensive, or childish emotional coloring. もん is the more casual/colloquial variant of もの.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 + もの／もん (女性や子供がよく使う、会話で頻出)
grammar.example: 「どうして食べないの？」「だってお腹がいっぱいなんだもん。」 — "Why aren't you eating?" "Because my stomach's full, you know."

grammar.meaning: "The moment/right after X happens, Y" — describes an action happening immediately after, almost simultaneously with, another action.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + や（否や）
grammar.example: 彼は家に着くや否や、倒れるように眠ってしまった。 (The moment he got home, he collapsed into sleep.)

grammar.meaning: Emphatic negative — "there's no way X" / "X doesn't happen at all" (しやしない, わかりやしない, etc.); strengthens a negation with a dismissive, emphatic tone.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb ます-stem) + やしない — e.g., し + やしない → しやしない; わかり + やしない → わかりやしない
grammar.example: そんなことを言っても、誰も信じやしないよ。 — Even if you say something like that, nobody's going to believe it at all.

grammar.meaning: Two related uses: (1) "～やら～やら" — listing multiple things/feelings in a chaotic, non-exhaustive way ("what with X and Y..."); (2) "〜やら" (single, often with question word) — expresses uncertainty, "I wonder..." similar to か.
grammar.conjugation: Listing: 名詞/動詞普通形 + やら + 名詞/動詞普通形 + やら: 泣くやら笑うやら (crying, laughing, and so on)
grammar.example: 引っ越しの日は荷造りやら掃除やらで一日中忙しかった。 — On moving day, I was busy all day with packing, cleaning, and so on.

grammar.meaning: "Because of X" / "For the reason of X" — a literary, formal way of stating a cause or reason. Written-language style.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞（-の）・普通形（ナ形容詞-な／-である・名詞-である） + ゆえ（に）
grammar.example: 慣れないことゆえ、数々の不手際、どうぞお許しください。 — Please forgive the various mistakes, as this is something I am not used to.

grammar.meaning: "There's no way to do X" / "it's impossible to do X because the means/method to do so don't exist."
grammar.conjugation: V-ます形(stem) + ようがない
grammar.example: こんなに古いと、部品がないので、直しようがありませんね。 — Since it's this old, there are no parts, so there's no way to fix it.

grammar.meaning: "If things continue to be like ~ (an undesirable state), the result will be bad" — points out an undesirable current state or habit and predicts that it will lead to an unfavorable result if it continues.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形（ナ形幹-な／-である・名詞幹-である）＋ ようでは
grammar.example: 小さな失敗をいちいち気にするようでは、この会社ではやっていけないよ。 — If you're going to fuss over every little mistake like this, you won't last at this company.

grammar.meaning: "Like..., as if..." — used to give an example or draw a comparison, illustrating something by likening it to another thing or situation.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + の + ように: 鳥のように (like a bird)
grammar.example: 鳥のように自由に空を飛べたらいいのに。 — I wish I could fly freely through the sky like a bird.

grammar.meaning: "So that..., in order to..." — expresses a purpose or goal, typically used with potential-form verbs or non-volitional verbs (unlike ため which requires volitional verbs).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形/ない形 (dictionary or nai-form, often potential) + ように: 忘れないように書いておく (I'll write it down so I won't forget)
grammar.example: 遅刻しないように、早めに家を出た。 — I left home early so that I wouldn't be late.

grammar.meaning: "If you dare do X, (something bad) will follow" — a bad-result conditional warning that a certain action, even attempted slightly, will trigger a severe or unwanted consequence.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞意向形（よう／おう） + ものなら + (negative/severe consequence clause)
grammar.example: 彼女は気が短くて、デートに少しでも遅刻しようものなら、怒って大変なことになるんだ。 (She's short-tempered, so if you're even a little late to a date, she'll get angry and it becomes a huge problem.)

grammar.meaning: A formal/stiff written equivalent of から, marking the starting point of something — a sender, source, or starting time — commonly seen in letters, citations, and official announcements.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + より
grammar.example: 【手紙】8月18日　山田ゆり子より。 — Letter: August 18th, from Yuriko Yamada.

grammar.meaning: "There's no way that..., it's impossible that..." — expresses strong confidence/conviction that something is logically impossible or extremely unlikely, based on the speaker's reasoning.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form) + わけがない
grammar.example: こんな短時間で全部終わるわけがない。 — There's no way we can finish everything in such a short time.

grammar.meaning: "It's not that... / that doesn't mean that..." — a partial denial or softening expression, used to clarify that a conclusion someone might draw from the preceding context is not entirely accurate, without denying it outright.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞普通形 + わけじゃない
grammar.example: 彼のことが嫌いなわけじゃないけど、一緒に仕事はしたくない。 — It's not that I dislike him, but I don't want to work with him.

grammar.meaning: "That means..., so it's natural that..., no wonder..." — draws a logical conclusion from previously stated information; indicates that a situation is the natural/expected result of given facts.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form) + わけだ
grammar.example: 3年間アメリカに住んでいたのか。道理で英語が上手なわけだ。 — You lived in America for three years? No wonder your English is so good.

grammar.meaning: "It's not that..., it doesn't mean that..." — a partial negation, denying a full/absolute interpretation of a previous statement without completely rejecting it. Often used to soften or qualify a generalization.
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form) + わけではない
grammar.example: 野菜が嫌いなわけではないが、あまり食べたくない時もある。 — It's not that I dislike vegetables, but sometimes I just don't feel like eating them.

grammar.meaning: "There's no way that... / it can't possibly be that..." — a casual, spoken contraction of わけがない (see **わけ（が）ない**) that strongly denies a possibility. Note: despite the surface components ("わけ" = reason/circumstance + "ない" = isn't), this is NOT a statement that something is "easy" or "no big deal" — it is an emphatic denial, just like its more formal counterpart わけがない, with the が simply dropped in casual speech.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞普通形 (plain-form verb) + わけない
grammar.example: そんな難しい問題、一日で解けるわけない。 — There's no way you can solve such a difficult problem in a single day.

grammar.meaning: "Cannot (afford to)..., can't just..." — expresses that an action is impossible due to social, moral, or situational obligations/common sense, even if one wanted to do it.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 + わけにはいかない: 休むわけにはいかない (I can't just take a day off)
grammar.example: 大事な会議があるので、今日は休むわけにはいかない。 — There's an important meeting today, so I can't just take the day off.

grammar.meaning: "Considering..., for (what one would expect)..., relatively..." — indicates that a result doesn't quite match what would normally be expected given a stated condition (either surprisingly better or worse than expected).
grammar.conjugation: 普通形 (plain form) + わりに(は)
grammar.example: このレストランは値段が高いわりに、味はそれほどでもない。 — This restaurant is expensive, but the taste isn't all that great for the price.

grammar.meaning: "So much X and Y (one after another)!" — repeats the sentence-final particle わ after two (often the same) verbs to express surprise or exasperation at an overwhelming, excessive degree of something happening.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形／た形 + わ + （同じ動詞 or 関連動詞）+ わ
grammar.example: 彼女をすし屋に連れて行ったら、食うわ食うわ、金がなくなっちゃったよ。 (I took her to a sushi restaurant, and she ate and ate so much that I ran out of money.)

grammar.meaning: "Treating X as Y, with X as/in the capacity of Y" — assigns a role, status, or category to something/someone; frequently used to state a designated function or position.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞A + を + 名詞B + として: 彼を代表として選んだ (chose him as the representative)
grammar.example: 会議では彼を議長として選出した。 — At the meeting, they elected him as the chairperson.

grammar.meaning: "Taking advantage of X (a convenient circumstance) to do something bad/selfish" — criticizes someone for exploiting a favorable situation, such as someone's absence or weakness, in order to misbehave.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞／動詞普通形 + の + をいいことに
grammar.example: 先生がいないのをいいことにサボっている。 — They're slacking off, taking advantage of the teacher's absence.

grammar.meaning: "Other than X, there's nothing/no one comparable" — used to emphatically single out something or someone as uniquely the best or most suitable, with no real alternative in the same league.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + をおいて
grammar.example: 今、こんな素晴らしい色使いの染色ができる人は、彼をおいてほかにいない。 — There's no one else, besides him, who can dye fabric with such wonderful use of color today.

grammar.meaning: "There's no one/nothing but X" — strongly asserts that X is the only suitable choice, with nothing else even in the running.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + をおいて + (ほかに) + ～ない (noun + をおいて + negative predicate, often with ほかに inserted for emphasis)
grammar.example: 彼をおいて、この難事件を解決できる探偵はいない。 (There's no detective but him who can solve this difficult case.)

grammar.meaning: "Doing X despite circumstances that would normally prevent it" — describes pushing forward with an action in spite of a hindering condition (illness, bad weather, objections).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を押して
grammar.example: キャプテンは高熱を押してサッカーの決勝戦に出場した。 (The captain played in the soccer finals despite having a high fever.)

grammar.meaning: "As of X" — marks a specific point (often "today" or a stated event) as the cutoff or final occurrence of something, typically signaling the end of a habit, relationship, or practice.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun, often a time expression) + をかぎりに
grammar.example: 今日を限りにあなたとは口をききません。 — As of today, I will not speak to you anymore.

grammar.meaning: "Combining X with (another purpose)" — describes an action or thing that serves two purposes simultaneously.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を兼ねて
grammar.example: 雑誌の取材を兼ねて一ヶ月ほどヨーロッパを旅行した。 (Combining it with magazine reporting work, I traveled around Europe for about a month.)

grammar.meaning: "Starting with X (and continuing on from there)" — marks the first in a series of events, especially one that kicks off an expanding sequence (e.g., a tour, campaign, or series of occurrences).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を皮切りに（して）
grammar.example: 彼のツアーは東京公演を皮切りに、全国十都市を回る予定だ。 (His tour, starting with the Tokyo performance, is set to travel to ten cities nationwide.)

grammar.pattern: ～をきっかけに（として）／を契機に（として）
grammar.meaning: "Taking X as a chance/trigger/opportunity" — marks an event as the catalyst that led to a subsequent change or action. をきっかけに is the more common/colloquial form; を契機に is a more formal, written synonym with the same meaning.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + をきっかけに(して/として): 留学をきっかけに英語が得意になった (studying abroad became the trigger for me getting good at English)
grammar.example: 友人に誘われたことをきっかけに、ヨガを始めた。 — Being invited by a friend was the trigger for me starting yoga.
grammar.file: grammar-をきっかけに(として)・を契機に(として).md

grammar.meaning: "Putting (feeling/effort) into, with (heart/soul) put into" — expresses that something is done with concentrated emotion, effort, or sincerity poured into it.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (feeling/effort word) + を込めて: 心を込めて (putting one's heart into it), 愛を込めて (with love), 感謝を込めて (with gratitude)
grammar.example: 彼女は心を込めて手作りのクッキーを焼いた。 — She baked handmade cookies with her whole heart put into it.

grammar.meaning: "Neglecting X" — expresses that someone is leaving X unattended or treating it carelessly, usually while focusing on something else instead.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + をなおざりにして
grammar.example: 息子は勉強を等閑にして、パソコンゲームに夢中になっている。 — My son is neglecting his studies, absorbed in computer games instead.

grammar.meaning: "Without X, leaving X aside" — indicates that something is excluded or set aside, often implying that proceeding without it would be unusual, impossible, or incomplete.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を抜きにして: 冗談を抜きにして (joking aside); 彼の協力を抜きにしては (without his cooperation...)
grammar.example: 冗談を抜きにして、真剣に話し合いましょう。 — Joking aside, let's talk about this seriously.

grammar.meaning: "Starting with X, such as X (and others)" — introduces a representative example of a larger group or category, implying there are other similar members not explicitly listed.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + をはじめ(として/とする): 校長先生をはじめ、多くの先生方が出席した (starting with the principal, many teachers attended)
grammar.example: この祭りには市長をはじめ、多くの来賓が参加した。 — Many dignitaries, starting with the mayor, attended this festival.

grammar.meaning: "With X coming up / facing X (in time or place)" — describes being in a state of anticipation or preparation because an event is imminent, or being positioned near something.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を控えて
grammar.example: 試験を一週間後に控えて毎日勉強に追われている。 (With the exam coming up in a week, I'm swamped with studying every day.)

grammar.meaning: "Based on/considering X" — describes taking a fact, prior experience, or piece of information into account before proceeding with a judgment, plan, or statement.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を踏まえて
grammar.example: 去年の反省を踏まえて今年の計画を立てましょう。 (Let's make this year's plan based on last year's reflections.)

grammar.meaning: "Through/via X (a process, place, or stage)" — describes passing through a stage, location, or experience as part of reaching an eventual outcome.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を経て
grammar.example: 彼は様々な困難を経て成功を手に入れた。 (He achieved success after going through various hardships.)

grammar.meaning: "Surrounding, over (the issue of), concerning (a dispute/debate)" — indicates that a topic is the subject of debate, conflict, or differing opinions among multiple parties.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + をめぐって: この問題をめぐって (over/concerning this issue)
grammar.example: この土地の所有権をめぐって、長年裁判が続いている。 — A lawsuit over the ownership of this land has continued for many years.

grammar.meaning: Two related senses: (1) "by means of X" / "using X" (instrument/means, especially emphatic when intensified as ～をもってすれば, "if one were to use X"); (2) "as of X" / "ending at X" (marking a formal cutoff point or deadline). These are distinct nuances that should not be conflated.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + をもって
grammar.example: 審査の結果は書面をもってお知らせします。 — The results of the review will be announced by means of a written document.

grammar.meaning: "Based on, using as a basis" — indicates that something (information, data, experience) serves as the foundation or source material for creating, deciding, or judging something else.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + をもとに(して): 実話をもとにして映画を作った (made a movie based on a true story)
grammar.example: この映画は実際にあった事件をもとにして作られた。 — This movie was made based on an actual incident.

grammar.meaning: "Undaunted by ~" / "Without being discouraged by ~" — describes someone pushing forward energetically despite an obstacle or hardship that would normally make a person give up or feel defeated.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 ＋ をものともせず(に)
grammar.example: 彼は体の障害をものともせずに、精力的に活動している。 — Undaunted by his physical disability, he is energetically active.

grammar.pattern: ～をものともせず(に)／しないで
grammar.meaning: "Undaunted by X / not letting X be a hindrance" — describes bravely pushing forward despite a significant obstacle, hardship, or danger, often with an admiring tone.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を物ともせず（に）
grammar.example: 彼女は周囲の批判をものともせず、自分の夢を追い続けた。 (Undaunted by criticism from those around her, she kept pursuing her dream.)

grammar.meaning: "Ignoring X / without concern for X" — describes proceeding with an action while disregarding a relevant concern, warning, or others' feelings/expectations.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + をよそに
grammar.example: 周囲の反対をよそに、彼は海外移住を決めた。 (Ignoring the opposition from those around him, he decided to emigrate abroad.)

grammar.meaning: "Centering on, focused around" — indicates that something is the central focus, hub, or main point around which other things are organized or revolve.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を中心に(して/として): 東京を中心に活動している (active centering around Tokyo)
grammar.example: この台風は関東地方を中心に大きな被害をもたらした。 — This typhoon caused major damage, centering on the Kanto region.

grammar.pattern: ～を余儀なくされる／～を余儀なくさせる
grammar.meaning: を余儀なくされる = "be forced to do X" (the subject has no choice, due to circumstances beyond their control, but to accept an undesired situation). を余儀なくさせる = the causative counterpart, "(something/someone) forces X to happen" — the subject is the cause compelling the change, not the one affected.
grammar.conjugation: N + を余儀なくされる (passive — subject is forced into the situation)
grammar.example: 台風の影響で電車が止まってしまい、旅行の中止を余儀なくされた。 — Because of the typhoon, the trains stopped, forcing us to cancel our trip.
grammar.file: grammar-を余儀なくされる・させる.md

grammar.meaning: "On the premise/assumption of X" — states that a subsequent plan, action, or proposal is based on X as its foundational condition or assumption.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + を前提に
grammar.example: 「弘美さん、結婚を前提に僕と付き合ってください！」「それはちょっと…」 — "Hiromi, please date me with marriage as the premise!" "Well, that's a bit..."

grammar.meaning: "Regardless of, irrespective of" — indicates that a stated distinction or category (age, gender, experience, weather, etc.) makes no difference to what follows.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を問わず: 年齢を問わず (regardless of age), 経験の有無を問わず (regardless of whether one has experience or not)
grammar.example: 本イベントは年齢を問わず、どなたでも参加できます。 — This event is open to anyone, regardless of age.

grammar.meaning: "With X as the turning point/boundary" — marks a specific event or point in time as the dividing line between a before-state and an after-state, often indicating a notable change.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + をさかいに
grammar.example: あの日の喧嘩をさかいに、彼女とは絶交状態になってしまった。 — With the fight that day as the turning point, I ended up completely estranged from her.

grammar.meaning: "With X coming up soon" — describes a person or situation being in a particular state (often tense or busy) in anticipation of a significant event that is approaching.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を控えて／を控えた＋名詞
grammar.example: 入試をひかえて、学生たちはぴりぴりしている。 — With entrance exams coming up, the students are on edge.

grammar.meaning: "Taking X as an opportunity/trigger" — marks an event as the turning point or catalyst that prompted a subsequent decision or change, often a significant life event.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + を機に
grammar.example: 二人目の出産を機に、退職することにしました。 — Taking the birth of my second child as an opportunity, I decided to retire.

grammar.pattern: ～を皮切りに（して）・～を皮切りとして
grammar.meaning: "Starting with X, one thing after another follows" — describes X as the opening event of a planned, connected series, after which similar events occur one after another and develop further.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を皮切りに（して）／を皮切りとして
grammar.example: この作家は自分の父親のことを書いた小説を皮切りに、次々に話題作を発表している。 — Starting with the novel he wrote about his own father, this author has gone on to publish one noteworthy work after another.
grammar.file: grammar-を皮切りに（して）・を皮切りとして.md

grammar.meaning: "Cannot help but feel X" — a strong emotion (sympathy, anger, tears, surprise) wells up involuntarily and cannot be suppressed, usually in reaction to something moving or tragic.
grammar.conjugation: N(感情を表す名詞) + を禁じ得ない
grammar.example: 大地震で両親を失ってしまった子どもが多い。同情を禁じえない話である。 — Many children lost their parents in the big earthquake. It's a story that makes you unable to help feeling sympathy.

grammar.meaning: Facing a certain situation, one cannot suppress an emotion welling up inside — "cannot help but feel ~." Formal, written register.
grammar.conjugation: 名 + を禁じ得ない
grammar.example: 生々しい戦争の傷跡を目の当たりにし、涙を禁じ得なかった。 — Witnessing the raw scars of war firsthand, I couldn't hold back my tears.

grammar.meaning: "Having gone through / passed through X" — describes reaching a current state or result only after passing through a certain process, stage, or period of time.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を経て／を経た＋名詞
grammar.example: 3年の交際を経て、二人は結婚した。 — After three years of dating, the two got married.

grammar.meaning: "Based on / taking X into account" — to do something while treating X (prior information, opinions, results, or experience) as a premise to build on.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を踏まえて／を踏まえた＋名詞
grammar.example: 前回の反省点を踏まえて、次の企画案を練ろう。 — Let's work out the next proposal, taking into account the points we reflected on last time.

grammar.meaning: "Through, by means of (over a period or via a medium)" — indicates a channel, medium, or duration through which something happens or is accomplished. を通じて also carries a secondary meaning of "throughout (a period of time)."
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を通して/を通じて: 友人を通して紹介された (introduced through a friend); 一年を通じて (throughout the year)
grammar.example: 彼とは共通の友人を通して知り合った。 — I got to know him through a mutual friend.
grammar.file: grammar-を通して・を通じて.md

grammar.meaning: "As of X, ... will stop" — a formal declaration that, from the point in time marked by X onward, something that had been continuing will be brought to an end.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + を限りに
grammar.example: 本年度を限りにこの講座の受講生募集を行わないことになりました。 — We have decided that, as of this academic year, we will no longer be recruiting students for this course.

grammar.meaning: "Relying on ~ / depending on the help of ~" — describes using something or someone (memory, a map, a person's help) as one's main support or guide in accomplishing something, often in an uncertain or difficult situation.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 (noun) + を頼りに
grammar.example: 昔の記憶を頼りに、学生時代によく通ったラーメン屋を探した。 — Relying on my old memories, I searched for the ramen shop I used to frequent as a student.

grammar.meaning: "For the purpose of X" — expresses carrying out an action with a strong, deliberate goal in mind. Written-language style, more intense and archaic than ために.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ない形 + んがため（に）（例外：する → せん）
grammar.example: 彼女は歌手になりたいという夢を実現させんがため、上京した。 — She moved to Tokyo in order to make her dream of becoming a singer come true.

grammar.meaning: "In order to X" — a literary expression of strong purpose or intent, derived from the archaic auxiliary ～んとする ("to be about to do X / intend to do X"); conveys a determined, often desperate or resolute effort to achieve a goal.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ない形 (verb ない-form, dropping ない and attaching ん) + がため(に) — e.g., 結婚せんがために (in order to marry); irregular verb する becomes せん (not しん)
grammar.example: 彼女は彼と結婚せんがために、自分の過去を偽っていた。 — In order to marry him, she had been hiding her past.

grammar.meaning: "As if about to do X" / "almost to the point of doing X" — describes an action or state so intense it looks like it's just on the verge of happening, though it doesn't quite occur.
grammar.conjugation: V-ない形(remove ない) + んばかり(に/の) (e.g., 今にも泣かんばかりに, "as if about to cry at any moment")
grammar.example: 台風で木の枝が今にも折れんばかりだ。 — The tree branch looks like it's about to snap at any moment because of the typhoon.

grammar.meaning: "As if about to ~" / "Looking as though it would ~ at any moment" — describes a state or action that is so extreme it looks almost like something else is about to happen, even though it doesn't actually reach that point.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ない形 ＋ んばかりだ （例外：する→せんばかりだ）
grammar.example: 彼は力強くうなずいた。任せろと言わんばかりだった。 — He nodded firmly, as if to say "leave it to me."

grammar.meaning: "On the other hand, meanwhile" — a conjunction contrasting two parallel facts or perspectives, more neutral and structural than emotional.
grammar.conjugation: Sentence-initial conjunction, no conjugation needed — attaches at the sentence boundary, connecting the previous sentence to the next. Can also attach directly after a plain-form verb/clause mid-sentence as 〜一方(で) to contrast two aspects of the same topic within one sentence (e.g. 便利である一方、危険も伴う).
grammar.example: 都市部では人口が増えている。一方、地方では過疎化が進んでいる。 — In urban areas, the population is increasing. On the other hand, depopulation is progressing in rural areas.

grammar.meaning: "From the standpoint of X / in terms of X" — attaches to a noun to indicate the perspective, field, or domain from which a statement is being made (e.g., legally, technically, historically).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + 上（で／の／は）
grammar.example: 法律上は問題ないが、倫理的には議論の余地がある。 — Legally there's no problem, but ethically there's room for debate.

grammar.meaning: "On the other hand," "while at the same time" — describes two contrasting aspects or qualities that coexist within the same subject/situation (unlike a simple contrast between two different things).
grammar.conjugation: 動詞普通形 + 反面
grammar.example: この薬はよく効く反面、副作用も強い。 — This medicine is very effective, while at the same time it has strong side effects.

grammar.meaning: "Suited for X," "geared toward X" — indicates that something is inherently well-matched or appropriate in nature/characteristics for a certain group or purpose (describes an objective fit, not a deliberate design choice).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + 向き: 初心者向きの本 (a book suited for beginners)
grammar.example: この部屋は南向きで、日当たりがいい。 — This room faces south and gets good sunlight.

grammar.meaning: "Targeted at X," "intended for X (audience/market)" — indicates that something was deliberately designed, produced, or aimed at a specific group.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + 向け(の) + 名詞: 子供向けの番組 (a program intended for children)
grammar.example: この製品は海外向けに開発された。 — This product was developed targeted at overseas markets.

grammar.meaning: Describes how, after a bad situation continued for a while, things finally ended up in such-and-such an unfortunate conclusion.
grammar.conjugation: 動辞書形 + 始末だ
grammar.example: おいは遊んでばかりいてまじめに働きもせず、とうとう会社を辞めてしまう始末だ。 — My nephew did nothing but play around and never worked seriously, and in the end he quit his job altogether.

grammar.meaning: Attached to a verb's masu-stem, expresses logical/abstract possibility "can happen / can do" (得る) or impossibility "cannot happen / cannot do" (得ない). Used for conceptual or logical possibility rather than physical skill-based ability.
grammar.conjugation: Verb ます形 (stem, drop ます) + 得る／得ない
grammar.example: そのようなミスは誰にでもあり得る。 — Such a mistake could happen to anyone.

grammar.meaning: "There is a fear/risk/danger that ~" — used to express concern that a negative or undesirable event may occur, typically in formal announcements, news reports, and weather warnings.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形 (verb dictionary form) + 恐れがある — 例: 崩れる恐れがある (there is a risk of collapsing)
grammar.example: 今夜、大雨で川が氾濫する恐れがあります。 — Tonight, there is a risk that the river will flood due to heavy rain.

grammar.meaning: "Given that X (would see/judge me)" — because the speaker is conscious of a certain standpoint, person, or prior statement, they feel they must act accordingly, or else lose face or be evaluated poorly.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞-の／動詞辞書形・た形・ている形 + 手前
grammar.example: 5月末までに問題を解決すると約束した手前、どうしても頑張らなければならない。 — Having promised to resolve the problem by the end of May, I absolutely have to work hard at it now.

grammar.meaning: "On the occasion of X" — marks a particular time, occasion, or opportunity, often used for polite, somewhat formal references to a chance meeting or event.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞た形 (verb た-form) + 折に
grammar.example: また何かの折にでも、お会いしたいですね。 — I'd love to meet again sometime, whenever the occasion arises.

grammar.meaning: "As much as one wants, unrestrained" — attaches to a verb stem to indicate an action done without limit or restriction (e.g., 食べ放題, "all-you-can-eat"; 飲み放題, "all-you-can-drink").
grammar.conjugation: 動詞ます形 (verb ます-stem, stem only) + 放題
grammar.example: このレストランは2000円で食べ放題だ。 — At this restaurant, you can eat all you want for 2000 yen.

grammar.meaning: "Right in the middle of (doing) X" — emphasizes that an action/event is at its peak or most intense ongoing point, often used to show that something else (often unexpected/interrupting) happens during that point.
grammar.conjugation: Verb (ている form, dropping いる) + 最中に
grammar.example: 会議の最中に、突然電話が鳴った。 — Right in the middle of the meeting, the phone suddenly rang.

grammar.meaning: Describes a state or quality as being at its absolute extreme — "extremely ~," "~ in the extreme." Formal, written register.
grammar.conjugation: ナ形 + 極まる
grammar.example: このような不当な判決が出たことは、残念極まる。 — That such an unjust ruling was handed down is extremely regrettable.

grammar.meaning: "As soon as X (then immediately Y)" — attached to a verb stem, indicates that the following action will be carried out immediately upon completion/occurrence of the first.
grammar.conjugation: Verb (ます stem) + 次第
grammar.example: 結果が分かり次第、お知らせいたします。 — As soon as the results are known, I will let you know.

grammar.meaning: "That's how it turned out / it depends on X" — ～次第だ explains the circumstances or reasoning behind a situation (often at the end of an explanation); ～次第で(は) means "depending on X," indicating that the outcome varies based on a certain factor.
grammar.conjugation: [explanation of events in plain form] + というわけで、～次第です
grammar.example: 今回の出張は、急な取引先の都合で延期になった次第です。 — This business trip was postponed due to the client's sudden circumstances — that's the situation.

grammar.meaning: "A bit, slight tendency toward (usually negative)" — indicates a mild degree or leaning toward an undesirable state, symptom, or trend.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + 気味
grammar.example: 最近風邪気味なので、早く寝ます。 — I've had a bit of a cold feeling lately, so I'll go to bed early.

grammar.meaning: "Just as one was about to ~ / right at the moment of ~" — describes something (often unexpected or unwelcome) happening right at the moment someone was about to do something or right after an event occurred.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞意向形+とした (volitional form + とした) + 矢先に
grammar.example: 出かけようとした矢先に、雨が降り出した。 — Just as I was about to go out, it started raining.

grammar.meaning: "As long as ~ (the condition holds) / so long as" — expresses that as long as a certain state or condition continues, the related result/action also holds true.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形/ている形 + 限り(は) — 例: 生きている限り (as long as I'm alive)
grammar.example: 命がある限り、諦めません。 — As long as I'm alive, I won't give up.

grammar.meaning: "As far as ~ (within the limits of my knowledge/experience/information)" — used to hedge a statement by limiting it to what the speaker personally knows, has seen, or has heard.
grammar.conjugation: 動詞辞書形/た形 + 限りでは — 例: 私が知っている限りでは (as far as I know)
grammar.example: 私が調べた限りでは、このレストランが一番評判がいい。 — As far as I've researched, this restaurant has the best reputation.

grammar.meaning: - **限り** — "as long as / to the extent that" (sets a boundary/condition — covered in depth separately for its ～限り(は) conditional usage).
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + に限り — 例: 本日に限り (limited to today only)
grammar.example: 本日に限り、全商品を20%引きにします。 — Only today, all items are 20% off.
grammar.file: grammar-限り・に限り・に限る.md

grammar.meaning: "On the occasion of X / when X (formal)" — marks a formal, often significant or official occasion/moment as the time frame for the main action, such as ceremonies, procedures, or important transitions.
grammar.conjugation: 名詞 + の際に／に際して
grammar.example: ご契約の際には、身分証明書が必要です。 — When signing the contract, identification is required.
